Abbadessa et al 2024 Neurol Neuroimmunol.body: Prospective noninterventional study of 41 patients with relapsing MS sampled before and 6 and 12 months after starting ocrelizumab (anti-CD20). Beyond depleting CD19+ B cells, ocrelizumab reduced activation, migratory, and cytotoxic markers on CD8+ T and NK cells and impaired CD8+ T-cell and NK-cell cytotoxic function. Critically, ocrelizumab selectively and significantly reduced CD8+ T-cell proliferation in response to EBV peptides while leaving CMV, SARS-CoV-2, and CEFX responses unchanged, suggesting B-cell depletion disrupts the source of EBV antigens that drive EBV-specific CD8+ T-cell expansion in MS.

Afrasiabi et al 2019 Genome Med.body: Genome-wide association study analysis integrating RNAseq of EBV-infected B cells (lymphoblastoid cell lines, LCLs) at Latency III, eQTL data, and EBV transcription factor binding to test whether MS risk loci reflect impaired control of EBV infection. The authors identify MS risk SNP:gene pairs whose expression is associated with the risk genotype in LCLs (LCLeQTLs), show these are over-represented in genes dysregulated by EBV infection and at EBNA2 binding sites, and demonstrate that CD40L signalling reduces LCL proliferation more strongly for protective CD40 and TRAF3 genotypes. They conclude reduced control of EBV is implicated in MS susceptibility and that targeting EBV may be of therapeutic benefit.

Afrasiabi et al 2020 Sci Rep.body: In-silico QTL study integrating MS risk SNPs, host and EBV gene/miRNA expression, EBV DNA copy number and intrinsic growth rate across >400 lymphoblastoid cell lines (LCLs) to test whether MS genetic risk loci interact with EBV phenotypes. MS (and SLE) risk genes were significantly over-represented among host genes whose expression correlates with EBV DNA copy number, more than for non-EBV diseases, implicating EBV in MS pathogenesis. The PVR risk SNP rs7260482 was associated with higher PVR expression, lower expression of EBV miRNAs BART3-5p and BART4-3p, and EBV DNA copy number, nominating PVR and these miRNAs as therapeutic targets.

Afrasiabi et al 2021 Int J Mol Sci.body: An in silico and in vitro study integrating MS GWAS risk loci with EBV-encoded and host cellular miRNA data in EBV-transformed B cells (lymphoblastoid cell lines, LCLs) versus uninfected B cells. The authors show EBV infection dysregulates the host B-cell miRNA machinery, including MS risk miRNAs (e.g., let-7b-5p and let-7e-5p downregulated, miR-21 upregulated in LCLs), and that EBV miRNAs and the EBV transcription factor EBNA2 target several MS risk genes. The MS risk SNP rs4808760 risk allele increases hsa-mir-3188-3p expression (LD block bound by EBNA2), and the MS risk SNP rs10271373 risk allele reduces ZC3HAV1 expression in LCLs but not B cells, consistent with let-7b-5p regulation of ZC3HAV1 and altered interferon response / EBV immune evasion.

Agostini et al 2018 J Transl Med.body: Case-control study of 117 EBV-seropositive multiple sclerosis (MS) patients and 89 age/sex-matched healthy controls evaluating how HLA-class I/II alleles modulate EBV blood viral load and anti-EBV antibody titers. MS patients had more frequently detectable EBV DNA, higher overall EBV viral load, and higher anti-EBNA-1 and anti-VCA IgG titers than controls. In MS (but not controls), the MS risk alleles HLA-B*07 and HLA-DRB1*15 were associated with higher EBV viral load and the protective HLA-A*02 with lower viral load; multiple regression identified HLA-B*07 as the allele most strongly associated with high EBV viral load (p=0.0001), supporting a model of suboptimal HLA-B*07-restricted CD8+ T-cell control of EBV in MS.

Agostini et al 2024 Front Neurosci.body: Case-control study of 57 EBV-seropositive multiple sclerosis patients (31 RRMS, 26 PMS) and 49 age/sex-matched healthy controls measuring EBV viral load, EBNA-1/VCA antibody titers, and LMP2A and EBNA-1 mRNA expression in blood. LMP2A mRNA was significantly more frequently detected (89% vs 61%) and more highly expressed in MS patients than controls (p<0.005), and EBNA-1 and VCA antibody titers were higher in MS (p=0.03 each), whereas EBNA-1 mRNA did not differ from controls but was more frequent in progressive than relapsing-remitting MS (p<0.05). The authors conclude that overexpression of the EBV latency gene LMP2A supports a role for EBV in MS etiopathology.

Alari‐Pahissa et al 2018 Eur J Neurol.body: A cross-sectional multicenter case-control study of 310 patients with multiple sclerosis (early MS, n=127; non-early MS, n=183) and 155 controls in Spain, evaluating humoral responses to CMV, EBV and HHV-6 plus T-cell and NK-cell immunophenotypes. CMV seroprevalence was significantly lower in early MS (48%) than in non-early MS (65%) or controls (63.8%) and was independently associated with disease duration (OR 1.04). CMV+ patients showed increased terminally differentiated T-cells (CD27-CD28-, CD57+, LILRB1+) and NKG2C+ NK-cells, the latter associated with lower disability in early MS, and CMV+ early MS patients showed an inverse correlation between anti-EBNA-1 antibodies and MS duration (R=-0.59), supporting a putative protective role of CMV in early MS consistent with the hygiene hypothesis.

Ali et al 2024 Mult Scler Relat Disord.body: Open retrospective case-control study measuring Epstein-Barr nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA1) IgG in paired serum and CSF of relapsing-remitting MS patients (n=61), optic neuritis patients (n=26) and healthy controls (n=15) by ELISA, and deriving EBNA1-based antibody indices. EBNA1 IgG levels in both serum and CSF were significantly elevated in RRMS and ON patients versus controls. CSF EBNA1 IgG alone (AUC 0.943, sensitivity 94%) and indices combining CSF EBNA1 IgG with CSF albumin or serum EBNA1 IgG with total serum IgG gave the highest discrimination, complementing the IgG index and oligoclonal bands. EBNA1 IgG and EBV-based indices correlated with T2 lesions, gadolinium-enhancing lesions and CSF leukocytes, and the authors propose an albumin-based EBNA1 antibody index (Qspec/Qalb) to aid earlier MS diagnosis.
Ali et al 2024 Mult Scler Relat Disord.identifier: Ali et al 2024 Mult Scler Relat Disord

Allanach et al 2025 Sci Adv.body: Allanach et al. developed a humanized PBMC (HuPBMC) experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) mouse model by engrafting NSG mice with PBMCs from EBV-seronegative healthy donors, EBV-seropositive healthy donors, or EBV-seropositive relapsing-remitting MS (RRMS) donors, then inducing EAE with MOG antigen. Donor EBV seropositivity and RRMS diagnosis both worsened clinical disease severity, increased CNS-infiltrating effector hCD4+ Th1 and cytotoxic hCD8+ T cells, shifted CD8 cytotoxicity toward granzyme B, and limited FOXP3+ regulatory T cell expansion, raising effector:Treg ratios. EBV-experienced donor T cells were more proliferative after TCR (CD3/CD28) stimulation. Effects occurred without detectable EBV reactivation, indicating latent EBV history dysregulates T cell responses to promote MS-like autoimmunity.

Alotaibi et al 2004 JAMA.body: Case-control study (Alotaibi et al, JAMA 2004) of 30 pediatric multiple sclerosis (MS) patients, 90 age-matched emergency department controls, and 53 bone marrow transplant donor controls, testing archived serum for IgG antibodies to EBV (VCA, EBNA, EA), CMV, parvovirus B19, HSV, and VZV. Serological evidence of remote EBV infection was markedly more common in pediatric MS (83%) than in either control group (42%; OR 7.04 vs BMT and OR 8.7 vs ED, P<.001), and MS patients were less often EBV-seronegative. MS patients were also less likely to be HSV-seropositive (52% vs 88%; OR 0.14, P=.003), while seropositivity for CMV, parvovirus B19, and VZV did not differ. The authors conclude EBV infection is associated with pediatric MS.

Alvarez-Lafuente et al 2008 Mult Scler.body: Case-control study quantifying DNA prevalences and viral loads of HSV, EBV, VZV, CMV, HHV-6, HERV-H and HERV-W by quantitative real-time PCR in cerebrospinal fluid from 48 MS patients at first demyelinating event versus 44 controls (23 OIND and 21 ONIND). EBV DNA was found in only 1/48 (2.1%) MS patients and no controls, while HHV-6 (all variant A) was detected in 5/48 (10.4%) MS patients and no controls. Overall HHV prevalence was significantly higher in MS (14.6%) than controls (2.3%, p=0.038), but only HHV-6 reached individual significance; HERV-H and HERV-W were not detected in any sample. The authors conclude only HHV-6A appears involved in MS pathogenesis in a subset of patients, and CSF viral detection is sensitive to long-term storage conditions.

Angelini et al 2013 PLoS Pathog.body: Angelini et al. used HLA class I peptide pentamers to quantify EBV-specific CD8+ T cell responses to latent (EBNA-3A, LMP-2A) and lytic (BZLF-1, BMLF-1) antigens in 113 relapsing-remitting MS patients (79 untreated, 20 IFN-beta-, 14 natalizumab-treated) and 43 healthy donors, correlating responses with disease activity by MRI and clinical evaluation. CD8+ T cells specific for EBV lytic antigens were more frequent in active MS, whereas EBNA-3A (latent)-specific CD8+ T cells were higher in inactive MS, with no difference in CMV responses; longitudinal monitoring showed BZLF-1/BMLF-1-specific T cell peaks during active disease. In post-mortem MS brain, the EBV lytic protein BZLF-1 (and BFRF1) was expressed in plasma cells within active white matter lesions and inflamed meninges, where cytotoxic CD8+/granzyme B+ T cells contacted EBV lytically infected cells, supporting a model in which intracerebral EBV reactivation drives an immunopathological response during MS relapses.

Ascherio et al 2001 JAMA.body: Prospective nested case-control study within the Nurses' Health Study and Nurses' Health Study II (62,439 women) testing whether serum IgG antibody titers to EBV antigens (VCA, EBNA, EBNA-1, EBNA-2, EA-D, EA-R) and to CMV precede onset of multiple sclerosis. Among 18 MS cases with blood drawn before disease onset, geometric mean anti-EBV (but not anti-CMV) titers were higher than in matched controls, significantly so for EBNA-1, EBNA-2, and EA-D; a 4-fold rise in anti-EBNA-2 carried the strongest risk (RR 3.9, 95% CI 1.1-13.7). The authors conclude the results support a role of EBV in the etiology of MS.

Ballerini et al 2025 Front Immunol.body: Bioinformatics network-medicine study using P-HIPSTer (EBV/CMV/Adenovirus-7 virus-host interactomes), NHGRI-EBI GWAS MS-associated genes, and the Human Protein Atlas to identify MS-associated genes overlapping the EBV interactome and expressed in immune and glial cells. EBV interactome significantly overlapped MS genes (45 genes, OR=2.2, p<0.001) more strongly than CMV (50 genes, OR=2.0), while Adenovirus-7 was a non-significant negative control (5 genes, OR=1.1, p=0.5). A core set of 21 genes was shared across the EBV interactome, MS genes, and immune/glial cells; pathway analysis highlighted prolactin signaling among others; transcriptomics showed MINK1 and ASAP1 upregulated in MS microglia, BCL2 upregulated and AHI1 downregulated in MS astrocytes, and ARHGAP27 upregulated in MS peripheral blood CD4+/CD8+ cells.

Banwell et al 2007 Lancet Neurol.body: Multinational observational case-control study of 137 children with multiple sclerosis (MS) and 96 age/region-matched non-MS controls across Canada/northern USA, southern USA, South America, and Europe, characterising clinical features and IgG serologies against EBV, CMV, parvovirus B19, VZV, and HSV. Paediatric MS was almost universally relapsing-remitting; ADEM-like first attacks occurred mainly in younger children. 86% of children with MS were seropositive for remote EBV infection versus 64% of controls; seropositivity for remote EBV conferred an ~2.8-fold increased likelihood of MS (p=0.025) and children with MS had significantly higher anti-EBNA1 titres, whereas CMV, parvovirus B19, VZV, and HSV seroprevalence did not differ between cases and controls, supporting a possible role for EBV in paediatric MS.

Banwell et al 2011 Lancet Neurol.body: Prospective Canadian national cohort study of 302 children with incident acute CNS demyelination, of whom 63 (21%) were diagnosed with multiple sclerosis. It assessed HLA-DRB1*15, remote Epstein-Barr-virus infection, and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D as predisposing factors and brain MRI/CSF oligoclonal bands as predictors. Each of the three predisposing factors independently increased MS risk (with EBV adjusted HR ~2.0-2.6), and higher anti-EBNA1 titres predicted MS; abnormal baseline MRI (HR ~38) and CSF oligoclonal bands (HR 6.33) strongly predicted MS, and a risk-stratification decision tree was derived.

Behrens et al 2026 Ann Neurol.body: High-dimensional serology profiling of virus-specific antibody features in 60 relapsing-onset MS patients (paired active-disease and remission samples) and 54 EBV-seropositive healthy controls from the Swiss MS Cohort. EBNA1-specific IgG in MS showed a distinct proinflammatory Fc signature: increased Fc gamma receptor (FcgammaR2A/FcgammaR3A) binding and enhanced Fc effector functions (ADCP, ADCD, ADNKA), specific to EBNA1 and not seen for EBV-gp350 or influenza-HA antibodies. Increased FcgammaR binding of EBNA1- and lytic EBV-gp350-specific IgG correlated with focal MS disease activity (clinical relapse and/or contrast-enhancing lesions), implicating EBV-antibody Fc effector functions in promoting disease activity.

Benincasa et al 2025 Int J Mol Sci.body: A post-mortem immunohistochemical study of brain tissue from secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (SPMS) donors investigating whether EBV exploits the PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitory checkpoint across phases of its life cycle. The authors found that EBNA2+ B cells in meningeal tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) co-express PD-L1, and that PD-L1 is also co-expressed on cells bearing the EBV early lytic antigens BHRF1, BMRF1 and BALF2, but not on cells expressing the immediate-early antigen BZLF1 or the late glycoprotein gp350/220. The percentage of EBNA2+ B cells correlated strongly with PD-L1+ cell numbers in inflamed meninges, and PD-L1+ CD35+ follicular dendritic cells contacted PD-1+ CD4+ T cells, supporting an immune-permissive niche for an intracerebral EBV reservoir.

Biström et al 2020 Eur J Neurol.body: Nested case-control study using pre-symptomatically collected blood from 670 Swedish individuals who later developed relapsing-remitting MS and 670 matched controls, with a bead-based multiplex serology assay measuring IgG against EBV (EBNA-1 trunc, EBNA-1 pep, VCA p18) and HHV-6A/HHV-6B (IE1A, IE1B, 101K). EBV seropositivity switched from a decreased MS risk below 20 years of age to an increased risk at ages 20-39 (trend p=0.020), with the protective-to-risk transition estimated at 18.8 years. HHV-6A (IE1A) seropositivity was associated with increased MS risk across all age groups (total cohort OR 2.1, 95% CI 1.6-2.7), while HHV-6B antigens showed no association. The authors conclude that EBV infection after adolescence and age-independent HHV-6A infection are risk factors for MS.

Bjornevik et al 2022 Science.body: Longitudinal nested case-control study within a cohort of >10 million active-duty US military personnel (1993-2013, Department of Defense Serum Repository) testing whether Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) causes multiple sclerosis (MS). Among 801 MS cases and 1566 matched controls, EBV seroconversion was associated with a 32-fold increased risk of MS (HR=32.4), all but one of 35 baseline EBV-negative MS cases seroconverted before MS onset, and serum neurofilament light chain (a neuroaxonal degeneration biomarker) rose only after EBV infection. Cytomegalovirus (a similarly transmitted herpesvirus) served as a negative control and showed no such association, and virome-wide VirScan screening found EBV as the only virus with elevated antibody responses in cases. The authors conclude EBV is the leading cause of MS.

Bjørnevik et al 2016 Mult Scler.body: Within the international EnvIMS case-control study (1904 MS patients and 3694 population-based frequency-matched controls from Norway, Italy, and Sweden), the authors examined the interaction between cigarette smoking and infectious mononucleosis (IM, a marker of symptomatic EBV infection) in the risk of multiple sclerosis. Smoking (pooled OR 1.73) and IM (pooled OR 2.14) were each independently associated with increased MS risk, but there was a statistically significant negative multiplicative interaction (ratio of ORs 0.52, p=0.001): among those reporting IM, smoking conferred no increased MS risk (OR 0.95), and the effect of IM was markedly lower among ever-smokers. The findings indicate competing antagonism, suggesting the two exposures operate on shared biologic pathways.

Bogers et al 2024 J Autoimmun.body: Bogers et al. studied how the MS coding risk SNP rs9808753 in IFNGR2 and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection cooperate to affect the IFN-γ signaling pathway in human B cells, using 4 selected B lymphoblastoid cell lines and primary blood B cells from MS patients and controls. In both cell lines and primary cells, EBV infection positively associated with IFN-γ receptor (IFNGR2) expression and STAT1 phosphorylation, while the IFNGR2 risk SNP selectively promoted downstream STAT1 phosphorylation, particularly in transitional B cells. The authors conclude that EBV and the IFNGR2 risk SNP independently amplify B cell-intrinsic IFN-γ signaling, potentially driving B cells to enter the MS brain.

Borkosky et al 2012 PLoS One.body: In vitro study transfecting two full-length Torque Teno Virus isolates (TTV-HD14b and TTV-HD14c, isolated from multiple sclerosis brain) into a panel of EBV-positive and EBV-negative Burkitt's lymphoma and B-cell lines. Both TTV genomes replicated up to day 21 post-transfection in all lines, with significantly higher replication (p<0.05) in EBV-positive lines (including the EBV-converted BJAB/EBV line) versus the EBV-negative BJAB calibrator, demonstrating an EBV helper effect on TTV replication. The enhancement was independent of EBV genome copy number and gp350/220 lytic activity. The authors propose that EBV (via EBNA-1) supports TTV persistence in memory B cells and that TTV proteins sharing motifs with myelin basic protein could drive molecular mimicry, linking EBV-TTV interaction to MS pathogenesis.

Bray et al 1992 Neurology.body: Bray et al assayed antibodies against three EBV antigens (EBNA-1, VCA, EA-D) in the CSF of multiple sclerosis (MS) patients versus neurologic disease controls (NDC). Anti-EBNA-1 IgG, reacting with a heat-stable 70 kD protein on immunoblot, was present in 85% (79/93) of MS CSF samples versus 13% of EBV-seropositive controls (p < 0.001), and chymotrypsin digestion yielded a confirmatory 40 kD glycine-alanine-copolymer fragment. The 14 MS patients lacking CSF anti-EBNA-1 all had CSF oligoclonal bands, giving 100% combined sensitivity. A FASTA search of the PIR database found two pentapeptide identities (QKRPS and PRHRD) shared only between EBNA-1 and myelin basic protein, supporting a molecular-mimicry mechanism in which MHC-restricted T cells damage MBP.

Brennan et al 2010 Mult Scler.body: Brennan et al. sequenced the EBV genes encoding EBNA1 (codons 1-89 and 340-641) and BRRF2 in EBV isolates from 40 multiple sclerosis (MS) patients and a similar number of controls, using spontaneous lymphoblastoid cell lines, to test whether genetic variability in EBV is associated with MS. Extensive sequence polymorphism was found in both genes in patients and controls, with several EBNA1 SNPs (positions 439, 499, 588) and one BRRF2 SNP (position 412, Ser->Tyr) overrepresented and others (positions 16/18/85/429) underrepresented in MS isolates. Phylogenetic trees showed no distinct MS-specific clades; the authors conclude there is no simple causal relationship between EBV strain variation and MS, though some haplotypes occur at different frequencies in patients versus controls.

Buljevac et al 2005 J Neurol Neurosurg P.body: A prospective cohort study (Rotterdam Study on Exacerbations in MS, ROSE) of 73 relapsing-remitting MS patients followed ~1.7 years, testing whether exacerbations and gadolinium-enhanced MRI activity associate with plasma anti-EBV antibodies and EBV DNA. All MS patients were anti-VCA IgG positive (100% EBV seropositive); 48% were anti-EA IgG positive versus 25% of age-matched healthy controls (p=0.013), with higher anti-EA titres in MS (p<0.001), while anti-CMV IgG did not differ. Anti-EA seropositivity and titres were stable over time (ICC=0.96) and unrelated to exacerbations, and EBV DNA viraemia was rare and transient. However, anti-EA-positive patients showed more gadolinium-enhanced and new MRI lesions (triple-dose Gd series significant), suggesting chronic EBV reactivation may associate with subclinical inflammatory MRI activity.

Casiraghi et al 2010 J Neuroimmunol.body: Casiraghi, Dorovini-Zis and Horwitz show that Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) can productively infect primary human brain microvessel endothelial cells (HBMECs), the cells of the blood-brain barrier (BBB), and express viral genes (EBNA-1 in two donors, BZLF-1 and LMP-2B in single donors). EBV infection up-regulated the pro-inflammatory chemokine CCL-5 (RANTES) and the adhesion molecule ICAM-1 (but not VCAM-1), and significantly increased adhesion of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) to the endothelial monolayer. The authors propose that reactivation of latent EBV in brain endothelial cells could breach the BBB and attract autoreactive lymphocytes, modeling a key step in MS pathogenesis.

Casiraghi et al 2015 Sci Rep.body: Using murine gamma-herpesvirus 68 (gammaHV-68), the murine homolog of EBV, as a model for the EBV-MS link, this study shows that latent (not acute) gammaHV-68 infection enhances experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) to resemble MS. Enhanced disease required the viral latent life cycle and was associated with upregulation of CD40 and phosphorylated STAT1 on uninfected CD11b+CD11c+ antigen-presenting cells, driving a strong Th1 response and CD4+/CD8+ T cell brain infiltration. Latency, acting via a CD40-dependent mechanism, also reduced regulatory T cell (Treg) frequencies in the periphery and CNS; CD40 knockout or use of the latency-deficient gammaHV-68 AC-RTA strain abolished these effects. The authors propose that latent gamma-herpesviruses like EBV predispose to autoimmunity by programming APCs (CD40/STAT1), skewing Th1, and suppressing Tregs.

Castellazzi et al 2010 Mult Scler.body: A case-control study measuring CSF and serum levels and intrathecal synthesis of anti-EBV IgG (anti-VCA and anti-EBNA-1) by ELISA in 80 untreated relapsing-remitting MS patients versus 80 OIND and 80 NIND controls. Anti-VCA IgG was lower in MS than in OIND and, in serum, was higher in MRI-inactive (Gd-) than MRI-active (Gd+) MS, whereas anti-EBNA-1 IgG was higher in MS than controls in both CSF and serum. Serum anti-VCA IgG correlated positively and anti-EBNA-1 IgG inversely with EDSS. Intrathecal synthesis of anti-EBV IgG occurred in only a small proportion of MS and controls, so the findings do not support a direct pathogenetic role of EBV-targeted humoral immunity in MS.

Castellazzi et al 2023 Int J Mol Sci.body: A longitudinal prospective pilot study of 17 relapsing-remitting MS patients evaluating the effect of dimethyl fumarate (DMF), a first-line oral disease-modifying treatment, on the amount and avidity of EBV-specific IgG over 6 months (T0 pre-therapy, then 1 week, 1, 3 and 6 months). Serum anti-EBV capsid antigen (CA) IgG levels decreased significantly from the first week and remained reduced through 6 months, with a partial reduction in anti-EBNA-1 IgG (significant at 3 months). All patients had high-avidity anti-CA IgG at baseline, and avidity (relative avidity index) did not change during therapy. The authors conclude DMF can reduce the quantity but not the avidity of the anti-EBV humoral response in MS from very early treatment stages, with no correlation between anti-EBV IgG and EDSS disability.

Cencioni et al 2017 Immunology.body: Cencioni et al. investigated effector cytotoxic CD8+ CD57+ T-cell responses to Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) in 36 healthy donors and 35 patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RR-MS) in stable versus active disease, plus post-mortem secondary progressive MS brain tissue. CD8+ CD57+ T cells were polyfunctional effectors that degranulated (CD107a, granzyme B, perforin) and released IFN-gamma to kill autologous EBV-infected B-lymphoblastoid cell lines, and their cytotoxicity inversely correlated with programmed death 1 (PD-1) expression. Patients with stable MS showed significantly elevated PD-1 on CD8+ CD57+ T cells with suppressed cytokine release and degranulation (an exhaustion-like phenotype), whereas anti-PD-1 blockade restored degranulation, cytokine release and cytotoxicity. CD8+ CD57+ T cells were detected in meningeal and perivascular MS infiltrates and their frequency correlated negatively with age at progression and death, supporting that impaired PD-1-regulated control of EBV during remission may enable CNS viral reactivation and disease progression.

Cepok et al 2005 J Clin Invest.body: Cepok et al. screened a human brain cDNA protein-expression array (37,000 clones) with CSF IgG from MS patients to decode the specificity of intrathecal oligoclonal antibodies. Epitope mapping of the two most frequent MS-specific reactivities identified peptide sequences from two adjacently encoded latent EBV proteins, EBNA-1 and BRRF2. IgG immunoreactivity to EBNA-1 and BRRF2 was significantly higher in serum and CSF of MS patients than controls, oligoclonal CSF IgG specifically bound both proteins (intrathecal synthesis), and EBV-specific CD8+CD28+ T cell responses were higher in MS patients, supporting an important role for EBV in MS pathogenesis.

Chang et al 2026 Mult Scler.body: A US Network of Pediatric MS Centers case-control (359 POMS cases, 560 controls) and longitudinal study investigating whether a history of adenotonsillectomy is associated with pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (POMS) risk and relapse rate. Prior adenotonsillectomy was associated with 63% increased odds of POMS (adjusted OR=1.63, 95% CI 1.01-2.64, p=0.046) and a twofold higher annualized relapse rate (adjusted IRR=2.00, 95% CI 1.15-3.48, p=0.013). The authors hypothesize a potential interplay between EBV, the tonsils/adenoids as a primary EBV reservoir, immune regulation, and MS pathogenesis.

Christensen et al 2006 J Neuroimmunol.body: A family-based serological study of 105 individuals from 46 multiple sclerosis (MS) families (25 sporadic, 42 familial cases) examining gene-environment interactions. Elevated, epitope-specific antibody reactivity to HERV-H peptides (notably Env E/E2 regions) correlated with MS disease activity and early onset, while high MBL and MASP-3 levels showed indications of a protective (slower-progression) effect. For seven representative families the authors also measured herpesvirus serology (HSV, VZV, EBV): all MS patients were anti-EBV EBNA IgG positive, but no significant difference in anti-EBV (or other herpesvirus) antibody levels was found between MS patients and unaffected relatives, although the three individuals with recent/ongoing EBV reactivation were all MS patients. HLA B7, DR2 (DRB1*1501) and DQ6 (DQB1*0602) alleles were common but occurred almost as frequently in unaffected relatives.

Cocuzza et al 2014 PLoS One.body: Case-control study quantifying EBV EBNA-1 DNA by standardized commercial real-time PCR in cell-free and cell-associated CSF and peripheral blood (plasma, PBMC) of 55 treatment-naive relapsing-remitting MS patients during acute relapse versus 51 controls (40 NIND, 11 OIND). EBV DNA positivity rates and median viral loads did not differ significantly between RRMS and controls in any compartment, except higher PBMC positivity in RRMS versus NIND (p=0.013, OR=3.1). The authors conclude, despite highly sensitive methods, there is a lack of association between EBV DNA and MS disease activity.

Comabella et al 2010 Mult Scler.body: A family-based case-control study comparing virus antigen-specific IgG responses in 25 untreated multiple sclerosis (MS) patients versus 49 healthy full-siblings raised in the same household. IgG responses to the latent Epstein-Barr virus nuclear antigen-1 (EBNA1) were selectively and markedly increased in MS patients versus their unaffected siblings (p=0.0007; confirmed p=0.0002 on diluted sera), whereas responses to EBV viral capsid antigen, HHV-6, HCMV, and measles virus, as well as EBV seroprevalence and cell-bound EBV DNA load, did not differ. The authors conclude that elevated anti-EBNA1 IgG is specifically associated with MS development rather than an MS-specific EBV strain.

Comabella et al 2011 Mult Scler.body: A prospective study of 28 relapse-onset MS patients who were clinical responders to interferon-beta (IFNbeta), evaluating EBV- and HCMV-specific humoral (ELISA) and cellular (CFSE flow cytometry) immune responses before and 1 year after treatment. Clinically effective IFNbeta therapy was associated with a marked downregulation of proliferative EBNA1-specific CD4+ T-cell responses, while anti-EBNA1 and anti-VCA IgG and CD8+ T-cell responses to lytic/transformation EBV antigens and HCMV were largely unchanged. HCMV-specific IgG slightly decreased. The authors conclude EBNA1 is a target antigen of the pathological immune response in MS and its specific T-cell response is associated with clinical response to IFNbeta.

Comabella et al 2022 J Neurol Neurosurg.body: A long-term (median 20-year) follow-up of a Barcelona cohort of 143 patients with MS (originally CIS) evaluated whether antiviral IgG responses measured at the first demyelinating event predict disability and inflammation outcomes. Elevated HCMV (cytomegalovirus) IgG at onset was protective, being associated in univariable analysis with lower risk of reaching EDSS 4.0, of developing SPMS, and of first-line treatment, plus longer time to first-line therapy. In contrast, elevated EBV-VCA IgG predicted earlier first- and second-line treatment, and elevated EBNA1 IgG independently predicted a higher relapse rate (and correlated with disease severity); HHV6 and measles played no major prognostic role.

Comabella et al 2025 J Neurol.body: A multicenter case-control study comparing antibody (IgG) responses to ubiquitous viruses (EBV EBNA1 and VCA, HCMV, HHV-6, and measles) in 68 primary progressive MS (PPMS) patients (mean follow-up 8 years) versus 66 sex- and age-matched healthy controls. PPMS patients showed a selective, significant increase in EBNA1-specific IgG (p=0.03) but not to VCA or other viral antigens, and significantly higher HCMV seroprevalence (76.5% vs 50%, p=0.001). Baseline antiviral immune responses did not correlate with disability progression (EDSS) at short, medium, or long term.

Cortese et al 2024 JAMA Neurol.body: Prospective nested case-control study of 30 US military personnel with multiple sclerosis (MS) and 30 matched controls, profiling the preclinical antibody response to the entire EBV peptidome (2263 peptides) using VirScan. The antibody response to the EBV peptidome and to EBNA antigens was overall stronger in pre-onset MS sera, and higher total anti-EBNA-1 antibodies were associated with elevated MS risk (top vs bottom tertile RR 27.6). After adjusting for total anti-EBNA-1, most peptide associations attenuated, but antibodies to EBNA-6/EBNA-3C, LMP-1, EBNA-3/EBNA-3A and BDLF3.5 peptides remained associated. The authors conclude anti-EBNA-1 is the strongest serologic risk factor for MS, with no single EBV epitope selectively targeted only in MS.

Cossu et al 2014 Mult Scler.body: Case-control immunology study (47 MS patients, 53 healthy controls; Sardinia) of humoral and T-cell responses against three homologous mimicry peptides: EBV tegument protein BOLF1_305-320, Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis MAP_4027_18-32, and human IRF5_424-434. Antibodies against the peptides were far more prevalent in MS patients than controls, the peptides cross-inhibited antibody binding (supporting molecular mimicry), and they induced Th1 cytokines (IL-6, IFN-gamma, TNF-alpha) from CD4+/CD8+ T cells and CD14+ monocytes while Th2 cytokines were downregulated. The authors conclude EBV and MAP epitopes elicit a consistent MS-correlated humoral and cellular immune response.

De Jager et al 2008 Neurology.body: A nested case-control study within the Nurses' Health Study (NHS) and NHS II cohorts (148 women with MS, 18 with pre-onset blood, and 296 age-matched healthy women) testing whether the HLA-DRB1*1501 (DR15) allele and anti-EBV antibody titers are independent risk factors for MS. The association between anti-EBNA-1 antibody titers and MS risk was unaffected by adjustment for DR15 and was similar in DR15-positive and DR15-negative women, indicating both are independent risk factors. The relative risk of MS among DR15-positive women with elevated (>1:320) anti-EBNA-1 titers was ninefold higher (RR 9.67) than among DR15-negative women with low titers, with the two factors combining multiplicatively.

De Jager et al 2009 Lancet Neurol.body: De Jager and colleagues built a weighted genetic risk score (wGRS) from 16 MS susceptibility loci (two MHC alleles plus 14 non-MHC SNPs) and tested it in a derivation set (2215 MS, 2189 controls) and two validation sets (TT therapeutic-trial cohort; US Nurses' Health Study I/II). The wGRS modestly discriminated MS from controls (C statistic 0.697 in derivation), with most predictive power from the HLA-DRB1*1501 allele. Adding non-genetic risk factors improved discrimination: sex raised the TT C statistic to 0.721, and smoking plus anti-EBNA1 (EBV) antibody titres raised the NHS C statistic from 0.635 to 0.683. The wGRS did not predict conversion of clinically isolated syndrome to MS (HR ~1.00, p=0.99).

DeLorenze et al 2006 Arch Neurol.body: A prospective nested case-control study within the Kaiser Permanente Northern California cohort (42 MS cases with serum collected up to 30 years before onset, vs 79 matched / 132 all controls) testing whether anti-EBV antibody titers precede MS onset. Geometric mean IgG titers to the EBNA complex and EBNA-1 were significantly higher in MS cases (RR per 4-fold increase 2.1 and 1.8 vs matched controls), whereas titers to VCA, early antigens, and CMV were not. Elevations of anti-EBNA complex and anti-EBNA-1 titers first appeared 15-20 years before symptom onset and persisted, suggesting elevated anti-EBV antibodies are an early event in MS pathogenesis rather than a result of nonspecific immune dysregulation.

Deffenbaugh et al 2024 J Neuroimmunol.body: Short communication describing a novel mouse model of multiple sclerosis in which myelin basic protein-specific transgenic TCR (TCR-MBP) mice on the B10.PL background were intranasally infected with murid gammaherpesvirus 68 (MHV68), an EBV-like virus. MHV68 infection induced encephalitogenic disease in 70.8% of mice (vs 13.6% PBS and 7.7% influenza, p=0.0003), with MS-like signs including optic neuritis and ataxia, focal CNS inflammation, demyelination, and CD4/CD8 T-cell infiltration. Single-cell RNA sequencing of splenic B cells identified an MHV68-expanded B-cell population (cluster 4) resembling age-associated B cells (Zeb2/T-bet high, CD21-low) that upregulates antigen-presentation, costimulation (Cd86, Cd69), and interferon-response genes, proposed to promote autoreactive T-cell responses in MS.

Dominguez-Mozo et al 2020 Sci Rep.body: Multicenter retrospective longitudinal study of 186 multiple sclerosis patients treated with natalizumab and followed for 2 years, searching for predictive factors and early biomarkers of treatment response (clinical response and NEDA-3). Three variables were independently associated with optimal response: lower baseline EDSS (<3.0), lower baseline anti-EBNA-1 IgG titers, and a decrease in HHV-6 IgG antibody titers between baseline and 6 months. Baseline VCA IgG and HHV-6 IgG/IgM titers, IgG/IgM oligoclonal bands, and HLA class II were not significantly associated after correction.

Dominguez-Mozo et al 2021 Cells.body: Cross-sectional case-control study of 191 MS patients (133 RRMS, 58 SPMS) and 79 healthy controls (HC) analyzing the humoral response to EBV (EBNA-1, VCA), HHV-6A/B and CMV, serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, and three short-chain fatty acids (acetate, propionate, butyrate), correlated with clinical variables and a wide panel of immune cell subsets. MS patients showed higher EBNA-1, VCA and HHV-6A/B IgG and lower CMV IgG and 25(OH)D than HC. The strongest clinical and cellular correlations were for 25(OH)D and SCFA; a 25(OH)D + propionate/acetate interaction negatively correlated with IL-17-producing CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in untreated MS patients.

Dominguez-Mozo et al 2023 Front Immunol.body: Multicenter longitudinal study of 101 Spanish RRMS patients treated with teriflunomide, evaluating in vivo antiviral activity by measuring anti-EBNA-1, anti-VCA (EBV) and anti-HHV-6 IgG/IgM titers and serum neurofilament light chain (Nf-L) at baseline and 6 months. Teriflunomide reduced antiviral IgG titers (EBNA-1 IgG decreased in 73.3%, VCA IgG 69%, HHV-6 IgG 60.4%, HHV-6 IgM 74.3%). Baseline VCA IgG correlated with Nf-L levels. Higher baseline EBNA-1 IgG titers and older starting age independently predicted NEDA-3 (better clinical/radiological response) after 2 years.

Dominguez-Mozo et al 2024 Front Immunol.body: Retrospective multicenter cohort of 151 relapsing-remitting MS patients treated with fingolimod for 24 months, assessing clinical, radiological, genetic (HLA-II) and viral serology (EBV EBNA-1/VCA IgG, HHV-6 IgG/IgM) factors as early predictors of NEDA-3 response. Male sex, older age, <=1 relapse 2-years before, and absence of Gd+ lesions at baseline predicted NEDA-3; DR4 (HLA-DRB1*04) carriers were better clinical responders and none progressed. Baseline EBV/HHV-6 serologies were not associated with NEDA-3, but EBNA-1 IgG titers decreased in 73.3% of relapse-associated-worsening (RAW) vs 20.0% of progression-independent-of-relapse-activity (PIRA) patients, linking EBV to relapse-associated MS progression.

Dooley et al 2016 J Neuroimmunol.body: Case-control study comparing the antibody response to individual Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) proteins in 80 relapsing-remitting MS patients versus 80 matched controls. Candidate EBV antigens were identified by immunoprecipitation with patient IgG followed by 4-plex iTRAQ quantitative mass spectrometry, and antibody responses to 10 recombinant EBV proteins were measured by quantitative ELISA. The increased anti-EBV antibody response in MS was restricted to three proteins, EBNA-1 (BKRF1), the small capsid protein BFRF3, and BRRF2, while the other seven antigens (BZLF1, BMLF1, MCP/BcLF1, BLRF2, gp42, gH, gp350) showed no significant increase; this is reported as the first replication of an increased anti-BRRF2 response in MS.

Décard et al 2012 J Neurol Neurosurg Psy.body: Retrospective German case-control study of 56 pre-CIS serum samples from 25 individuals who later developed MS, plus post-diagnosis samples and age/gender-matched healthy blood donor controls. Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (measured by LC-MS/MS, seasonally deconvoluted) was progressively reduced during the 24 months before clinically isolated syndrome and lowest after established MS diagnosis, while anti-EBNA1 IgG (ELISA) was elevated across the pre-CIS phase, most pronounced 2-3 years before CIS. Vitamin D and EBNA1 immunoreactivity were not correlated and not associated with disease course or severity, suggesting low vitamin D and remote EBV infection mark a susceptible 2-3 year pre-clinical window for MS.

Eberspächer et al 2020 J Neurol Neurosur.body: A seroepidemiological study of the German National MS cohort measuring EBV antibodies (EBNA-1 IgG and VCA IgG by CLIA, with EBV IgG immunoblot confirmation) in 901 patients with early MS (clinically isolated syndrome or early relapsing-remitting MS). All 901 of 901 (100%) patients were EBV-seropositive, including 100% of the 380 CIS patients, whereas a large hospital reference population (N=16 163) never reached 100% seropositivity in any age cohort (95.2% at age 20-40 years; p<0.0001). The complete EBV seropositivity strengthens evidence for a role of EBV in MS and suggests a negative EBV serology in suspected inflammatory CNS disease should prompt consideration of diagnoses other than MS.

Eisner et al 2026 Environ Epigenet.body: In the Australian Ausimmune incident case-control study (206 MS cases, 348 matched controls), the authors tested whether human herpesvirus (HHV) indices are associated with MS-associated DNA methylation (DNAm) modules and whether HHV-6 DNA positivity influences MS onset risk through epigenetic pathways. HHV-6 DNA positivity was associated with the A2 DNAm module and higher CMV IgG with the A4 module, while EBV serologies (VCA, EA-D, EA-R), HHV-6 IgG/IgM, and VZV indices were not associated with any module. Counterfactual mediation analysis found the A2 module mediated 45% of the HHV-6 DNA positivity-MS onset association (OR_indirect=1.65, P=.008); the A2 module was enriched for lymphatic/immune cell types (notably CD8+ cytotoxic T cells), SUMOylation pathways, and immune transcription factors (TERC, IRF5, EGR2/EGR3). HHV-6 epigenetic mediation varied by combined HLA risk genotype.

Engdahl et al 2019 Front Immunol.body: A Swedish case-control study using a novel bead-based multiplex serology assay that distinguishes IgG against the immediate-early 1 proteins of HHV-6A (IE1A) and HHV-6B (IE1B), tested in an established MS cohort (8,742 MS, 7,215 controls) and a pre-MS cohort (478 future-MS, 476 controls). High anti-IE1A IgG was positively associated with MS (OR=1.55) and with future MS risk (OR=2.22, strongest in adolescents), while anti-IE1B IgG was negatively associated with MS (OR=0.74). An additive interaction was found between strong IE1A and EBV responses (AP=0.24), and serological responses mapped genetically to the HLA region, supporting a role for HHV-6A in MS etiology.

Engelenburg et al 2026 Acta Neuropathol.body: Post-mortem neuropathology study of perivascular cuffs in white matter of 255 MS donors (Netherlands Brain Bank), with detailed immunohistochemical characterization of 457 cuffs from 18 donors. Cuffs were present in 25.5% of donors and associated with a more inflammatory active disease (younger age at death, more nodules, higher brainstem lesion count, more active and fewer inactive lesions). Cuffs showed a relative increase in CD4+ over CD8+ T cells and increased B-lineage (CD79a/CD19/CD20) cells in active and mixed active/inactive lesions, with CD38+ antibody-secreting cells and IgG; CD38+/B-cell abundance correlated with CD4+ T-cell density and proliferation. EBV was detected by qPCR in CNS-isolated B cells of 6/6 MS donors, but LMP-1+ B cells were sparse in cuffs (13/122 cuffs, 6/11 donors), indicating EBV is unlikely the main driver of cuff B-cell accumulation. BTK was abundant in B cells and CD206+ macrophages and correlated with CD19+ and CD206+ cell abundance, supporting targetability by brain-penetrating BTK inhibitors.

Erdur et al 2016 J Neuroimmunol.body: Erdur et al. measured the frequency of CD8+ T cells specific for one HLA-B35-restricted EBNA1-derived epitope (HPVGEADYFEY) in blood and cerebrospinal fluid of patients with multiple sclerosis versus other inflammatory neurological diseases (OIND), using HLA-class-I pentamer staining, with a CMV pp65 epitope (NLVPMVATV) as comparison. The frequency of HPVGEADYFEY-specific CD8+ T cells did not differ significantly between MS and OIND in blood (p=0.18) or CSF (p=0.11). However, HPVGEADYFEY-specific CD8+ T cells were consistently more frequent in CSF than in blood regardless of diagnosis (9/9 patients), whereas CMV-specific CD8+ T cells were more frequent in blood than CSF (4/4 patients), suggesting privileged intrathecal access of EBNA1-specific CD8+ T cells.

Franciotta et al 2010 J Neuroimmunol.body: A retrospective study measuring serum and CSF BAFF and determining total and EBV-specific oligoclonal IgG bands (OCBs) in 43 MS patients, 23 with other inflammatory demyelinating diseases (ADEM, NMO), and 20 with non-inflammatory neurological diseases. Serum and CSF BAFF did not differ between groups, but in RR-MS the highest CSF BAFF was found in samples with more than 6 OCBs (233.1 vs 79.2 pg/mL, p<0.0001), associating BAFF with intrathecal IgG production rather than diagnosis. EBV-specific OCBs were detected in 50% of patients with similar frequency across groups and predominantly as a serum/CSF 'mirror pattern' (30 of 33 cases), indicating the EBV-specific antibody response is mostly systemic and not preferentially restricted to MS.

Gabibov et al 2011 FASEB J.body: Gabibov et al. constructed a phage-display single-chain variable fragment (scFv) library from blood lymphocytes of 8 relapsing-remitting MS patients and selected 13 anti-MBP monoclonal scFv clones. Structural/germline analysis showed that 10/13 heavy and 7/13 light chains were homologous to Griffin1-selected anti-EBV LMP1 antibodies and to CSF MS-associated autoantibodies. One clone, E2, in both scFv and full-size human IgG (rhAb E2) form, bound both myelin basic protein (MBP) and EBV latent membrane protein 1 (LMP1) in vitro, providing structural evidence for germline-encoded molecular mimicry as a possible link between EBV and MS.

Gieß et al 2017 PLoS One.body: Prospective observational cohort study (Berlin CIS cohort, NCT01371071) of 100 patients with clinically isolated syndrome (CIS) or early relapsing-remitting MS and 60 healthy controls, examining whether serum EBNA-1 and VCA IgG antibodies and salivary EBV DNA load are associated with MRI and clinical (EDSS) disease activity and conversion to clinically definite MS. EBNA-1 IgG frequency and EBNA-1/VCA IgG levels were significantly higher in patients than controls and EBV seroprevalence was 100% in patients, confirming EBV's association with early MS. However, neither EBV antibody levels nor salivary EBV DNA load were associated with any radiological or clinical disease activity marker at baseline or follow-up, nor with conversion to CDMS. Salivary EBV DNA load did not differ between patients and controls.

Goldacre et al 2004 J Epidemiol Communit.body: Record-linkage cohort study using the Oxford record linkage study (hospital admission and death records, central southern England, 1963-1999) comparing rates of subsequent multiple sclerosis in 2767 people admitted for infectious mononucleosis versus a reference cohort of 640,163 patients. Across all time intervals the association was non-significant (rate ratio 2.17, 95% CI 0.79-4.77), but at intervals of 10+ years it was significant (rate ratio 4.01, 95% CI 1.48-8.93), based on 6 observed MS cases. The mean interval from infectious mononucleosis to first MS admission was 14 years, supporting EBV/IM as an initiator of MS remote in time rather than an activator of latent disease.

Goldacre et al 2024 Mult Scler.body: Retrospective national population-based cohort study using English Hospital Episode Statistics (2003-2023) comparing MS incidence in 51,592 individuals hospitalised with infectious mononucleosis (IM) versus a reference cohort of 6,711,441 representing the general population. MS incidence in the IM cohort was nearly three times higher after multivariable adjustment (aHR=2.80, 95% CI 2.31-3.39). The elevated risk was driven by strong associations at long time intervals (aHR=4.31 at 5-9 years and 3.27 at 10-20 years) and was not significant in the first 1-4 years, implicating the clinical disease process of IM beyond EBV infection alone over the long term.

Gottlieb et al 2024 Proc Natl Acad Sci U.body: Gottlieb et al. used bulk TCR Vβ CDR3 RNA sequencing of CSF, PBMC, and antigen-stimulated T cells from eight relapsing-remitting MS patients (plus OND and healthy controls) to test whether expanded CSF T-cell clones are specific for autologous EBV-infected lymphoblastoid cell lines (LCL). LCL-specific T cells comprised 13.0 ± 4.3% of CSF reads (more than EBV, VZV, flu, or candida), the CSF repertoire overlapped most with LCL (Jaccard 0.03, significant in all MS subjects, FDR P<0.0009), and LCL specificity rose to ~47% in the top 1% most abundant CSF clones. The authors conclude that expanded LCL-specific T-cell clones are present in MS CSF at symptom onset, implicating the anti-EBV-infected-B-cell immune response in MS pathogenesis.

Gouzouasis et al 2025 J Neuroimmunol.body: A flow-cytometry immunoprofiling study of matched peripheral blood (PB) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from 33 treatment-naive Hellenic multiple sclerosis patients, relating immune cell profiles to plasma EBV serology and EBV gene expression (BZLF1 mRNA, EBNA1 DNA). 12 of 33 patients (39%) showed serological evidence of EBV reactivation (EBV-R) and 7 were positive for plasma BZLF1 mRNA. EBV-R was associated with reduced CD19+ B cells, increased cytotoxic CD56dim NK cells and CD14+ monocytes in PB, while in CSF B cells stayed elevated and cytotoxic NK cells were absent; regulatory CD56bright NK cells were reduced in both compartments during EBV-R. Plasma EBNA1 DNA correlated with active spinal cord lesions.

Gronen et al 2006 J Neuroimmunol.body: Case-control study comparing the frequency of HLA-B7-restricted EBV-specific CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTL) by IFN-gamma ELISPOT in HLA-B7+ MS patients (n=23) and healthy controls (n=26), using seven HLA-B7-restricted immunogenic EBV peptides. CTL responses were dominated by the EBNA3A peptide RPPIFIRRL, but the frequency and magnitude of EBV-specific CTL did not differ significantly between MS patients and controls (RPPIFIRRL: 16/23 vs 21/26, p=0.51; mean 68.5 vs 94.9 spots/10^6 PBMC, p=0.38). All MS patients were EBV-seropositive (100% vs 89.7% of controls), and HLA-B7 was more frequent in MS (39.7% vs 25%, n.s.) and significantly enriched in PPMS. The data do not support the hypothesis that EBV contributes to MS via quantitatively altered EBV-specific CTL responses.

Grut et al 2021 Eur J Neurol.body: A nested, presymptomatic case-control study (670 matched case-control pairs from Swedish MS registries and biobanks) using a bead-based multiplex serology assay to test whether cytomegalovirus (CMV) serostatus influences multiple sclerosis (MS) risk. CMV seropositivity was associated with a reduced risk of developing MS (adjusted OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.56-0.88, p=0.003), independent of EBV and HHV-6A serostatus and robust in samples drawn >8 years before onset. EBV seropositivity raised MS risk at age 20-39 and HHV-6A seropositivity raised MS risk across all ages. Significant additive interactions were found between CMV seronegativity and seropositivity for HHV-6A and for the EBV antigen EBNA-1 peptide (aa 385-420), supporting a protective role for CMV in MS aetiology.

Guerrero-Fernández et al 2026 Mult Scler.body: Case report of a 48-year-old woman diagnosed with MS in 2019 who, 15 years earlier (2003) as a spinal-anaesthesia control in a virus/MS case-control study, already showed elevated intrathecal antibody synthesis (ITS) specific to Epstein-Barr virus (anti-EBNA1 ITS EBV = 3.32, the only value above cut-off among 15 subgroup-1 controls) while her MRZ reaction (measles/rubella/varicella-zoster ITS) was negative. A 2025 medical-record review found she was the only subgroup-1 control who later developed MS. The authors propose that a specific EBV intrathecal antibody response may be an early biological marker of an EBV-associated 'biologically isolated syndrome', present years before clinical MS onset.

Gustavsen et al 2014 BMC Neurol.body: Norwegian questionnaire-based case-control study of 530 MS patients and 918 healthy controls examining environmental and lifestyle risk factors for multiple sclerosis, with a focus on childhood exposures and the hygiene hypothesis. It replicated that a history of infectious mononucleosis and smoking are associated with increased MS risk, while ever snuff use was less frequent in patients. It also found that growing up with a cat (and to a lesser extent a dog) in the household before age 18 was associated with reduced MS risk, an effect that persisted for cat ownership after adjusting for age, gender, smoking, IM and HLA-DRB1*15:01.

Haahr et al 1992 Neuroepidemiology.body: A 1992 hypothesis/review article proposing that multiple sclerosis (MS) and MS-like diseases are caused by a dual infection: a hitherto uncharacterized retrovirus as the etiological agent, with development of neurologic disease related to or dependent on a delayed (late childhood) EBV infection. The authors review evidence that 99-100% of MS patients are EBV-seropositive (vs 86-95% of controls), that a prior history of infectious mononucleosis (late EBV) is positively associated with MS (relative risk 3.7), and that a cell line from an MS-like patient produced both retrovirus-like and EBV particles, indicating dual infection. They argue this dual-infection hypothesis is consistent with MS epidemiology (latitude gradient, migration, familial/geographic clustering, the Faroe Islands epidemic) and suggest EBV may drive MS relapses, raising the possibility of treatment with acyclovir-type nucleoside analogues.

Haahr et al 1995 Mult Scler.body: A Danish nationwide historical prospective study linking records of heterophile antibody (Paul-Bunnell) tests for infectious mononucleosis (IM, a marker of clinically apparent/late primary EBV infection) at the State Serum Institute to the Danish Multiple Sclerosis Registry. Among 6853 HA-positive persons, 16 developed MS after the test versus 5.70 expected, giving a relative risk of 2.81 (P<0.05); no patient developed MS before IM. Among 12886 HA-negative persons, MS incidence (12 observed vs 10.47 expected) did not differ from the general population. The authors conclude that late symptomatic EBV infection is a co-factor in MS pathogenesis, proposing a dual EBV-retrovirus hypothesis.

Haahr et al 2004 Acta Neurol Scand.body: Danish seroepidemiological/case-control study assessing the timing of EBV seroconversion in a high-MS-prevalence area and the recall of infectious mononucleosis in young MS patients versus matched controls. EBV serology on 1154 blood samples showed that more than one third of the Danish population remains EBV-seronegative at puberty (late seroconversion; 94% seropositive in adulthood), in contrast to early complete seroconversion in low-MS-prevalence areas. Recall of diagnosed IM was significantly more frequent in MS patients (12/53) than controls (4/53), all MS patients (including immunosuppression-naive) were EBV seropositive, and a serologic EBV-reactivation pattern was significantly more frequent in MS diagnosed within the preceding 2 years, supporting a role of late EBV infection in MS.
Haahr et al 2004 Acta Neurol Scand.identifier: Haahr et al 2004 Acta Neurol Scand

Hanefeld et al 2009 J Neurol.body: Pohl/Hanefeld et al studied paired CSF and serum from 43 pediatric onset MS, 50 adult onset MS, and 32 other-CNS-disease patients to assess intrathecal (CNS-derived) antibody production against EBV (EBNA-I and EBV-VCA) versus measles, rubella, VZV and HSV using CSF-to-serum Antibody Indices. Intrathecal EBV antibody synthesis was infrequent (26% pediatric, 10% adult MS) and lower in both frequency and intensity than for measles, rubella and VZV, and EBV genome was undetectable in all 43 CSF samples by PCR. The authors conclude the EBV-targeted humoral immune response is only part of a polyspecific CNS antibody production and argue against a direct pathogenic role of EBV-targeted humoral immunity within the CNS, while not excluding cellular immune mechanisms.

Hassani et al 2018 PLoS One.body: Hassani et al. examined 1055 specimens (440 DNA samples and 615 brain tissue blocks) from 101 MS and 21 non-MS postmortem brains for EBV using PCR, EBER in situ hybridization (EBER-ISH), qPCR and immunohistochemistry. EBV was detected in 91/101 (90%) of MS cases versus 5/21 (24%) of non-MS cases, while HSV-1, CMV and HHV-6 were absent, indicating selective EBV presence. EBV viral load was generally low to moderate, but 18/101 cases were heavily infected; the latent protein EBNA1 (14/18 cases) and to a lesser extent the lytic protein BZLF1 (3/18) were expressed. Double staining showed EBV-infected cells included not only CD20+ B cells but also GFAP+ astrocytes (11/18) and Iba1+ microglia (7/18), supporting a role for transcriptionally active EBV in MS pathogenesis beyond B cells.

Hassani et al 2021 Front Immunol.body: Using a rabbit model in which intravenous EBV inoculation establishes persistent latent infection mimicking human infection, Hassani et al show that primary peripheral EBV infection can traverse to the CNS and cause neuroinflammation. Cell-associated (PBMC/splenic) virus, but not free plasma virus, correlated with brain infection; infected brain cells were IgG+/IgM+ B lymphocytes. EBV (but not PBS) induced inflammatory cellular aggregates of central macrophages surrounded by reactive astrocytes and B/T lymphocytes that were devoid of myelin; aggregate incidence increased with cyclosporin A immunosuppression and peaked at 14-21 dpi alongside peak viral load. Peripheral infection drove temporal upregulation of brain EBV latent transcripts (EBER1/2, EBNA1) and proinflammatory cytokines (IL6, IL2, IL1beta, TNFalpha), with EBER expression strongly correlating with cytokine expression.

Hay et al 2000 Mult Scler.body: Hay and Tenser used PCR to detect HHV-6 (major capsid protein gene) and EBV (LMP1 gene) DNA in peripheral blood mononuclear leukocytes (PBL) of 29 clinically definite MS patients (17 relapsing-remitting, 12 secondary progressive) and 7 normal controls. EBV DNA was detected in 100% of both MS patients and controls, while HHV-6 DNA was detected in only 7% (2/29) of MS patients and 14% (1/7) of controls. The authors conclude their results and other investigations do not show an association between HHV-6 in PBL and MS, and that the ubiquitous EBV detection does not permit specific conclusions about an EBV role in MS.

Hayashi et al 2026 Nat Immunol.body: A paired single-cell RNA-sequencing and TCR-sequencing study of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and blood from 18 individuals (13 MS/CIS, 5 control) identified 33 highly expanded, CSF-enriched T cell clonotypes, more than 70% of which were CD8+ T cells with a cytotoxic, tissue-resident-memory phenotype. Using unbiased pMHC yeast display and targeted TCR-database antigen discovery, three highly expanded CSF-enriched CD8+ T cell clonotypes from patients with MS were validated as reactive to EBV antigens (EBNA3A 193-201/FLRGRAYGL on HLA-B*08:01 and BZLF1 54-64/EPLPQGQLTAY on HLA-B*35:01), and a fourth (MS27) reacted to EBV-transformed B cells via HLA-A*29:02. EBV DNA was detected in CSF of 6/13 MS/CIS and 2/5 control samples, and EBV BamHI-W transcripts were significantly increased in the MS/CIS CSF (P=0.0227), supporting that EBV reactivation and EBV-specific CD8+ T cell expansion are uniquely enhanced in the CSF in MS.

Hedström et al 2014 Eur J Neurol.body: Two Swedish population-based case-control studies (EIMS, 1780 incident cases/3885 controls; GEMS, 4502 prevalent cases/4039 controls) tested whether adolescent obesity (BMI > 27 kg/m2) interacts with past infectious mononucleosis (IM) in multiple sclerosis risk. A substantial synergistic interaction was found, most pronounced for IM after age 10: subjects with both exposures had an MS odds ratio of 14.7 (EIMS) and 9.3 (GEMS) versus those with neither, with attributable proportion due to interaction ~0.7-0.8. The interaction persisted regardless of HLA-DRB1*15 status. The authors propose obesity-driven chronic inflammation plus altered immune response to EBV/IM as a mechanism, and suggest preventing adolescent obesity as an MS prevention strategy.
Hedström et al 2014 Eur J Neurol.identifier: Hedström et al 2014 Eur J Neurol

Hedström et al 2019 Front Neurol.body: Two Swedish population-based case-control studies (EIMS and GEMS; 5,316 MS cases and 5,431 controls) tested whether elevated anti-EBNA-1 antibody levels and a history of infectious mononucleosis (IM) are separate EBV-related risk factors for multiple sclerosis and whether they interact with MS-associated HLA alleles. Both aspects acted mainly directly on MS risk (anti-EBNA-1 direct effect OR 2.8; IM direct effect OR 1.7), showed significant synergistic interaction (RERI 1.2, ~50% of the total effect), and each interacted with DRB1*15:01 and absence of A*02:01, with the highest-risk combination reaching OR 27.1.

Hedström et al 2020 J Neurol Neurosurg P.body: Two Swedish population-based case-control studies (EIMS and GEMS; 7520 relapsing-onset MS cases, 540 progressive-onset MS cases, 11 386 controls) assessing whether environmental/lifestyle risk factors and their interaction with HLA-DRB1*15:01 differ between relapsing-onset and progressive-onset MS. Smoking, obesity and high anti-EBNA-1 antibody levels increased risk of both phenotypes, while snuff use, alcohol consumption and sun exposure reduced risk; high EBNA-1 antibody levels gave OR 3.0 (relapsing-onset) and OR 2.0 (progressive-onset). Additive interactions between DRB1*15:01 and smoking, obesity, EBNA-1 antibody levels and sun exposure increased MS risk in both phenotypes, supporting shared underlying disease mechanisms across MS clinical courses.
Hedström et al 2020 J Neurol Neurosurg P.identifier: Hedström et al 2020 J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry

Hedström et al 2020 Sci Rep.body: Two pooled Swedish population-based case-control studies (EIMS and GEMS; 6,340 MS cases and 6,219 matched controls) investigating whether smoking interacts with aspects of EBV infection (elevated anti-EBNA-1 IgG and infectious mononucleosis history) to influence MS risk. Current and past smokers had higher EBNA-1 IgG levels than never smokers (p<0.0001). A significant additive interaction (synergy) was found between current smoking and high EBNA-1 IgG (AP 0.3) and between current smoking and IM history (AP 0.2), but no interaction was found for past smoking with either EBV aspect, indicating current smoking increases EBNA-1 antibody levels and acts synergistically with both aspects of EBV infection to raise MS risk.

Hedström et al 2021 Eur J Neurol.body: Population-based case-control study (Swedish EIMS cohort; 2017 incident MS cases, 2443 matched controls) testing whether sun exposure/vitamin D moderates the role of EBV (EBNA-1 antibody levels) in MS etiology. Low sun exposure (OR 1.4) and high EBNA-1 antibody levels (OR ~3.0) each increased MS risk, and the two acted synergistically on the additive scale (combined OR 4.3 vs reference; attributable proportion due to interaction AP 0.2, 95% CI 0.03-0.3). The interaction persisted regardless of HLA-DRB1*15:01 status, suggesting low sun exposure may reinforce EBV-related adaptive immune mechanisms in MS risk.

Hilton et al 1994 J Neurol Neurosurg Psy.body: Short report testing whether Epstein-Barr virus is present in multiple sclerosis brain tissue. EBV-encoded EBER 1/2 RNA was sought by in situ hybridisation in the brains of 10 MS patients (21 plaques: acute, chronic active, chronic inactive, and shadow plaques). Mitochondrial rRNA control probes confirmed RNA preservation in all cases and a Hodgkin's lymph node positive control was strongly positive, yet no EBV RNA signal was detected in any MS plaque. The authors conclude persistent or latent EBV infection of the CNS is unlikely in MS, though a role for EBV in disease initiation is not excluded.

Holden et al 2018 Mult Scler Relat Disor.body: Holden et al. used real-time quantitative PCR (qPCR) to measure EBV DNA levels in saliva across three separate relapsing MS patient cohorts (INSPIRE, ExIMS, MEAVIS), defining EBV shedding as >5.8 copies/uL. The frequency of EBV shedding was similar across cohorts (20-25% of subjects releasing virus on any given date). Salivary EBV levels varied markedly within individuals over short periods (26% of subjects showed >10-fold diurnal variation), and shedding at one time point did not predict shedding later, so MS subjects could not be divided into stable shedders vs non-shedders. The assay is proposed as a tool for assessing salivary gland EBV lytic activity, e.g. in trials of antiviral drugs in MS.

Holmøy et al 2004 J Neurovirol.body: Short communication reporting that IL-2-expanded CD4+ T-cell lines from the cerebrospinal fluid of six of six multiple sclerosis (MS) patients (and four of six patients with other neurological diseases) proliferated in response to autologous Epstein-Barr virus-transformed B-cell lines (EBV-LCLs). The CSF T-cell responses were predominantly HLA-DR restricted and could not be reproduced by CD40-activated autologous B cells, αB-crystallin, or myelin basic protein, indicating the responses are likely directed against a viral epitope rather than these autoantigens. The authors conclude that EBV-specific CD4+ T cells gaining access to the intrathecal compartment could contribute to MS pathogenesis by activating or expanding autoreactive T cells.

Holmøy et al 2004 J Neurovirol [855596].body: Holmøy, Kvale and Vartdal report that CD4+ T cells specific for the Epstein-Barr virus DNA polymerase peptide EBV 627-641 were present in the cerebrospinal fluid of one of two multiple sclerosis patients (MS1), and that 8 of 14 EBV 627-641-specific T-cell clones derived from CSF cross-recognized the immunodominant myelin basic protein peptide MBP 85-99. The proportion of EBV 627-641-specific CD4+ T cells appeared higher in CSF (>1/10 000) than in blood (~1/100 000), proving such cells gain access to the intrathecal compartment. The cross-reactive clones produced large amounts of IFN-gamma (Th1/Th0 phenotype) and showed HLA-DR and HLA-DP restriction, supporting a molecular-mimicry pathogenetic role for EBV-specific CD4+ T cells in MS.

Houen et al 2020 J Neuroimmunol.body: Houen et al. investigated whether the diagnostic MRZ antibody-index panel (Measles, Mumps, Varicella Zoster) could be extended to an EMMRZ panel (adding Epstein-Barr virus EBNA1 and Rubella) to improve diagnosis of relapsing-remitting MS (RRMS) and optic neuritis (ON). Serum and CSF from RRMS and ON patients and controls were tested by ELISA for IgG/IgM against viral antigens. RRMS patients showed significantly increased IgG to EBV EBNA1, VZV lysate, MeV NuP and MuV NuP in serum and CSF, with strong serum-CSF correlations and high intrathecal antibody indices (EBNA1 AI positive in 100% of RRMS and 96% of ON; MeV AI positive in >82%). The EMMRZ panel raised sensitivity ~40% over MRZ, and combining EMMRZ with oligoclonal bands reached 100% sensitivity in RRMS, supporting an important role of EBV in MS and ON etiology.

Huang et al 2024 Brain.body: A large Swedish case-control study (8744 MS cases, 7229 controls) measuring plasma IgG against EBNA-1 (truncated aa325-641 and peptide aa385-420) and viral capsid antigen VCAp18 by multiplex serology, cross-evaluating EBV serology and infectious mononucleosis (IM) history with MS risk and host genetics. Higher anti-EBNA-1 (especially the aa385-420 peptide, OR up to ~12x) and anti-VCAp18 IgG levels were associated with increased MS risk; HLA haplotypes (notably DRB1*15:01 and DRB1*03:01) were the primary genetic determinants of EBV antibody levels and overlapped with MS risk alleles. No non-HLA variants reached genome-wide significance. IM history was not associated with class II HLA but was negatively associated with the MS-protective HLA-A*02:01 allele, supporting independent roles of EBNA-1 serology and IM in MS susceptibility.

Hvalkof et al 2025 Clin Immunol.body: Exploratory study measuring EBV-encoded microRNAs in CSF exosomes (by qPCR) across 50 treatment-naive relapsing-remitting MS, 24 CIS, 45 symptomatic controls, 24 natalizumab-treated and 15 anti-CD20 antibody-treated pwRRMS. Of 43 screened EBV miRNAs, only ebv-miR-BART19-3p and ebv-miR-BART13-5p were reliably measured. ebv-miR-BART19-3p was lower in treatment-naive pwRRMS than controls but higher in natalizumab-treated pwRRMS, correlated positively with MS disease severity (ARMSS/EDSS) and with natalizumab treatment duration, and correlated negatively with CSF sBCMA, sCD27 and ZO-1 in natalizumab-treated pwRRMS. Plasma anti-EBNA1 antibody titers were higher in pwRRMS and natalizumab-treated pwRRMS; ebv-miR-BART13-5p was elevated in CIS that converted to MS.

Höllsberg et al 2003 Clin Exp Immunol.body: Case-control immunological study comparing CD8+ T cell responses to immunodominant EBV, HCMV and measles virus peptides between 33 multiple sclerosis (MS) patients and 33 healthy controls using an IFN-gamma ELISpot assay. MS patients showed a significantly increased frequency of CD8+ T cells responding to the EBV epitopes HLA-A2/CLG (from LMP2, P=0.02-0.03) and HLA-B7/RPP (from EBNA3A, P=0.05), but responses to most other EBV peptides and to HCMV epitopes did not differ. All MS patients were EBNA1 seropositive. The authors propose the altered, epitope-selective response is consistent with cross-reactive (molecularly mimicking) epitopes, potentially including self/myelin antigens.

Höllsberg et al 2005 Acta Neurol Scand.body: A nested virological analysis of 33 Danish active RRMS patients from a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled valacyclovir trial, using real-time PCR after ultracentrifugation to detect EBV and HHV-6B DNA in saliva and plasma. Valacyclovir significantly reduced EBV (but not HHV-6B) DNA in saliva (9% vs 41%, P=0.000017), with EBV saliva positivity disappearing after 20 weeks, whereas plasma EBV and HHV-6B DNA levels were unchanged by treatment and not different from healthy controls. Patients with high disease activity had significantly more EBV-positive (P=0.018) and HHV-6B-positive (P=0.023) plasma samples, and EBV and HHV-6B co-expression in plasma was strongly correlated (P<0.00000001) but independent in saliva (P=0.41), consistent with an underlying immunologic defect in MS.

Ingelfinger et al 2024 Med.body: Reanalysis of mass cytometry data from 57 monozygotic twin pairs discordant for multiple sclerosis (MS), with CITE-seq, in vitro B-cell culture, and CSF/serum ELISA validation. The frequency of circulating class-switched CXCR3+ memory B cells is reduced in twins with MS and is the only subset altered in untreated twin pairs, identifying it as a non-heritable disease feature. CXCR3+ memory B cells over-express IFI30/HLA, IGHG1 and TBX21 (T-bet), preferentially differentiate into antibody-secreting cells in vitro, and their reduction is reversed by natalizumab; the CXCR3 ligand CXCL10 is elevated in MS CSF versus serum, supporting CNS homing. The authors propose environmental cues such as Epstein-Barr virus drive these B cells.

Ingram et al 2010 Eur J Neurol.body: A case-control study of 100 subjects (25 PPMS, 25 stable RRMS, 25 active RRMS in acute relapse, 25 controls) assessing serum anti-EBNA-1 IgG by two assays (Liaison chemiluminescent and Biotest ELISA) as a potential biomarker of MS clinical disease activity. The authors confirmed higher anti-EBNA-1 IgG and EBV seropositivity in MS patients versus controls but found no difference between MS disease subgroups and no correlation with clinical phenotype (age at onset, disease duration, EDSS, MSSS). They conclude anti-EBNA-1 IgG is not a reliable marker of MS clinical disease activity and could not confirm the previously reported association with disease course/activity.
Ingram et al 2010 Eur J Neurol.identifier: Ingram et al 2010 Eur J Neurol

Ingvarsson et al 2024 Eur J Neurol.body: Nested case-control study of 670 pre-MS cases and 670 matched controls from a Swedish biobank, measuring serological responses to rubella virus (RV) E1 and other neurotropic viruses with a bead-based multiplex assay before MS onset. RV E1 seropositivity was associated with increased MS risk in unvaccinated subjects even after adjusting for EBV, CMV, HHV-6A and vitamin D (adjusted OR=4.0, 95% CI 1.8-8.8), and cases had higher anti-RV E1 antibody reactivity than controls; no such associations were seen for HSV1, HSV2 or VZV. The authors propose molecular mimicry between a rubella E2 epitope and MOG as a possible mechanism, broadening the virus hypothesis in MS aetiology.

Ioannides et al 2021 Front Neurol.body: Open-label phase I follow-up study (n=10 progressive MS patients) assessing longer-term outcomes 2 and 3 years after autologous EBV-specific CD8+ T cell therapy (AdE1-LMPpoly-expanded, targeting EBNA1, LMP1, LMP2A). No serious treatment-related adverse events occurred. Four participants had some sustained clinical improvement at year 2 and three at year 3, including reduced fatigue and reduced EDSS. More sustained improvement was associated with higher EBV-specific CD8+ T cell reactivity (>5%) in the administered T cell product; all sustained responders had received strong-reactivity products, and the strongest responder (participant 5, 45.45% reactivity) had the greatest year-3 benefit.
