Jafari et al 2010 J Clin Virol.body: Case-control study of paired serum and CSF from MS patients and non-inflammatory neurological disease (NIND) controls examining the anti-EBV IgG response, mapping EBNA-1 B-cell epitopes, and testing for intrathecal EBNA-1-specific IgG synthesis. The overall anti-EBV antibody repertoire was similar between MS and controls, but IgG reactivity to the immunodominant EBNA-1 region (residues 394-451, EBNA-1^394-451) was significantly increased in MS serum and CSF (p<0.0001). After normalizing CSF anti-EBNA-1^394-451 IgG for total IgG, the disease association disappeared and serum/CSF levels correlated, indicating the elevated CSF levels reflect blood-brain barrier dysfunction rather than intrathecal synthesis. The authors conclude there is no evidence for intrathecal EBNA-1-specific IgG synthesis in MS.
Jafari et al 2010 J Clin Virol.identifier: Jafari et al 2010 J Clin Virol

Jakhmola et al 2022 Comput Biol Med.body: An in-silico molecular mimicry study analyzing antigenic epitopes within four human myelin sheath proteins (MBP, PLP1, MAG, MOG) and their sequence similarity to Herpesviridae proteins (EBV/HHV-4, CMV, HHV-6, HHV-8). Using SVMTrip/EMBOSS epitope prediction, BLASTp homology search, NetMHCpan MHC I/II binding prediction, HPEPDOCK peptide-protein docking, and conventional plus Gaussian accelerated molecular dynamics with MM/GBSA, the authors found that myelin epitopes mimic EBV antigens (EBNA1, LMP2B, gp350/220), CMV gM/gB, and HHV-6 proteins. Specific HLA alleles (HLA-B*57:01, HLA-B*51:01, HLA-A*68:02, HLA-DRB1*04:05, HLA-DR1*01:01) bound myelin peptides with high affinity, supporting molecular mimicry and these MHC alleles as contributing MS risk factors.
Jakhmola et al 2022 Comput Biol Med.identifier: Jakhmola et al 2022 Comput Biol Med

Jakimovski et al 2019 Mult Scler.body: A case-controlled magnetization transfer ratio (MTR) study of 101 MS patients (69 RRMS, 32 SPMS) and 41 healthy controls evaluating associations between EBV-specific humoral response (serum anti-EBNA-1 IgG titer by ELISA) and brain myelin content measured by in vivo MTI. MS patients had ~4-fold higher anti-EBNA-1 titer than HCs (median 107.9 vs 27.8 U/mL, p<0.001). Higher anti-EBNA-1 titer was associated with lower T1-lesion MTR in the total MS group (r=-0.287, p=0.035) and, more strongly, in RRMS (T1-lesion MTR r=-0.524, p=0.001; NAGM MTR r=-0.308, p=0.043), but not in SPMS or HCs. The authors conclude that greater EBV humoral response is associated with lower gray-matter MTR and more severe focal destructive lesion pathology in RRMS.

Jilek et al 2008 Brain.body: Jilek et al. studied EBV- and CMV-specific cellular (proliferation, ELISPOT) and humoral (anti-EBV/CMV antibody) immune responses in 164 subjects (108 MS patients at different stages, 35 with other neurological diseases, 21 healthy controls). EBV infection rate was 99% versus 51% for CMV. Patients with clinically isolated syndrome (CIS, early MS) had a significantly higher frequency of IFN-gamma secreting EBV-specific CD8+ T cells than all other groups; this response was inversely correlated with time since MS onset and declined over 1 year of follow-up. No such pattern was seen for EBV-specific CD4+ T cells or for CMV-specific responses. Anti-EBNA-1 IgG correlated moderately with EBV-specific CD8+ T cells in inflammatory MS. The data support EBV being associated with the onset (trigger) of MS but not with CMV.

Jilek et al 2026 J Immunol.body: Case-control immunological study (Lausanne, 439 HLA-typed subjects; 220 EBV/CMV-typed) testing whether EBV-specific CD8+ T cells are intrinsically dysregulated in multiple sclerosis. Using HLA-A2/B7/B8 viral peptide tetramers, the authors confirm HLA-B7 is more prevalent and HLA-A2 less prevalent in MS patients, and find that HLA-B7/EBV_RPP (EBNA-3A)-specific CD8+ T cells are more prevalent yet functionally dysregulated in MS: lower IFN-gamma and IL-2 production, lower perforin and granzyme B, and reduced cytotoxicity that decreases with disease duration. The cytotoxic/granule deficits are rescued by exogenous rhIL-2, and no increase in EBV DNA load was detected, pointing to a suboptimal HLA-B7-restricted viral epitope presentation rather than overt EBV-specific T-cell deficiency.

Jog et al 2019 J Autoimmun.body: This study used solid-phase epitope mapping to characterize the fine specificity of the anti-EBNA-1 humoral response in multiple sclerosis (MS) patients. MS patients had significantly higher anti-EBNA-1 IgG than controls (no difference for VCA, CMV, HSV-1, HSV-2, or CMV-IE epitope profiles), and uniquely recognized an EBNA-1 epitope spanning amino acids 411-426 (EBNA411-426, EADYFEYHQEGGPDGE) not bound by controls or IFN-beta-treated patients. Affinity-purified anti-EBNA411-426 antibodies cross-reacted with myelin basic protein (MBP) epitopes (MBP aa 205-224). Immunizing SJL and Balb/c mice with EBNA411-426 induced anti-MBP IFN-gamma responses, EAE-like clinical signs, rotarod impairment, and cortical brain lesions, supporting EBV-MS linkage via EBNA-1/MBP molecular mimicry.

Johansson et al 2025 Eur J Epidemiol.body: A Swedish population-based case-control study (EIMS; 3128 MS cases, 5986 controls) investigating whether a history of infectious mononucleosis (IM), used as a proxy for inadequate EBV control, interacts on the additive scale with modifiable lifestyle risk factors for multiple sclerosis. A history of IM was associated with MS (OR 1.86, 95% CI 1.63-2.12). Synergistic (additive) interactions were observed between IM and passive smoking, low alcohol consumption, low fish consumption, low vitamin D, short adolescent sleep duration, and low sleep quality, with attributable proportions due to interaction (AP) ranging 0.20-0.35. The authors interpret the findings as supporting EBV as a crucial factor in MS whose effect is amplified by factors impairing viral immune control.
Johansson et al 2025 Eur J Epidemiol.identifier: Johansson et al 2025 Eur J Epidemiol

Jons et al 2021 Mult Scler Relat Disord.body: Prospective follow-up cohort study comparing antibody reactivity against single-protein viral antigens in 42 individuals sampled during acute infectious mononucleosis (IM, 2003-2007) and again ~10 years later (FU), versus EBV-seropositive healthy controls and 22 persons with MS. Anti-gp350 IgG was robustly increased at FU and persisted more than a decade after IM (higher than controls, p=0.007), reminiscent of the elevated anti-EBV reactivity of presymptomatic MS, while EBNA1 and VCA IgG did not distinguish the groups. Acute IM was associated with heightened anti-measles (Ncore) and anti-VZV (VZVgE) IgG (MRZ-like polyspecific reaction), with measles reactivity persisting at the limit of significance after a decade. In MS samples, serum anti-gp350 and anti-Ncore IgG (and CSF anti-Ncore, anti-VZVgE) were elevated versus controls.
Jons et al 2021 Mult Scler Relat Disord.identifier: Jons et al 2021 Mult Scler Relat Disord

Jørgensen et al 2012 PLoS One.body: Case-control immunology study comparing HLA-E expression and the frequency of CD8+ cells recognizing HLA-E tetramers presenting either an HLA-A2 leader peptide (HLA-E/A2) or an EBV BZLF1_39-47 peptide (HLA-E/BZLF1) in relapsing-remitting (MS-RR) and primary progressive (MS-PP) multiple sclerosis patients versus healthy controls. EBV and IFN-alpha/IFN-gamma upregulated HLA-E on CD4+ cells; only MS-PP had increased resting CD4+ HLA-E. MS-RR patients had fewer CD8-dim cells but expanded CD8-bright cells recognizing HLA-E/BZLF1, which was predominantly recognized by CD8-bright T cells (CD94-independent), whereas HLA-E/A2 was predominantly recognized by CD8-negative NK cells in a CD94-dependent manner.

Keane et al 2021 EBioMedicine.body: Keane et al. used allele-specific ChIP-PCR and a peptide inhibitor of EBNA2 (EBNA2-TAT) in EBV-infected lymphoblastoid cell lines (LCLs) to test whether the EBV transcription factor EBNA2 binds and regulates six MS risk loci in an allele-dependent manner. EBNA2 bound dependent on the MS risk allele at five of six loci (preferring the risk allele at TRAF3/RCOR1 and CD40, and the protective allele at TNFAIP8, TNFRSF1A and TBX6). EBNA2-TAT inhibition significantly altered expression of TRAF3, CD40, CLECL1, TNFAIP8 and TNFRSF1A, reduced LCL proliferation and the EBV gene LMP1, and ablated a TNFAIP8-genotype effect on EBV DNA copy number. The findings support EBNA2 driving the association of these risk loci with MS by enhancing EBV latency III survival/immune evasion, and propose EBNA2/EBV as therapeutic targets in MS.

Keane et al 2021 Front Immunol.body: Keane et al. investigated whether sex and the sex hormone estradiol affect MS risk gene expression and EBV latency III traits in Epstein-Barr virus-infected B cells (lymphoblastoid cell lines, LCLs). Using GEUVADIS eQTL data they found many MS risk SNP eQTLs in LCLs are gender-biased and that Estrogen Receptor 2 (ESR2) expression correlates with EBV latency III traits (EBNA2, LMP1, EBV DNA copy number) differently in males and females. Culturing LCLs in serum-free medium and supplementing with 100 nM estradiol showed that estradiol altered MS risk gene expression, LCL proliferation, EBV DNA copy number and EBNA2 expression in a sex-dependent manner, suggesting estrogen-mediated gender-specific differences in host response to EBV that may contribute to female MS susceptibility.

Krone et al 2008 Mult Scler.body: Case-control study of 152 German children with multiple sclerosis (onset <16 years) and sex- and age-matched controls, measuring IgG (and IgM for Chlamydia pneumoniae) antibody to ~10 common infectious agents by ELISA, immunofluorescence and haemagglutination inhibition. IgG antibody concentrations were significantly elevated in MS patients for influenza A, measles, parainfluenza 2, varicella and (lysate-antigen) HSV-2, while recombinant gG2 testing showed almost no true HSV-2 infection; Chlamydia pneumoniae IgM prevalence was significantly higher in patients (28.9% vs 2.0%). No significant differences were found for adenovirus, HHV-6, HSV-1, mumps or rubella. The authors emphasize a complex infectious/immunologic background of MS rather than a single causative pathogen, building on prior work showing near-universal remote EBV infection in paediatric MS.

Kvistad et al 2014 Mult Scler.body: A prospective sub-study of the Norwegian OFAMS cohort (87 RRMS patients) followed for two years before and during interferon beta (IFNB) treatment, with paired MRI scans and serum EBV antibody measurements (IgG to VCA, EBNA-1, EA and IgM to VCA). Higher anti-EBNA-1 IgG levels were associated with increased MRI activity (combined unique activity, CUA), OR = 2.95 (95% CI 1.07-8.10; p = 0.036), while anti-VCA IgM levels showed an inverse association with CUA, particularly during IFNB treatment, OR = 0.32 (95% CI 0.12-0.84; p = 0.021). Anti-EA IgG and anti-VCA IgG were not associated with MRI activity, and neither anti-EBNA-1 IgG nor anti-VCA IgM was associated with relapses or EDSS progression. All 87 patients were EBV seropositive.

Kyllesbech et al 2022 J Neuroimmunol.body: Case-control study (26 RRMS patients vs 15 healthy controls) measuring serum and CSF IgG by ELISA against a panel of viral antigens: EBV EBNA1 (latent) and BARF1 (lytic), CMV pp52, measles virus (MeV) nucleoprotein, mumps virus (MuV) nucleoprotein, and rubella virus (RuV) capsid protein. CSF IgG to EBV EBNA1, RuV CaP and MeV NuP and serum IgG to RuV CaP were significantly elevated in MS, while CMV pp52 serum IgG was higher in HCs. Antibody indices (intrathecal synthesis) were significantly elevated in MS for EBV EBNA1, EBV BARF1, MeV NuP, MuV NuP and RuV CaP but not CMV. The optimized antigen panel achieved 81% sensitivity and 86% specificity (89% sensitivity when combined with oligoclonal band status), supporting a pivotal role for EBV in MS and a possible protective role for CMV, and demonstrating that virus-specific antibody indices may supplement the total IgG index in MS diagnosis.

Lang et al 2002 Nat Immunol.body: Lang et al. show that a single T-cell receptor (Hy.2E11) cloned from a relapsing-remitting MS patient cross-reacts with the immunodominant myelin basic protein peptide MBP(85-99) presented by HLA-DRB1*1501 and an Epstein-Barr virus DNA polymerase peptide EBV(627-641) presented by HLA-DRB5*0101. The crystal structure of the soluble DRB5*0101-EBV peptide complex (PDB 1H15, 3.1 A) reveals marked structural equivalence to the DRB1*1501-MBP complex over the TCR footprint, with four identical solvent-exposed peptide side chains (P-1 Val, P2 His, P3 Phe, P5 Lys). This provides direct structural evidence for HLA class II-based molecular mimicry between EBV and a CNS autoantigen, offering a mechanism by which EBV could trigger MS-like autoimmunity and an explanation for the predominance of MHC class II associations in autoimmune disease.

Langelaar et al 2020 Eur J Immunol.body: Short communication examining how EBV persistence in B cells influences CXCR3+ memory B-cell and plasma-cell development in multiple sclerosis, using two cohorts. Ex vivo, in nine MS patients after autologous bone marrow transplantation (BMT), high EBV DNA load in class-switched memory B cells positively correlated with CXCR3+ (but not CXCR4+ or CXCR5+) fractions, peaking at 3-7 months post-BMT. In vitro, CD27+ memory B cells from natalizumab-treated MS patients with high EBV load preferentially differentiated into CXCR3+ plasma cells secreting anti-EBNA1 IgG under IL-21/CD40L/IFN-gamma (GC-like) conditions. The authors conclude EBV persistence potentiates brain-homing, antibody-producing CXCR3+ B-cell subsets in MS.
Langelaar et al 2020 Eur J Immunol.identifier: Langelaar et al 2020 Eur J Immunol

Langer-Gould et al 2017 Neurology.body: Multiethnic incident case-control study (MS Sunshine Study, Kaiser Permanente Southern California) of MS/CIS in blacks, Hispanics, and whites testing whether EBV (EBNA-1) or CMV seropositivity is associated with MS and whether hygiene-hypothesis markers or breastfeeding explain the findings. EBNA-1 seropositivity and a history of infectious mononucleosis were independently associated with increased MS/CIS risk consistently across all three racial/ethnic groups, supporting a strong biological EBV-MS link. CMV seropositivity was associated with lower MS/CIS risk only in Hispanics (not blacks or whites), which the authors interpret as a likely noncausal association. An additive (not multiplicative) interaction between EBNA-1 seropositivity and HLA-DRB1*15:01/*15:03 carrier status was detected in blacks.

stats.qualifier: MS/CIS in blacks, Hispanics, and whites

Lanz et al 2022 Nature.body: Lanz et al. (Nature 2022) identify high-affinity molecular mimicry between the EBV nuclear antigen EBNA1 and the CNS protein GlialCAM (encoded by HEPACAM). A CSF-derived clonally expanded MS B-cell antibody (MS39p2w174, IGHV3-7) binds the MS-associated EBNA1 epitope AA386-405 and cross-reacts with GlialCAM; the crystal structure (PDB 7K7R) and bio-layer interferometry show cross-reactivity is enabled by phosphorylation of GlialCAM at Ser376. Anti-EBNA1 and anti-GlialCAM antibodies are elevated in MS plasma (20-25% cross-reactive), and EBNA1 immunization of EAE mice generates anti-GlialCAM antibodies and exacerbates demyelinating disease, providing a mechanistic link between EBV and MS.

Latham et al 2015 Acta Neurol Scand.body: Prospective longitudinal study of 20 subjects with early active relapsing-remitting MS, followed 16 weeks with blood/saliva every 2 weeks and brain MRI every 4 weeks, testing whether antiviral immune activity (proliferation, IFN-gamma ELISPOT) and viral DNA reactivation precede MRI disease activity. The proliferative response to autologous EBV-infected lymphoblastoid cell lines (LCL) was most significantly and positively correlated with the number of gadolinium-enhancing and combined-unique-active (CUA) lesions 4 and 8 weeks later, and IFN-gamma-secreting cells responding to LCL correlated with enhancing lesions 8 weeks later. The increased antiviral immunity was directed primarily against EBV (not tetanus, VZV, or mitogens), supporting a possible causal role for EBV reactivation in driving MS disease activity.
Latham et al 2015 Acta Neurol Scand.identifier: Latham et al 2015 Acta Neurol Scand

Lehikoinen et al 2024 Neurol Neuroimmuno.body: A case-control study of 45 EBV-seropositive patients with MS and 45 HLA-DRB1*15:01-matched seropositive controls examined EBV DNA in CSF supernatant, CSF cells, and blood CD19+ B cells using highly sensitive droplet digital PCR (ddPCR), plus RNA NGS of blood lymphocyte subsets. EBV DNA was rarely found in CSF supernatant (1/45 MS, 0/45 controls) but was detectable in CSF cellular DNA of a cumulative 64% of MS and 54% of controls (p=0.59), reaching 59% overall across repeated ddPCRs, with no significant difference between groups. The inferred prevalence of EBV-positive B cells (>1/10,000) was higher than previously estimated in both CSF and blood. No EBV or other viral RNA was detected in blood CD4+, CD8+, or CD19+ cells, only endogenous retroviral (HERV-W) transcripts.
Lehikoinen et al 2024 Neurol Neuroimmuno.identifier: Lehikoinen et al 2024 Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm

Lehikoinen et al 2026 NAR Mol Med.body: Lehikoinen et al. developed an ex vivo 6-day PBMC culture method (TPA + cyclosporin-A stimulation) to reactivate and enrich endogenous wild-type EBV DNA into supernatant, then performed RNA-bait-capture NGS to recover near-complete EBV genomes from 9 MS patients (average coverage 97%) and 4 controls (85%). They identified 1088 single-nucleotide variants (355 nonsynonymous) outside repeat regions; EBNA-3B/3C and EBNA1 carried the highest missense burden. No statistically significant overall difference in variant number between MS and controls survived coverage adjustment, but several variants were MS-exclusive (e.g. multiplex-PCR-tested SNVs near EBNA1, including 94289:G>T predicted to create a CTCF binding site near latency III promoters), and in silico analysis showed EBNA1 cross-reactive-region missense variants altered HLA class I/II peptide binding (e.g. A439T increased class II binding, V429M and P476Q decreased it).
Lehikoinen et al 2026 NAR Mol Med.identifier: Lehikoinen et al 2026 NAR Mol Med

Leibovitch et al 2018 Mult Scler.body: Retrospective cross-sectional study comparing salivary herpesvirus (EBV and HHV-6) shedding in 32 pediatric MS patients versus 42 age-matched controls (with adult cohorts for comparison), using droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) for EBV lmp-1 and HHV-6 u57. Pediatric MS patients did not differ from controls in frequency or magnitude of salivary EBV or HHV-6 shedding, and EBV seropositivity also did not differ between cohorts. Low-amplitude (mutated) EBV lmp-1 probe-binding region variants were absent in EBV-positive pediatric MS patients (0/8) but present in pediatric controls (5/12, 42%) and common in adults, suggesting differential host-immune control of EBV in this pediatric MS cohort.

Levin et al 2005 JAMA.body: Nested case-control study within the US Department of Defense Serum Repository (>3 million military personnel) testing whether anti-EBV antibody titers are elevated before MS onset. Among 83 MS cases and 166 matched controls with serial prediagnostic sera, serum IgG to EBNA complex and EBNA-1 were the strongest predictors of MS: titers rose 2-3 fold in cases (not controls) in early adulthood (age >=25), the RR for the highest vs lowest EBNA complex titer category was 9.4 (and up to 35.9 vs the lowest reference), and a within-person 4-fold rise in EBNA complex/EBNA-1 titers carried RR ~3 (RR up to 18 in those first sampled at age <=20). No association was found for CMV antibodies. The findings support an age-dependent role of EBV as a risk factor preceding MS onset.

Levin et al 2010 Ann Neurol.body: Nested case-control study within the US military Department of Defense Serum Repository (305 incident MS cases, 610 matched controls) using serial prediagnostic serum samples to time EBV infection relative to MS onset. Only 10 cases (3.3%) and 32 controls (5.2%) were EBV seronegative at baseline; all 10 seronegative cases seroconverted to EBV positive before MS onset, whereas only 10 of 28 seronegative controls seroconverted (exact p=0.0008). No incident MS occurred in EBV-negative individuals, so the relative risk of MS following EBV infection tends toward infinity. CMV, used as a control herpesvirus, showed no association with MS risk.

Lindsey et al 2008 Mult Scler.body: Lindsey et al. used real-time quantitative PCR to measure EBV DNA (BamHIW repeat, LMP2a gene) and EBV RNA (EBER2, BZLF1, BALF5, BLLF1) in peripheral blood leukocytes of 91 stable RRMS patients and 74 controls. EBV DNA and EBER2 RNA were frequently detectable in both groups with no significant difference between MS and controls, and lytic transcripts were largely absent, indicating latent infection under effective immune control. In a small set of paired stable-versus-relapse samples, BamHIW DNA tended to rise before and during clinical relapse, suggesting EBV reactivation may correlate with MS disease activity.

Lindsey et al 2010 Eur J Neurol.body: Case-control study (80 MS patients, 80 matched controls, plus 19 RRMS patients with paired relapse/stable samples) measuring anti-EBV humoral responses by quantitative ELISA. Anti-EBNA-1 IgG was significantly higher in MS (index 23.3 vs 16.3, P=0.007) and EA IgA was modestly increased (median 1.964 vs 1.248, P=0.029), whereas EA IgG and EBV neutralizing antibodies (NeutAb, measured by a 72A1 competitive ELISA against gp350) did not differ between MS and controls. No antibody level changed in relapse; individual antibody patterns remained stable over time and correlations between antibody specificities were minimal.
Lindsey et al 2010 Eur J Neurol.identifier: Lindsey et al 2010 Eur J Neurol

Lindsey et al 2010 J Neuroimmunol.body: Lindsey and Hatfield investigated T-cell immunity to Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) in 20 relapsing-remitting MS patients versus 20 matched controls by measuring proliferation, cytotoxicity, and IFN-gamma secretion of PBMC, CD4, and CD8 cells stimulated with autologous EBV-infected lymphoblastoid cell lines (LCL), and assessed cross-reactivity of the anti-EBV response with human brain antigens. No measured response (proliferation, cytotoxicity, or IFN-gamma secreting cell number) differed significantly between MS and controls, though there was a non-significant trend toward decreased LCL-stimulated proliferation in MS (most marked in CD8 cells, p=0.070). No cross-reactivity between LCL and brain antigens was detected; the authors conclude the cellular immune response against EBV-infected cells is neither increased nor decreased in MS. An unexpected vigorous proliferation of LCL-stimulated cells to autologous PBMC/APC suggested a possible alternative autoimmune mechanism.

Lindsey et al 2012 J Neuroimmunol.body: Lindsey et al. measured the IgG antibody response to whole, cell-free EBV virions in serum and CSF of MS patients versus controls using ELISA and Western blot. By ELISA, anti-EBV IgG was significantly increased in MS serum (median 7.98 vs 4.94 ug/ml, p<0.001) and CSF (33 vs 19 ng/ml, p=0.006). Western blots resolved ~12 antigen bands and showed the MS antibody response was broadly higher across all antigens, with the most significant increases for the 77 kD and the small 19/12 kD capsid antigen bands. Monoclonal-antibody mapping identified the high-MW bands as gp350 and small bands as VCA components, and the authors propose that an altered, cross-reactive anti-EBV response could drive autoimmunity in MS.

Loosen et al 2022 Front Immunol.body: Retrospective matched cohort study using the German Disease Analyzer database (IQVIA) comparing 16,058 outpatients with infectious mononucleosis (ICD-10 B27, EBV) to 16,058 matched individuals without it, over a 10-year follow-up. The incidence of multiple sclerosis was significantly higher in the mononucleosis cohort (22.6 vs 11.9 cases/100,000 person-years; HR 1.86, 95% CI 1.09-3.16), with the strongest association in the 14-20 year age group (HR 3.52, 95% CI 1.00-12.37) and a stronger association in men than women. The data support a decisive involvement of EBV in MS pathophysiology.

Lossius et al 2011 J Neuroimmunol.body: Lossius, Vartdal and Holmoy established EBNA-1 reactive T cell lines from the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and blood of three relapsing-remitting MS patients and cloned EBNA-1 specific CD4+ T cells from two of them. EBNA-1 specific CD4+ T cell clones from both CSF and blood displayed Th1 or Th17 phenotypes and were restricted by HLA-DR molecules (in MS1 encoded by DRB1*0403 or DRB1*1501). The biologically active vitamin D metabolite 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D (1,25(OH)2D) inhibited T cell proliferation and suppressed secretion of IFN-gamma and IL-17 in a dose-dependent manner, irrespective of T cell origin and HLA restriction, without inducing apoptosis; 24,25(OH)2D and 25(OH)D had no effect at physiological concentrations. This is the first study showing that intrathecal EBNA-1 specific CD4+ T cells in MS are present in CSF and are susceptible to vitamin D modulation.

Lossius et al 2013 Mult Scler.body: The EnvIMS multinational case-control study (1660 MS cases, 3050 controls from Norway and Italy) used a validated questionnaire to assess self-reported history and season of past infectious mononucleosis (IM). A history of IM was associated with MS to a similar degree in Norway (OR 2.12) and Italy (OR 1.72), with no significant between-country difference. IM was associated with increased MS risk in every season (spring, summer, fall, winter) and the association was not stronger for spring-onset IM, when vitamin D reaches its nadir, arguing against biological interaction between low vitamin D and IM in MS development. The seasonal distribution of IM (peak in spring) suggests modulation of EBV infection risk by solar radiation/latitude.

Lossius et al 2014 Eur J Immunol.body: Lossius et al. used high-throughput TCR-beta sequencing of paired CSF and blood from 10 multiple sclerosis (MS) patients and 11 controls with other inflammatory neurological diseases (OIND), combined with reference TCR-beta libraries from sorted EBV- and influenza A virus-reactive blood T cells, to map the diversity, compartmentalization, persistence and EBV-reactivity of intrathecal T-cell responses. TCR repertoires were highly diverse and compartmentalized, with expanded CSF clones distinct from blood and persistent for over a year. TCR-beta sequences of EBV-reactive CD8+ T cells, including public EBV-specific sequences, were selectively enriched in MS CSF (median 3.9% vs 2.1% blood; p=0.006), whereas EBV-reactive CD4+ T cells were enriched in CSF of both MS and controls. MS patients also had higher anti-EBNA-1 and anti-VCA antibody titers and more frequent infectious mononucleosis history than controls.
Lossius et al 2014 Eur J Immunol.identifier: Lossius et al 2014 Eur J Immunol

Läderach et al 2025 Nature.body: Using a novel HLA-DRB1*15:01 (HLA-DR2b) humanized mouse model (BRGS-A2DR2) of primary EBV infection, the authors show that EBV expands oligoclonal, CNS-homing T-bet+CXCR3+ B cells. These B cells infiltrate submeningeal and perivascular brain regions, where they attract activated effector memory CD8+ T cells, CD4+ TH1 and TH17 cells via CXCR3-dependent chemokines (CXCL9/10) and CCL3/4/5. CXCR3 blockade, EBNA3B deletion, or B cell depletion with rituximab reduces neuroinvasion and T cell brain infiltration, suggesting EBV-driven T-bet+CXCR3+ B cells initiate multiple sclerosis pathology.

Lünemann et al 2006 Brain.body: A case-control immunological study of 20 untreated EBV-seropositive multiple sclerosis (MS) patients and 20 HLA-DR-matched healthy EBV carriers, characterizing T-cell responses to the EBV nuclear antigen-1 (EBNA1) C-terminal domain (aa 400-641) using overlapping peptides. EBNA1-specific, predominantly CD4+ memory T cells in MS patients were strikingly increased in frequency, showed higher proliferative capacity, higher functional avidity, broadened epitope recognition, and enhanced Th1 (IFN-gamma) production, whereas T-cell responses to other latent/lytic EBV antigens and CMV pp65, and EBV DNA loads, did not differ between groups. The authors suggest highly antigen-sensitive EBNA1-specific Th1 cells may sustain autoimmunity in MS by cross-recognition of CNS autoantigens.

Lünemann et al 2008 J Exp Med.body: In 24 untreated MS patients and 24 HLA-matched healthy EBV carriers, the authors found that T cell responses to the EBV nuclear antigen EBNA1 (but not to other EBV proteins, HCMV-pp65, or influenza) are selectively increased in MS, mediated by expanded EBNA1-specific central- and effector-memory CD4+ Th1 cells with elevated EBNA1-specific IgG1 titers. A fraction of these EBNA1-specific CD4+ T cells cross-recognized myelin antigens (3.37% of TCLs) more frequently than the control autoantigen proinsulin (0.45%); myelin cross-reactive clones produced IFN-γ and high IL-2 but less MIP-1β, a polyfunctional phenotype. EBV viral load, B-cell transformation/regression, and HCMV/influenza immunity were unchanged in MS, supporting the concept that clonally expanded, myelin cross-reactive EBNA1-specific CD4+ T cells contribute to MS.
Lünemann et al 2008 J Exp Med.identifier: Lünemann et al 2008 J Exp Med

Lünemann et al 2009 Ann Neurol.body: Prospective study of 147 untreated clinically isolated syndrome (CIS) patients (mean 7-year follow-up) versus 50 demographically matched healthy controls measuring humoral (ELISA IgG) and cellular (IFN-gamma ELISPOT) immune responses to EBV antigens (EBNA1, VCA, EA), HCMV, HHV-6, measles and influenza. CIS patients showed a selective and significant increase of EBNA1-specific IgG (p<0.0001) and EBNA1-specific IFN-gamma-producing T cells (p=0.0074), but not to other antigens, plus ~4-fold higher cell-bound EBV DNA load (p=0.036). EBNA1 was the only antigen whose IgG correlated with T2 lesions, Barkhof criteria and EDSS at baseline and follow-up, and elevated EBNA1 IgG predicted conversion to MS by McDonald criteria (univariate HR 2.2, 95% CI 1.2-4.3, p=0.003), suggesting EBNA1 IgG titers as a prognostic marker for conversion and disability progression.

Lünemann et al 2024 Mult Scler.body: A long-term (median 20-year follow-up) study of 98 patients with a first demyelinating event/clinically isolated syndrome from the Cemcat (Barcelona) cohort, examining whether humoral immune responses to HCMV and EBV (EBNA1, VCA) at disease onset associate with serum and CSF levels of nine inflammatory/neurodegeneration biomarkers. High anti-HCMV immune responses inversely correlated with serum neurofilament light chain (rho=-0.367, p=0.039) and were associated with lower NfL (p=0.006) and reduced disability progression (EDSS 4.0, SPMS), supporting a protective role of HCMV. Elevated serum NfL predicted worse disability outcomes, and high anti-EBNA1 responses associated with higher serum soluble CD21 (p=0.020) and an increased relapse rate (RR=1.707, p=0.001).

Magliozzi et al 2013 J Neuropathol Exp N.body: Postmortem study of 44 secondary progressive MS (SPMS) cases showing that subpial cortical lesions with dense perivascular lymphocytic infiltrates occur in 11 of 26 cases with meningeal B-cell follicles (F+) but none of the 18 F- cases. Intracortical infiltrates were enriched in CD20+ B cells and Ig+ plasmablasts/plasma cells alongside CD3+/CD8+ T cells. EBV-encoded small RNA (EBER) positive cells were found in 3/3 infiltrates analyzed, and EBV lytic proteins BZLF1 and BFRF1 were expressed in plasma cells of active (but not chronic active) cortical lesions. CD8+ T cells expressing granzyme B, perforin, and CD107a contacted EBV-infected plasma cells, suggesting an EBV-driven cytotoxic immunopathologic response contributes to cortical damage in MS progression.
Magliozzi et al 2013 J Neuropathol Exp N.identifier: Magliozzi et al 2013 J Neuropathol Exp Neurol

Malyavantham et al 2015 PLoS One.body: Case-control serological study of 969 serum samples (315 healthy controls, 411 RR-MS, 128 SP-MS, 33 PP-MS, 82 other neurological diseases) testing autoantibodies against two putative MS antigens (CSF114(Glc) and KIR4.1a/KIR4.1b peptides) plus 24 endogenous autoimmune antigens, with associations to HLA DRB1*15:01, anti-EBV (EBNA-1, VCA), anti-CMV antibodies, EDSS and MRI measures. Antibodies against CSF114(Glc), KIR4.1a and KIR4.1b peptides were not increased in MS versus controls and were not associated with disability or MRI measures; HLA DRB1*15:01 positivity and anti-EBV antibodies (both established MS risk factors) were not associated with these putative MS antibodies. Anti-EBV EBNA-1 and anti-VCA titers were significantly higher in every MS sub-group than controls, and HLA DRB1*15:01 was associated with anti-EBV EBNA-1 and anti-VCA status.

Mameli et al 2012 PLoS One.body: In vitro study investigating whether Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and its major envelope glycoprotein 350 (EBVgp350) activate the potentially neuropathogenic human endogenous retrovirus W elements MSRV and syncytin-1 in cells relevant to multiple sclerosis (MS): U87-MG astrocytes and PBMC subsets. Using discriminatory env-specific real-time RT-PCR and flow cytometry, the authors show basal HERV-W/MSRV/syncytin-1 expression in astrocytes and in NK, B cells and monocytes (but not T cells), amplified in untreated MS patients and reduced under therapy. EBV/EBVgp350 stimulates MSRV and syncytin-1 transcription in astrocytes (NF-kappaB-dependent) and in B cells and monocytes (especially MDM), but not in T or NK cells; NK and B cells respond instead to proinflammatory cytokines. The findings support a model where EBV is an initial trigger of MS and HERV-W/MSRV/syncytin-1 a contributor to pathogenicity.

Mameli et al 2013 J Neuroimmunol.body: Short communication measuring anti-EBNA-1 IgG antibodies by ELISA in 125 Sardinian MS patients and 140 healthy controls. EBNA-1 IgG seroprevalence and titers were significantly higher in MS than controls (91% vs 69%, AUC=0.75; median 81.5 vs 46.4 RU/ml; both p<0.0001), and subjects in the highest EBNA-1 IgG quartile had a 4.6-fold increased MS risk (OR=4.6). In a subset of 37 patients, anti-EBNA-1 IgG titers decreased after 6 months of IFN-beta therapy (median 99.37 to 70.75 RU/ml, p=0.0003), strengthening the EBV-MS association in Sardinia.

Mameli et al 2013 PLoS One.body: Case-control study of 17 hospitalized infectious mononucleosis (IM) patients and 24 healthy donors testing whether EBV activates the potentially neuropathogenic HERV-W/MSRV in vivo. MSRVenv mRNA in PBMC was strongly elevated during acute IM (median 6.9-fold over healthy donors, p=0.014; ~2 Log10 over EBV-negative controls, p=0.000006) and correlated with anti-EBNA-1 IgG titers in latently infected healthy donors (Spearman rho=0.60, p<0.05). Flow cytometry showed increased HERV-Wenv protein on the membrane of B cells, NK cells and monocytes (highest in monocytes, 5.4-fold, p=0.043), but not T cells. The authors propose HERV-W/MSRV activation as the missing link between EBV and multiple sclerosis.

Mameli et al 2014 J Neuroimmunol.body: Case-control serological study of 53 untreated Sardinian multiple sclerosis (MS) patients and 53 matched healthy controls. The authors used ELISA to measure IgG antibodies against the homologous peptides EBNA1(400-413) of Epstein-Barr virus, MAP121-132 of Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis, and the myelin basic protein epitope MBP85-98. Antibodies against all three peptides were highly prevalent in EBV+ MS patients versus controls, and competition assays showed anti-EBNA1(400-413) and anti-MAP121-132 antibodies cross-react with MBP85-98, supporting a molecular mimicry mechanism by which EBV and MAP may trigger autoimmunity in MS.

Mancuso et al 2006 J Med Virol.body: Case-control study using nested-PCR to detect DNA of six human herpesviruses (HSV-1/2, EBV, VZV, HCMV, HHV-6) and JC virus in cerebrospinal fluid from 38 MS patients, 28 patients with other neurological diseases (OND), and 19 without neurological diseases (NND). VZV DNA was detected significantly more often in relapsing-remitting MS (43.5%) than in OND (10.7%, P<0.05), and in none of the NND controls, suggesting a possible role of VZV in MS pathogenesis. EBV, HCMV, HHV-6, and JCV were found at low frequency in MS without significant differences from controls, HSV-1/2 was not detected in MS, and viral detection was not associated with altered blood-brain barrier or IgG indexes.
Mancuso et al 2006 J Med Virol.identifier: Mancuso et al 2006 J Med Virol

Mancuso et al 2010 J Med Virol.body: Italian case-control study testing cell-free and cell-associated DNA of four neurotropic viruses (JCV, VZV, HHV-6, EBV) by real-time qPCR in CSF from 51 MS patients and 30 patients with other neurological diseases. Viral DNA was detectable in only a minority of patients and the overall prevalence in MS (6/51, 11.8%) was not significantly different from controls (3/30, 10%; P=0.9, OR=1.2). Cell-free EBV DNA was found in only 1 RRMS patient and HHV-6 in 1 chronic progressive MS patient; JCV was detected in both groups but did not predict active MRI lesions. The authors conclude these viruses are unlikely to play a pivotal role in MS pathogenesis and likely reach the CNS via peripheral cell trafficking rather than blood-brain barrier leakage.
Mancuso et al 2010 J Med Virol.identifier: Mancuso et al 2010 J Med Virol

Maple et al 2019 J Infect.body: UK case-control serological study comparing CMV and EBV antibody responses in 78 relapsing MS patients versus 124 (CMV) / up to 83 (EBV VCA) general-population controls, all from the Midlands region. CMV IgG seroprevalence and geometric mean IgG levels were significantly LOWER in PwMS than controls, while EBNA-1 IgG levels were significantly HIGHER in PwMS; EBV VCA IgG levels did not differ. Within PwMS, EBNA-1 IgG was non-significantly lower in CMV-seropositive than CMV-seronegative patients. The authors interpret CMV infection as potentially immunomodulatory/protective in MS and worthy of further study.

Maple et al 2024 Pathogens.body: A seroepidemiological case-control study comparing IgG seroprevalence and antibody levels against four human herpesviruses (CMV, EBV [VCA and EBNA-1], HSV, VZV) in serum from 200 Italian relapsing-remitting people with MS (PwMS) and 137 healthy controls (HCs) from the CRESM Biobank, Orbassano, Italy, using commercial ELISAs. EBV VCA IgG and EBNA-1 IgG were seroprevalent in 100% of PwMS and at higher levels than HCs (VCA p=0.0002; EBNA-1 p<0.0001), supporting EBV's fundamental role in MS. CMV IgG seroprevalence (58.7% PwMS vs 62.9% HC) showed no negative association with MS; HSV IgG levels were significantly lower in PwMS (p=0.0005); VZV seroprevalence was high (~98%) in both groups. Several markers were influenced by age and sex.

Marti et al 2024 Front Immunol.body: Marti et al. used an in vitro IL-2 + R848 memory B cell expansion assay to characterize antibody-secreting cell repertoires in untreated RRMS, natalizumab-treated RRMS, aHSCT, and healthy donors. They confirmed elevated anti-EBNA1_380-641 (C-terminal) IgG secretion in MS, positive correlations of C-terminal EBNA1 antibodies with anti-ANO2_1-275 and anti-GlialCAM_262-416 autoantibodies, and provided cross-reactivity (cross-absorption) evidence that EBNA1_380-641 blocks anti-ANO2_1-275 binding. They further showed natalizumab potentiates while aHSCT reduces the anti-EBNA1 humoral response, and that high pre-transplant serum anti-EBNA1 IgG associates with post-aHSCT EBV reactivation.

Martin et al 2009 Acta Neurol Scand.body: Martin et al. (Acta Neurol Scand 1997; 95: 280-283) used nested PCR at two Swedish laboratories to test CSF and serum for DNA from seven human herpesviruses (HSV-1, HSV-2, EBV, VZV, CMV, HHV-6 and HHV-7) in patients with multiple sclerosis (n=26), monosymptomatic optic neuritis (n=19) and other neurological diseases (n=20), plus consecutive samples from 6 MS patients in an acyclovir trial. No viral DNA was detected in any CSF (n=115) or serum (n=116) sample despite high assay sensitivities (e.g. EBV down to 0.1-1.0 fg, ~4 genomes). The authors conclude these results argue against a disseminated, productive herpesvirus infection in MS but do not exclude a lesion-associated, low-grade infection in the MS brain.
Martin et al 2009 Acta Neurol Scand.identifier: Martin et al 2009 Acta Neurol Scand

Martyn et al 1993 J Neurol Neurosurg Psy.body: Case-control reanalysis (214 MS-spectrum patients: optic neuritis, isolated demyelinating lesions, clinically definite MS; vs HLA-DR2-positive blood donors and non-MS neurological controls) of serological and infection-history data from a 1980s London study. Among subjects seropositive for EBV viral capsid antigen, recall of infectious mononucleosis was associated with MS (OR 2.9, 95% CI 1.1-7.2, p=0.03), and the association was strongest for IM at or before age 17 (OR 7.9, 95% CI 1.7-37.9, p=0.01). Odds ratios were adjusted for age, sex and HLA-DR2 status. The authors conclude MS is associated not with EBV infection per se but with delayed (post-childhood) EBV infection, implicating an age-dependent host response in demyelination.
Martyn et al 1993 J Neurol Neurosurg Psy.identifier: Martyn et al 1993 J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry

Massa et al 2007 Neuroepidemiology.body: Nested case-control study within the Nurses Health Study (NHS) and NHS II cohorts (18 prospectively collected MS cases matched 1:1 to controls) testing whether plasma IgG titers to the EBV early lytic protein BZLF1 predict multiple sclerosis risk. Anti-BZLF1 ODU was higher in MS cases than controls (0.80 vs 0.44, p=0.05) with an unadjusted RR of 4.6 (95% CI 0.84-25.24), but this association was attenuated after adjustment for anti-EBNA-1 titers and disappeared after further adjustment for anti-EBNA-2 (RR 0.72). The authors conclude that antibody titers to EBNAs are the strongest predictor of MS risk and that anti-BZLF1 antibodies add little further contribution.

Mccutcheon et al 2026 Neurol Neuroimmuno.body: McCutcheon et al. discover an MS patient-derived monoclonal antibody (mAb) to the predictive MS signature motif P-(SA)-x-(SGA)-R-(SN)-(LRKH) and use it to qualify a Luminex consensus-peptide autoantibody serologic test. Seropositivity to the motif was ~9-11% in the UCSF EPIC MS cohort and predicted MS up to 8 years before clinical diagnosis in DoDSR samples. The mAb identifies EBV tegument protein BRRF2 (and EBV glycoprotein M) as nanomolar-affinity tolerance-breaking antigens carrying the motif, with anti-BRRF2 IgG restricted to CSF oligoclonal bands of MS signature-positive patients, and identifies vimentin as the dominant cross-reactive CNS host antigen.

Mechelli et al 2011 Mult Scler.body: Fine-specificity study of the humoral immune response to Epstein-Barr nuclear antigen-1 (EBNA-1) in 12 monozygotic twin pairs (9 MS-discordant, 3 healthy), 3 non-twin MS patients and 2 healthy subjects, using solid-phase ELISA against all unique maximally overlapping octapeptides of EBNA-1. The glycine-alanine rich domain was immunodominant in all seropositive subjects, but MS patients (affected co-twins and non-twin patients) showed a significantly increased antibody response to a C-terminal EBNA-1 epitope (aa 401-411, GRRPFFHPVGE) versus healthy controls (p=0.006 in discordant twins; p=0.002 overall). This epitope contains an RRPFF motif with homology to alpha-B-crystallin, a candidate MS autoantigen, suggesting molecular mimicry relevant to MS pathogenesis. History of infectious mononucleosis, smoking, and serology to other viruses did not correlate with the 401-411 response.

Mechelli et al 2013 PLoS One.body: A 'candidate-interactome' aggregate analysis of GWAS data in multiple sclerosis (using IMSGC & WTCCC2 SNP p-values, ALIGATOR and Ingenuity Pathway Analysis) testing 13 interactomes (viral, immune, vitamin D receptor, aryl hydrocarbon receptor) for statistical enrichment of MS-associated genes. The Epstein-Barr virus, HIV and hepatitis B virus interactomes reached significance (with and without MHC SNPs), with EBV emerging as the etiologically most relevant, while phylogenetically related herpesviruses (CMV, HHV8) and JCV, HCV, H1N1, hu-IFN, AIRE, VDR and AHR were not enriched. The authors interpret EBV-host genotype interaction as supporting a causal role in MS, while noting that viruses use both common and unique strategies to perturb the human molecular network.

Mechelli et al 2015 Neurology.body: Case-control study analyzing the most polymorphic region of the Epstein-Barr nuclear antigen 2 (EBNA2) gene in 53 patients with multiple sclerosis (MS) and 38 matched healthy donors using seminested PCR/Sanger sequencing plus Illumina MiSeq deep sequencing. MS risk was significantly associated with an excess of the EBNA2 1.2 allele (OR 5.13) and newly identified 1.2-related variants (especially amino acid 245, OR 9.4), while the 1.3B allele was protective (OR 0.23). EBNA2 variants did not correlate with HLA typing or clinical/MRI features, and a Bayesian Network classifier of EBNA2 genotypes discriminated MS from controls (AUC 0.715). The authors conclude EBV genomic variants are associated with MS, reinforcing an EBV contribution to disease.

Mechelli et al 2025 Proc Natl Acad Sci U.body: This PNAS study shows that genes encoding EBV interactors are enriched in MS risk loci but not in other diseases, and in prioritized MS therapeutic targets. These MS-associated EBV interactors (MS-AIG) are dysregulated in MS blood and brain transcriptomes (notably the CD40 pathway) and are strongly enriched in EBNA2 binding sites, often colocalizing with CTCF and POLR2A. EBNA2 was detected in CD79a+ B cells in postmortem MS brain. The 1.2 EBNA2 viral allele downregulates CD40 expression analogously to the CD40 MS-risk variant and associates with a 2.5-fold increased MS risk, demonstrating convergence of host and viral genetic variability in MS-specific mechanisms.

Meloni et al 2026 Neurol Neuroimmunol Ne.body: An integrated virus-host molecular study of 77 therapy-naive persons with MS (PwMS) and 40 healthy donors (HD) from 3 Italian centers, profiling EBV serology, DNA load (ddPCR), and viral RNA (preamplified RT-PCR) in PBMCs and CSF cells, plus expression of 47 immune-related genes. Anti-EBNA1 IgG titers, EBV DNA load, and detection of EBV latency II/III and lytic transcripts (LMP1, LMP2A, EBNA1, EBNA3A, BZLF1, gp350/220) were all higher/more frequent in PwMS, with compartmentalized EBV activity in CSF. PwMS showed broad upregulation of cytotoxic, type I IFN, and chemokine immune genes, and exploratory factor analysis linked the lytic transcript BZLF1 with an inflammatory/IFN/chemokine signature, supporting EBV latency disruption and lytic reactivation as drivers of immune dysregulation in MS.

Miguel et al 2001 Epidemiology.body: Nested case-control study (Hernan, Zhang, Lipworth, Olek, Ascherio) within the Nurses' Health Study and Nurses' Health Study II (301 MS cases, 1,416 healthy controls, 262 breast cancer controls) testing whether late infection with common childhood viruses raises MS risk. A history of infectious mononucleosis, a marker of late EBV infection, was a moderate risk factor for MS (OR=2.1, 95% CI 1.5-2.9); mumps after age 15 (OR=2.3, 95% CI 1.2-4.3) and measles after age 15 (OR=2.8, 95% CI 0.8-9.1) were also associated, whereas overall history of measles, mumps, rubella, chickenpox, tonsillectomy, cat ownership and birth order were not. The findings support the polio hypothesis that delayed exposure to common viruses, particularly EBV, increases MS risk.

Monaco et al 2023 Neurol Neuroimmunol Ne.body: Monaco et al. quantified EBV DNA load in PBMCs and CD19+ B cells from 26 healthy controls, 25 stable-MS, and 25 active-MS patients, and generated spontaneous lymphoblastoid cell lines (SLCLs) immortalized with endogenous EBV. EBV was detected far more frequently in CD19+ B cells of active-MS patients (80%) than in stable MS (28%) or controls (42%), and SLCLs were more readily generated from MS patients. The EBNA1 small-molecule inhibitor VK-1727 selectively blocked proliferation and metabolic activity of EBV+ SLCLs (but not EBV- B cells) in a cytostatic manner without inducing apoptosis, in contrast to cladribine which was cytotoxic to all B cells. VK-1727 reduced EBNA1 DNA binding at the viral DS and Qp sites and the cellular CLIC1 site and modestly reduced EBNA1/EBNA2 latent gene expression.

Monte et al 2025 J Neurol.body: Retrospective case-control study of 57 pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (POMS) patients at Bambino Gesu Children's Hospital (2010-2024) compared to 162 age- and sex-matched controls (50 primary-headache non-autoimmune controls plus 112 non-neurological autoimmune controls: 80 IBD and 32 JIA). All 57 POMS patients (100%) were EBV seropositive versus 59% of controls, yielding an odds ratio of 79.2 (95% CI 4.8-1305, p=3.9x10^-11). Anti-EBNA IgG and anti-VCA IgG titers were significantly higher in POMS than in autoimmune and non-autoimmune controls (p<0.0001), while anti-VCA IgM did not differ. The authors conclude EBV has a disease-specific role in POMS development, distinct from other pediatric autoimmune disorders.

Morandi et al 2019 Front Immunol.body: Pilot case-control study comparing RNA expression of the MSRV/HERV-W envelope gene and Toll-like receptors TLR2 and TLR4 in blood of 22 MS patients, 9 HIV+ patients, and 22 healthy controls. MSRV/HERV-Wenv was significantly higher in MS than in HC and HIV; TLR4 was higher in both MS and HIV, while TLR2 was higher only in MS. HERV-W Env protein was expressed mainly by B cells and monocytes but not T cells. EBV-immortalized lymphoblastoid cell lines (LCL) showed strong induction of MSRV/HERV-W env, and in vitro Efavirenz (alone at high dose) and combined antiretroviral drugs reduced MSRV/HERV-W env expression, suggesting ART might protect from MS by suppressing HERV expression.

Mostafa et al 2017 J Med Virol.body: Iranian case-control study quantifying MSRV (HERV-W)-type Env DNA by qPCR in PBMCs of 52 relapsing-remitting MS patients versus 40 healthy controls, alongside EBV status (DNA load and anti-EBNA1 IgG) and serum vitamin D. MSRV DNA copy number was significantly higher in RRMS patients than controls (P<0.0001). MSRV copy number inversely correlated with serum vitamin D in RRMS patients (P=0.0131), but showed no correlation with EBV load or anti-EBNA1 IgG, nor with EDSS, gender, age, or treatment duration.
Mostafa et al 2017 J Med Virol.identifier: Mostafa et al 2017 J Med Virol

Mouhieddine et al 2015 Clin Immunol.body: Retrospective case-control study at the American University of Beirut (249 MS patients vs 230 controls, 2010-2014) examining EBV seropositivity and MS risk factors in the Lebanese population. EBV seropositivity (anti-VCA and anti-EBNA-1) and antibody titers were higher in MS patients than controls; the anti-EBNA-1 titer was significantly higher. MS patients had lower vitamin D (after excluding supplemented subjects), more heavy smokers, and more overweight/obese individuals. Multivariate predictors of MS were high anti-VCA/anti-EBNA-1 titers, young age, more smoking packs, and low vitamin D.

Mrad et al 2021 Neurol Neuroimmunol Neur.body: Cross-sectional study isolating 45 serum-derived exosome preparations from 15 healthy controls, 15 stable RRMS, and 15 active RRMS patients to test whether exosomes express EBV proteins and how they activate monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs). Serum exosomes from MS patients (especially active RRMS) expressed higher levels of EBV proteins EBNA1, LMP1, and LMP2A than healthy controls, and EBV(+) exosomes induced higher CXCL10 and CCL2 secretion by MDMs. MDMs from active patients were better secretors of CXCL10, CCL2, and CXCL9 and had a higher frequency of a CD14(++) macrophage subset that correlated with CXCL10 secretion, suggesting exosomal EBV proteins correlate with disease activity and drive a proinflammatory response.
Mrad et al 2021 Neurol Neuroimmunol Neur.identifier: Mrad et al 2021 Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm

Munch et al 2009 Acta Neurol Scand.body: Case-control serological study (Munch et al., Acta Neurol Scand 1998: 97: 171-174) testing sera from 138 sex- and age-matched multiple sclerosis (MS) patients, 138 healthy controls, and 44 HIV-positive patients with a commercial Biotest recombinant-antigen ELISA (EBNA1 and early antigen) that classifies EBV infection stage. 99% of MS patients (137/138) were EBV seropositive versus 90% of controls (124/138; P=0.00036). No primary EBV infections were detected in the MS group, whereas 4 of 124 seropositive controls showed primary infection (P=0.049652, Fisher's exact test), supporting the hypothesis that MS patients are infected with EBV before MS onset. Antibody patterns and titres in MS patients were comparable to controls, so the near-universal seropositivity could not be explained by immunodeficiency.
Munch et al 2009 Acta Neurol Scand.identifier: Munch et al 2009 Acta Neurol Scand

Munch et al 2009 Acta Neurol Scand [2142.body: Munch et al. (Acta Neurol Scand 1998;98:395-399) investigated the distribution of EBV subtypes, defined by the number of 39 bp repeats in the EBNA 6 (EBNA-3C) coding region, in members of two Danish multiple sclerosis (MS) clusters and in control cohorts (cluster schoolmate controls, random healthy controls, unrelated MS patients, and autoimmune-disease patients). All MS patients were EBV seropositive (vs 10% of healthy controls seronegative) and all seropositive individuals carried type A EBV. The subtype with 3 39 bp repeats predominated; notably all 8 members of the Fjelso MS cluster harboured this single subtype, significantly more often than the 16 healthy controls (Fisher exact P=0.0047) and all non-clustered individuals (P=0.017), giving circumstantial evidence that infection with the same EBV subtype links the cluster and that MS development is linked to EBV infection.
Munch et al 2009 Acta Neurol Scand [2142.identifier: Munch et al 2009 Acta Neurol Scand [21420e]

Munger et al 2015 Neurology.body: Prospective longitudinal analysis of 468 patients with clinically isolated syndrome (CIS) in the BENEFIT interferon beta-1b trial, measuring EBV (EBNA-1, VCA), CMV IgG antibodies and serum cotinine (a tobacco-use biomarker) at up to 4 time points and relating them to conversion to clinically definite/McDonald MS, relapse rate, EDSS change, and MRI lesion/brain-volume outcomes over 5 years. The study found no association between any EBV or CMV IgG antibody level, or cotinine level, and CIS-to-MS conversion or MS activity/progression (e.g., highest vs lowest EBNA-1 quartile RR for CDMS conversion 1.14, 95% CI 0.76-1.72; cotinine >25 vs <10 ng/mL RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.71-1.31). The authors conclude that, despite EBNA-1 IgG and smoking being established MS risk factors, neither predicts MS prognosis in early interferon-treated CIS.

Munger et al 2017 Mult Scler.body: Nested case-control study among US military personnel (222 incident MS cases, 444 matched controls) using pre-onset serum from the Department of Defense Serum Repository. Serum IgG titers against EBV antigens (EBNA complex, EBNA-1, EBNA-2, VCA) measured before MS onset were strongly and monotonically associated with MS risk: ~36-fold higher MS risk for the highest vs lowest anti-EBNA complex titers and ~8-fold for anti-EBNA-1. The associations were consistent across sex and race/ethnicity and were independent of serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, supporting pre-onset anti-EBNA antibodies as robust serological markers of MS risk (ROC C-statistic 0.67 for EBNAc, 0.65 for EBNA-1).

stats.qualifier: prospective nested case-control study of EBV serology and MS risk

Munger et al 2019 Ann Neurol.body: Prospective nested case-control study in the Finnish Maternity Cohort (FMC) testing whether maternal EBV/CMV IgG antibody levels during pregnancy predict MS risk in offspring (176 cases, 326 controls) and whether prediagnostic EBNA-1 IgG predicts MS in the women themselves (1,049 cases, 1,867 controls). High maternal VCA IgG during pregnancy was associated with a 2.4-fold increased MS risk in offspring (top vs bottom quintile, p trend=0.004), with no association for maternal EBNA-1, EA-D, or CMV IgG. Among women, higher prediagnostic EBNA-1 IgG was strongly associated with MS (top vs bottom quintile RR=3.42, p trend<1.11e-16); associations were independent of 25(OH)D and cotinine, and elevated cotinine (smoking) carried a 45-50% increased MS risk.

Myhr et al 1998 J Neurol Neurosurg Psych.body: Population-based case-control study from Hordaland county, western Norway, comparing anti-herpesvirus antibody prevalence in 144 patients with multiple sclerosis and 170 age-, sex-, and area-matched controls. IgG antibodies to EBV viral capsid antigen (VCA), nuclear antigen (EBNA), and early antigen (EA) were all significantly more frequent in MS patients than controls (all patients had anti-EBNA and/or anti-VCA IgG vs 95.3% of controls), whereas antibody prevalence to HSV, VZV, and CMV did not differ between groups. The altered EBV antibody pattern was independent of disease course and activity, suggesting a role for EBV in MS aetiology.

Márquez et al 2020 Front Immunol.body: Using a murine model where latent gammaherpesvirus-68 (γHV-68, a rodent homolog of EBV) infection enhances experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), Márquez et al. show that adoptive transfer of latently infected CD19+IgD- (memory) B cells from γHV-68 mice into naïve mice enhances EAE, increasing CD8+ T-cell CNS infiltration and IFNγ production while downregulating IL-17 (Th1 skewing). Depleting B cells with α-CD20 after EAE onset only partially reduces disease, whereas depletion before γHV-68 infection prevents EAE enhancement and abolishes splenic viral latency. The authors conclude that latency in memory B cells is required to drive the Th1 response that produces MS-like disease, supporting EBV vaccination as a prevention strategy.

Nielsen et al 2007 Arch Neurol.body: A Danish population-based cohort study of 25 234 persons tested serologically for EBV-related infectious mononucleosis (positive Paul-Bunnell reaction), linked to the Danish Multiple Sclerosis Registry. During 556 703 person-years of follow-up, 104 MS cases were observed versus 45.91 expected, giving a standardized incidence ratio of 2.27 (95% CI 1.87-2.75). The more than 2-fold increased MS risk was present in both men and women, was uniformly distributed across strata of sex and age, persisted for more than 30 years after mononucleosis, and did not vary by presumed severity of infection.

Nielsen et al 2007 Mult Scler.body: Cross-sectional study of 517 healthy Danish individuals (316 female, 201 male) testing whether non-viral MS risk factors are associated with anti-EBV viral capsid antigen (VCA) IgG antibody levels, measured by ELISA and analyzed by linear regression on log(anti-VCA IgG). Female gender, HLA-DR2 carriage, current smoking, and cumulative pack-years smoked were each positively associated with elevated anti-VCA IgG levels; the smoking effect was pronounced in females and absent in males. The authors interpret these correlations as support for the view that EBV is critically involved in MS etiology, with non-viral risk factors possibly acting through dysregulated EBV-specific immune responses.

Nielsen et al 2009 Mult Scler.body: Danish/Swedish case-control investigation assessing whether HLA-DRB1*15 and a history of infectious mononucleosis (IM, primary EBV infection) interact to confer multiple sclerosis (MS) risk. Comparing DRB1*15 prevalence in MS patients with (n=76) and without (n=1836) IM versus blood donors with (n=62) and without (n=484) IM, the authors found DRB1*15 carried a 2.4-fold increased MS risk in IM-naive persons but a 7.0-fold risk in persons with IM history. The MS risk from DRB1*15 was 2.9-fold stronger in the presence of IM (interaction OR 2.9, 95% CI 1.3-6.5, P=0.007), and DRB1*15-positive persons with IM history were estimated to have a 10.0-fold increased MS risk, indicating DRB1*15 and IM act synergistically to cause MS.

Nociti et al 2010 J Neuroimmunol.body: Case-control study comparing serum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) anti-EBV (anti-VCA IgG/IgM, anti-EBNA1 IgG) and anti-CMV (IgG/IgM) antibody titres across 267 treatment-naive relapsing-remitting MS, 50 CIDP and 88 ALS patients. Serum anti-VCA IgM, anti-VCA IgG and anti-EBNA1 IgG titres were significantly higher in MS than in CIDP and ALS, and intrathecally synthesised anti-EBNA1 IgG was detected in CSF only of MS patients. Conversely, MS patients showed a lower prevalence of anti-CMV IgG positivity (attributed partly to younger age). The findings provide additional evidence for a possible involvement of EBV in MS.

Noui et al 2024 J Neurol Neurosurg Psych.body: Multicentre retrospective observational cohort study (AutoMS-Swe) of 174 patients with relapsing-remitting MS who received autologous haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (AHSCT) in Sweden before 2020, investigating factors associated with treatment outcomes via univariable Cox models. Rituximab as the last DMT before AHSCT was protective against inflammatory disease activity (HR 0.18) whereas serum EBV DNA detection after AHSCT was associated with higher inflammatory disease activity (HR 2.3). Rituximab-treated patients had a much lower proportion of post-AHSCT EBV DNA detection (15% vs 49%, p<0.001), consistent with B-cell depletion, and the only rituximab-treated patients with inflammatory activity were also EBV DNA positive. Shorter disease duration and presence of gadolinium-enhancing lesions were associated with better disability outcomes (less worsening, more improvement).

Nourbakhsh et al 2021 Ann Neurol.body: Retrospective re-evaluation of 189 pediatric patients diagnosed with clinically isolated syndrome (CIS) or multiple sclerosis (MS) at the UCSF Regional Pediatric MS Center, of whom 25 (13%) were confirmed EBV-seronegative. MOG-IgG was positive in 11 of 25 (44%) EBV-seronegative patients versus only 9 of 164 (5.5%, p<0.001) EBV-seropositive patients, and all MOG-IgG-positive cases met criteria for MOG-antibody disease (MOGAD). HLA-DRB1*15:01/15:03 was less frequent in EBV-seronegative patients (16% vs 39%, p=0.019). After critical clinical and MRI review, MS remained the most plausible diagnosis in only 4 of 25 (16%) EBV-seronegative children, indicating that EBV seronegativity in an MS-like presentation should prompt consideration of alternative diagnoses, especially MOGAD.

Nova et al 2025 Eur J Neurol.body: A UK Biobank retrospective cohort study of 487,144 individuals testing whether the non-classical HLA class I allele HLA-E*01:01 interacts with infectious mononucleosis (IM, a clinical manifestation of EBV infection) to modulate multiple sclerosis (MS) risk. HLA-E*01:01 alone was not associated with IM (HR=0.99) or MS (HR=1.06, p=0.055), but a significant multiplicative interaction between HLA-E*01:01 and IM was found for MS risk (interaction beta=0.50, p<0.001): among individuals with IM history, MS risk was elevated in HLA-E*01:01/01:03 heterozygotes (HR=1.74) and HLA-E*01:01/01:01 homozygotes (HR=3.01) versus HLA-E*01:03 homozygotes. This interaction was independent of the known HLA-DRB1*15:01 x IM interaction, supporting the hypothesis that HLA-E*01:01 confers weaker CD8+ T-cell control of EBV-infected B cells and thus higher MS susceptibility.

Nova et al 2026 Mult Scler.body: A bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization study in individuals of European ancestry testing whether anti-EBNA1 IgG antibody levels causally influence multiple sclerosis (MS) risk. Using a robust cis-MR framework on UK Biobank anti-EBNA1 IgG GWAS data (7972 seropositive individuals) and IMSGC MS GWAS data (115,803 individuals), a one SD increase in genetically predicted anti-EBNA1 IgG levels was causally associated with a 69% higher MS risk (OR=1.69, 95% CI 1.28-2.23, p<0.001), consistent across sensitivity analyses, external French-cohort validation, and with no directional pleiotropy. Reverse MR found no evidence that MS influences anti-EBNA1 IgG levels (p>0.05), supporting a unidirectional causal effect of elevated anti-EBNA1 immune responses on MS risk.

Oikonen et al 2011 Mult Scler.body: Retrospective ecologic study in Southwestern Finland (1986-1995, before interferons) comparing monthly MS relapse occurrence among 407 interferon-naive MS patients with population-level epidemics of specifically diagnosed viral infections. Logistic regression (two-month relapse lag, three-month moving-average virus data) showed that peaks of influenza A and Epstein-Barr virus infections in the general population were temporally followed by higher MS relapse counts, whereas adenovirus epidemics were not. MS relapses were lowest in summer (Jun-Aug), suggesting seasonally varying environmental factors modulate relapse rate.

Ong et al 2020 Genes Immun.body: Whole-genome bisulfite sequencing study testing whether EBV-driven DNA hypomethylation in lymphoblastoid cell lines (LCLs) acts on multiple sclerosis (MS) risk loci. EBV-transformed B cells (LCLs) showed widespread hypomethylation (45.9% of 1-kb tiles), but MS risk loci (LCLeQTL and MSGWAS lists) and transcribed B-lymphocyte/immune genes were significantly UNDERrepresented among differentially methylated regions versus GWAS-catalog and genome-wide controls. Promoters were minimally affected by EBV. The authors conclude MS genetic risk is not driven by EBV hypomethylation, which instead appears tied to B-cell immortalization/tumorigenesis.

Operskalski et al 1989 Neurology.body: A matched case-control study of 145 US white MS patients (identified in a 1970 prevalence cohort, onset 1960-1969) and 145 friend controls examining whether MS is associated with exposure to uncommon viruses or older age at common-virus infection. The most striking finding was a strong positive association between a history of infectious mononucleosis (IM) and MS (13% of cases vs 2% of controls; OR=17.0, 95% CI 2.0-81.8), interpreted as suggesting older age at Epstein-Barr virus exposure. The study also found significant associations of MS with a greater number of different domiciles, visits to Mexico, and earlier age at menarche, but no association with measles, mumps, household pets, or canine distemper.

Opsahl et al 2007 J Neurol.body: Opsahl and Kennedy used in situ hybridisation (ISH), fluorescent ISH (FISH) and immunofluorescence (IF) to look for EBV latent (EBNA) and lytic (Zebra/BZLF1) gene transcription and protein in post-mortem brain from MS lesions, MS normal-appearing white matter (NAWM) and normal control brains. IF and mRNA FISH were essentially negative across all samples, largely owing to tissue RNA/protein degradation; non-fluorescent mRNA ISH showed only weak, scattered latent and lytic EBV signals in all three tissue categories with no quantitative or qualitative difference between MS and control tissue. The study provided no positive evidence of ongoing EBV involvement in MS but could not exclude a hit-and-run role.

Orr et al 2025 Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A.body: High-dimensional CODEX (CO-detection by indexing) spatial imaging study of postmortem brain tissue from secondary progressive (SPMS) and primary progressive (PPMS) multiple sclerosis patients versus non-MS controls across two independent biobanks (15 samples). EBV markers, particularly EBNA1 and LMP1, were enriched in MS lesions and spatially closer to and more frequently interacting with reactive astrocytes, microglia, and neurons. EBNA1 staining was confirmed within neurons and glial cells, immune cells were enriched and positioned closer to neurons, and blood-brain barrier integrity was disrupted (loss of Claudin-5/CD31, increased BAX, reduced Claudin-5 interactions). The authors propose EBV drives immune modulation, glial dysfunction, and neuronal damage in progressive MS, suggesting antiviral and brain-penetrant immune-modulator therapies.

Otto et al 2011 Neurology.body: Otto et al. determined the intrathecal fraction (F_S) of anti-EBV IgG of total intrathecally synthesized IgG in 24 CIS/MS patients with elevated EBV antibody indices (AIs), 3 cerebral PTLD patients (positive controls), and assessed EBV AI prevalence in 36 CIS/optic neuritis patients. Median F_S anti-EBV in CIS/MS was low (0.65%) and did not differ from F_S anti-measles (0.9%), whereas it was ~40-fold higher in PTLD (27.82%, p=0.008). All 24 CIS/MS patients with elevated EBV AI had at least one other elevated antiviral AI, EBV DNA was undetectable in CIS/MS CSF but present in all 3 PTLD CSF, and only 2/36 (5.6%) CIS patients had an elevated EBV AI. The authors conclude intrathecal anti-EBV antibodies are part of the polyspecific intrathecal immune response in CIS/MS, arguing against a direct CNS EBV infection.

Ovchinnikova et al 2024 Front Immunol.body: A case-control study using modified Phage ImmunoPrecipitation Sequencing (PhIP-Seq) on serum IgG from multiple sclerosis (MS) patients and healthy donors to identify novel autoantibody B-cell epitopes. The autoantibody response was highly heterogeneous, but elevated IgG titers against a spectrin alpha chain (SPTAN1) peptide were reproducibly and significantly higher in MS than in healthy donors, with serum levels correlating with CSF. MS sera were also reactive to EBV latent membrane protein 1 (LMP1). A four-peptide panel (SPTAN1, PRX, PTK6, LMP1) discriminated MS from controls with AUC=0.818 (sensitivity 79%, specificity 86%).

Pache et al 2024 Neurol Neuroimmunol Neu.body: A case-control study analyzing seroprevalences and frequencies of intrathecal IgG production (elevated antibody indices, AIs) to EBV (EBNA-1, VCA) compared with 10 other microbes in paired CSF/serum of 50 patients with MS (and 20 NIND controls). All 50 MS patients were EBV seropositive (100%), yet the frequency of elevated EBV AIs was paradoxically low (10%) and, relative to seroprevalence, the lowest among all microbes; parvovirus B19 showed the highest AI frequency (73%). Intrathecal antimicrobial antibody production was practically absent in seronegative patients, the number of elevated AIs correlated with total intrathecal IgG production, and a history of infectious mononucleosis was associated with higher serum EBNA-1 IgG and intrathecal IgG production. Findings support a hypothesis that B lineage cells are primed during acute EBV infection to enter the CNS, underscoring a unique peripheral role of EBV in MS.

Pender et al 2011 BMC Neurol.body: Case-control flow cytometry study of 62 MS patients (23 RRMS, 25 SPMS, 14 PPMS) and 59 healthy subjects quantifying PBMC subsets and HLA class I/II expression. HLA class I and class II expression on T cells, B cells and monocytes was normal in MS (except very low B-cell class II in 2 SPMS patients), so the previously described decreased CD8+ T cell response to EBV-infected B cells in MS is not due to reduced HLA class I expression. The study confirmed a significantly decreased percentage of CD8+ T cells and increased percentage of CD4+ T cells and CD4:CD8 ratio in MS, most pronounced in progressive MS.

Pender et al 2014 Mult Scler.body: First-in-human case report of EBV-specific adoptive immunotherapy for multiple sclerosis. A 42-year-old man with secondary progressive MS (EDSS 8.0) and a CD8+ T-cell deficiency was treated with four fortnightly IV infusions of in vitro-expanded autologous EBV-specific CD8+ T cells generated with the recombinant adenovirus AdE1-LMPpoly (encoding EBNA1, LMP1 and LMP2A epitopes). The therapy had no significant adverse effects and produced clinical improvement, increased circulating EBV-specific CD8+ T cells, reduced gadolinium-enhancing MRI lesion load and decreased intrathecal IgG production. The findings support the hypothesis that defective CD8+ T-cell control of EBV-infected B cells in the CNS contributes to MS.

Pender et al 2017 Clin Transl Immunology.body: A comprehensive case-control analysis of the T-cell response to EBV in 95 MS patients and 56 EBV-seropositive healthy subjects using flow cytometry and intracellular IFN-gamma staining against autologous EBV-infected lymphoblastoid cell lines and pools of HLA-class-I-restricted EBV lytic, EBV latent and CMV peptides. The CD8+ T-cell response to EBV lytic (but not CMV lytic) antigens was decreased at MS onset and all stages, while the response to EBV latent antigens was increased but functionally exhausted (reduced cytokine polyfunctionality), skewing the EBV-specific CD8+ response from lytic to latent. EBV-specific T cells expanded during clinical attacks and progressively declined with disease duration; the anti-EBNA1 IgG titre correlated inversely with EBV-specific CD8+ T-cell frequency. The authors postulate that defective CD8+ T-cell control of EBV reactivation permits expansion of latently infected (including autoreactive) B cells in the CNS.
Pender et al 2017 Clin Transl Immunology.identifier: Pender et al 2017 Clin Transl Immunology

Pender et al 2018 JCI Insight.body: An open-label phase I clinical trial (ACTRN12615000422527) treating 10 patients with progressive multiple sclerosis (5 SPMS, 5 PPMS) with 4 escalating doses of autologous in vitro-expanded EBV-specific T cells (generated using the AdE1-LMPpoly adenoviral vector) targeting EBNA1, LMP1, and LMP2A. The therapy was safe with no serious adverse events; 7 of 10 patients showed clinical improvement, with reduced fatigue, improved QOL, and reduced intrathecal IgG production in 3 patients. Clinical improvement was strongly associated with the EBV reactivity and polyfunctionality of the administered T cell product: all 6 patients receiving T cells with strong EBV reactivity (>5% of CD8+ T cells) improved, versus only 1 of 4 receiving weak-reactivity cells (P=0.033).

Perlejewski et al 2020 PLoS One.body: Case-control study searching for viral RNA/DNA in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of 34 relapsing-remitting MS patients and 13 controls using in-house quantitative real-time RT-PCR/PCR against common neurotropic viruses, plus shotgun DNA/RNA metagenomics in 13 MS patients and 4 controls. Real-time PCR detected viral nucleic acid in 7/34 (20.59%) MS patients (HHV-6 in 3, EBV in 2, VZV in 1, Enterovirus in 1) and 1/13 (7.69%) controls (EBV), a difference that was not statistically significant (Fisher's exact test). Metagenomics detected no eukaryotic viruses even in three real-time-PCR-positive samples (viral loads 550-1650 copies/ml), indicating metagenomics is less sensitive than real-time PCR for low-copy CSF.

Persson Berg et al 2022 BMJ Neurol Open.body: Serological cohort study within the Swedish IMSE natalizumab pharmacovigilance cohort measuring serum IgG to EBV glycoprotein 350 (EBVgp350) and measles virus nucleocapsid protein (MeV N_CORE) by indirect ELISA in 728 patients with MS (714 NAT-treated, 170 with prior IFN-beta samples) versus 144 matched blood donors. Patients with MS had higher anti-EBVgp350 (p=0.0006) and anti-MeV N_CORE IgG (p<0.0001) than controls. Both anti-EBVgp350 and anti-MeV N_CORE IgG declined during natalizumab treatment (p<0.0001) but were relatively stable during prior IFN-beta therapy. All 728 patients with MS were EBV seropositive (confirmed with VCA/EBNA1 in gp350-negative samples), whereas 10/144 (6.9%) controls were EBV seronegative, supporting a role for EBV in MS pathogenesis.

Petersen et al 2012 J Neuroimmunol.body: Longitudinal study of 26 relapsing-remitting MS patients starting de novo IFN-beta therapy, analysing serologic antiviral responses to the herpesviruses EBV, VZV, and HSV from baseline to 1-year follow-up, stratified by disease activity (IFN-beta responders vs non-responders). Anti-EBNA-1 IgG and anti-VZV IgG reactivity increased significantly from baseline to follow-up, driven by the six patients with active MS (IFN-beta non-responders), whereas no significant changes were seen for EBV early antigen, HSV, rubella, or parvovirus B19. No correlations were found between herpesvirus serology and the lectin complement pathway components MBL, MASP-2, and MASP-3. The authors conclude that EBV and VZV, together with HERV-H/HERV-W and the antiviral immune response, may play a role in MS development.

Pfuhl et al 2015 J Neuroimmunol.body: Cross-sectional analysis of 96 patients with clinically isolated syndrome (CIS) or early relapsing-remitting MS from the Berlin CIS cohort, testing whether serum IgG antibody levels to EBV nuclear antigen-1 (EBNA-1), EBV viral capsid antigen (VCA), rubella virus, and varicella zoster virus (VZV) associate with intrathecal IgG synthesis. Serum anti-EBNA-1 IgG, but not anti-VCA, anti-rubella, or anti-VZV IgG, was significantly higher in patients with a calculated intrathecal IgG synthesis >0% (p=0.03) and correlated with the percentage (r=0.27, p=0.009) and concentration (r=0.27, p=0.012) of intrathecally produced IgG. The authors conclude there is a specific link between EBV infection (via EBNA-1 antibody response) and the events leading to intrathecal IgG synthesis in early MS.

Pohl et al 2006 Neurology.body: Case-control study of EBV serology in 147 pediatric patients with multiple sclerosis (disease onset before age 16) and paired age- and gender-matched controls in Goettingen, Germany. Children with MS showed near-complete seropositivity for anti-EBV-VCA IgG (98.6% vs 72.1% in controls, p=0.001) and higher anti-EBNA1 seropositivity (92.5% vs 57.5%, p<0.0001), with significantly higher median antibody concentrations, but no serologic evidence of recent EBV infection. The authors conclude that a prior EBV infection might be a conditio sine qua non for the development of pediatric MS.

Ponsonby et al 2005 JAMA.body: Population-based case-control study in Tasmania, Australia (1999-2001; 136 MRI-confirmed MS cases, 272 sex- and birth-year-matched community controls) evaluating whether exposure to infant siblings (a younger sibling aged <2 years) during the first 6 years of life is associated with MS risk, and exploring EBV infection as a possible mechanism. Increasing cumulative infant-years of contact was strongly and inversely (dose-response) associated with MS (AOR 0.12 for >=5 vs <1 infant-year; trend P=.002), and was associated with delayed MS onset. Among controls, higher infant contact reduced the likelihood of infectious mononucleosis and very high composite EBV IgG titers. Cases had higher composite EBV antibody titers and more past infectious mononucleosis than controls, but the protective infant-contact effect on MS persisted after adjustment for EBV antibody titer.
