Pérez-Pérez et al 2021 Front Immunol.body: Cross-sectional study of 80 RR-MS, 21 PP-MS, and 37 healthy donors comparing pHERV-W ENV/syncytin-1 protein (flow cytometry) and gene (qPCR) expression and their relationship with anti-EBV (anti-VCA, anti-EBNA-1 IgG) and anti-HHV-6A/B (IgM, IgG) antibody titers. MS patients showed significantly higher pHERV-W ENV/syncytin-1 protein and gene expression than HD, with PP-MS highest. Anti-HHV-6A/B IgM (in RR-MS) and anti-HHV-6A/B IgG (in PP-MS) titers positively correlated with pHERV-W ENV protein expression, while anti-EBNA-1 IgG correlated negatively in HD monocytes, supporting a possible HHV-6A/B transactivation of pHERV-W ENV in MS.

Pérez-Pérez et al 2021 Sci Rep.body: Prospective study of 71 pregnant women (50 pregnant MS patients, P-MS, and 21 pregnant healthy controls, P-HC) analysing antibody titres against EBV and HHV-6A/B and MSRV (HERV-W) env mRNA expression in serum across each pregnancy trimester and postpartum. IgM antibody titres against HHV-6A/B were significantly higher in P-MS than P-HC in every trimester and postpartum, and first-trimester anti-HHV-6A/B IgM trended higher in P-MS who relapsed postpartum (p=0.052). MSRV env mRNA prevalence was higher in P-MS than P-HC in the first trimester (OR=3.000, p=0.003) and significantly more prevalent in P-MS who relapsed during gestation (OR=10.023, p=0.038). IgG antibodies against EBV (anti-VCA, anti-EBNA-1) and against HHV-6A/B showed no significant differences, suggesting first-trimester IgM anti-HHV-6A/B and MSRV env mRNA could act as relapse predictors.

Pérez‐Pérez et al 2018 Eur J Neurol.body: A 2-year observational study of 482 Spanish multiple sclerosis (MS) patients examining the link between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6). 25(OH)D was higher in the second semester of the year; carriers of the MS risk allele rs2248359-C had lower 25(OH)D. EBV viral load measured by qPCR was significantly and inversely correlated with 25(OH)D levels (highest when 25(OH)D was low), whereas antibody titres (anti-EBNA1, anti-VCA) and all HHV-6 measures showed no significant association with 25(OH)D. The authors conclude 25(OH)D may regulate EBV replication/reactivation in MS.
Pérez‐Pérez et al 2018 Eur J Neurol.identifier: Pérez‐Pérez et al 2018 Eur J Neurol

Querol et al 2013 Neurology.body: Querol et al. used a protein antigen microarray of 9,393 human proteins to profile CSF-derived IgG reactivity in multiple sclerosis (MS) versus controls, identifying recombination signal binding protein for immunoglobulin kappa J region (RBPJ) as a novel MS autoantigen. RBPJ reactivity discriminated MS from controls on the array (p=0.0052) and, in a large validation cohort, anti-RBPJ autoantibodies were more prevalent in MS CSF (12.5%) than in CSF of patients with other neurologic disease (1.6%; p=0.02 by ELISA), confirmed by immunocytochemistry. Reactivity was restricted to CSF (intrathecal origin), with no serum difference between MS and healthy controls. The authors note RBPJ is a Notch-pathway transcriptional regulator central to Epstein-Barr virus infection through its interaction with EBNA proteins, making it a biologically relevant MS autoantigen candidate.

Raffel et al 2013 Mult Scler Relat Disor.body: Prospective study measuring serum anti-EBNA-1 IgG titres by quantitative ELISA in 10 relapsing-remitting MS patients before and 12 months after starting interferon-beta and 10 patients starting natalizumab. Neither disease modifying drug produced a significant change in individual anti-EBNA-1 IgG titre, and there was no significant difference between groups in mean titre or percentage change. The authors conclude anti-EBNA-1 IgG titre is unlikely to be a good surrogate marker of disease activity in patients on DMDs, and the lack of titre rise after natalizumab argues against dysregulated EBV infection in the CNS.
Raffel et al 2013 Mult Scler Relat Disor.identifier: Raffel et al 2013 Mult Scler Relat Disord

Rafiee et al 2021 Neuroepidemiology.body: Case-control study (Intervirology 2021;64:203-208) comparing immune-cell cytokine responses to EBV peptides in whole-blood cultures from 10 relapsing-remitting MS patients (all on interferon beta-1A) and 10 healthy controls. Whole blood was stimulated with EBV EBNA1 (HLA-B*3501, HPVGEADYFEY) and BRLF1 (HLA-A*2402, DYCNVLNKEF) peptides, and IL-2 and IFN-gamma mRNA were quantified by real-time RT-PCR (2^-ddCT). IL-2 mRNA was significantly higher in MS patients than controls after both peptides (p<0.05), and IFN-gamma mRNA was significantly increased in MS patients after EBNA1 (p<0.05). MTT assay showed no peptide cytotoxicity. The authors conclude EBV peptides reactivate immune cells, especially T lymphocytes, potentially contributing to MS-related inflammation.

Rahimi et al 2026 Mult Scler Relat Disor.body: A case-control study from Southern Iran quantifying EBV viral load (EBNA-1 q-PCR), EBV-encoded miR-BART10-3p expression (q-RT-PCR), and EBV-VCA IgG serostatus (ELISA) in buffy coat from 80 MS patients (40 newly diagnosed treatment-naive, 20 interferon-beta treated, 20 B-cell-depleting mAb treated) and 30 healthy controls. EBV viral load and miR-BART10-3p were significantly elevated in newly diagnosed (ND-MS) and interferon-beta (MS-IFN) groups versus controls, but markedly suppressed in the B-cell-depletion (MS-mAb) group. EBV-VCA IgG seropositivity did not differ among groups. The authors conclude EBV viral load and miR-BART10-3p are promising, treatment-responsive biomarkers of EBV activity in MS.
Rahimi et al 2026 Mult Scler Relat Disor.identifier: Rahimi et al 2026 Mult Scler Relat Disord

Ramagopalan et al 2009 Neuroepidemiology.body: Population-based Canadian case-control study (CCPGSMS) of 14,362 MS index cases and 7,671 spouse controls, asking about childhood histories of measles, mumps, rubella, varicella and infectious mononucleosis plus several vaccinations. After sex stratification, no MS association was found for any vaccine or for measles/mumps/rubella/varicella, but a clinical history of infectious mononucleosis was strongly associated with MS (699 cases vs 165 controls; OR 2.06, 95% CI 1.71-2.48, p<0.001), implicating EBV in MS susceptibility. Males gave far more 'unknown' responses than females, confirming a sex-specific recall/reporting bias.

stats.qualifier: study analyzed the CCPGSMS case-control dataset

Ramagopalan et al 2011 Arch Neurol.body: A prospective cohort study (University of Edinburgh, 1999-2003) comparing 179 asymptomatic EBV seroconverters with 175 patients who developed infectious mononucleosis (IM), genotyping 5 classical HLA loci to test whether MS and IM share common HLA associations. HLA-DRB1*01:01 was the allele most significantly associated with IM (OR 2.49; with an extended cohort OR 3.2, P<.001), while no association was found with the strong MS risk allele HLA-DRB1*15. IM patients carrying HLA-DRB1*01:01 had lower EBV viral load (median 783 vs 7366 copies/10^6 PBMCs; P=.03). The authors conclude that MS and IM do not share a common HLA genetic basis, supporting a causal (not merely shared-genetic) role for EBV in MS.

Ramagopalan et al 2011 Neurology.body: Ecological study correlating geographic (28 English Strategic Health Authority) period prevalences of multiple sclerosis and infectious mononucleosis (from 1998-2005 Hospital Episode Statistics) with NASA Nimbus-7 satellite UVB (305 nm) intensity in England. MS prevalence was highly correlated with IM prevalence and inversely with seasonal UVB; regression of MS on all-season UVB gave r2=0.61, rising to r2=0.72 when adding an IM-by-seasonal-UVB interaction. The authors conclude UVB exposure and IM together explain much of the variance in MS, most plausibly through UVB-driven vitamin D synthesis modulating the response to EBV.

stats.qualifier: study population: English NHS hospital admissions, 51 million

Ramesh et al 2020 Proc Natl Acad Sci U S.body: Single-cell RNA-Seq, single-cell Ig-Seq, and bulk RNA-Seq of paired cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and blood B cells from relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS), other neurologic disease, and healthy control subjects. CSF B cells were ~13-fold enriched in RRMS vs healthy controls and were polarized toward an inflammatory, clonally expanded IgM+/IgG1+ memory and plasmablast/plasma cell phenotype with NF-kB and cholesterol biosynthesis pathway activation and down-regulated TGF-beta1 signaling. Clonal expansion of CSF B cells correlated with the CSF IgG index and gadolinium enhancement on MRI. Critically, using unbiased metagenomic sequencing the authors detected no EBV (or other viral) transcripts in MS blood or CSF B cell subsets, despite positive detection in an EBV-infected control cell line, arguing against constitutive EBV transcription in MS B cells.
Ramesh et al 2020 Proc Natl Acad Sci U S.identifier: Ramesh et al 2020 Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A

Rand et al 2000 J Neurol Sci.body: Using antigen-specific immunoblotting and isoelectric focusing of CSF, Rand et al. tested whether Epstein-Barr virus nuclear antigen-1 (EBNA-1) is a target of the oligoclonal bands (OCBs) in multiple sclerosis (MS). A distinctive oligoclonal EBNA-1-specific banding pattern co-migrating with total IgG OCBs was found in 5/15 MS patients but 0/12 controls (P=0.037), and CSF/serum antibody indices to EBNA-1 were markedly elevated in MS (averaging 11.4 in the five-patient subgroup) but not to VCA or varicella zoster. In one patient, EBNA-1 and the antigenically equivalent peptide p62 absorbed a kappa-bearing antibody clone, suggesting that in a subset of MS patients EBNA-1 is a major target of selected intrathecal OCBs.
Rand et al 2000 J Neurol Sci.identifier: Rand et al 2000 J Neurol Sci

Rang et al 2022 Mult Scler Relat Disord.body: A bioinformatics study integrating GEO transcriptomics datasets to dissect how Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-encoded microRNAs regulate multiple sclerosis (MS)-related genes in B cells. Among MS-related viruses (EBV, CMV, HIV, measles), EBV infection showed the strongest correlation with MS risk (p<1.0e-11). Integrating 284 MS susceptibility genes with 293 B-cell DEGs yielded 568 MS-related genes; 112 were EBV-regulated, and 33 of these were targets of 33 EBV miRNAs. The authors identified 15 target EBV miRNAs regulating 7 MS-related genes (MALT1, BCL10, IFNGR2, STAT3, CXCR4, PTK2B, FOXP1) acting through NF-kB (MALT1/BCL10) and PD-L1/PD-1 (IFNGR2/STAT3) pathways, and experimentally confirmed ebv-miR-BHRF1-2-5p directly targets MALT1.
Rang et al 2022 Mult Scler Relat Disord.identifier: Rang et al 2022 Mult Scler Relat Disord

Reijm et al 2026 iScience.body: Reijm et al. used spectral flow cytometry to compare HLA-B7-restricted (higher MS risk) and HLA-A2-restricted (lower MS risk) EBV- and CMV-specific CD8+ T cells in blood of healthy donors, untreated and natalizumab-treated people with MS, plus postmortem CNS compartments of one HLA-A2+B7+ MS donor. HLA-B7-restricted EBV-specific CD8+ T cells recognized almost solely the latent epitope EBNA3A(379-387), displayed a more exhausted phenotype (PD-1+CD244+CD160+KLRG1+TIGIT+), expressed brain-residency markers (CD20dim, CXCR3, CXCR6) and were most abundant in CNS compartments. Anti-EBNA1 and anti-VCA IgG titers were higher in HLA-B7+HLA-A2- pwMS, supporting a model where HLA-B7-restricted CD8+ T cells are less able to control EBV and more prone to infiltrate the CNS.

Ricigliano et al 2015 PLoS One.body: ChIP-seq overlap study testing whether the Epstein-Barr virus nuclear antigen 2 (EBNA2) preferentially binds genomic intervals associated with multiple sclerosis (MS) susceptibility. Using publicly available EBNA2, RBPJ and VDR ChIP-seq data in lymphoblastoid cell lines processed with the Genomic HyperBrowser, the authors found EBNA2 (O/E=5.392) and its co-factor RBPJ (O/E=6.841) bind MS susceptibility loci more than expected by chance, remaining significant after controlling for open-chromatin (DHS) confounders. EBNA2 occupancy strikingly overlaps VDR binding sites genome-wide (O/E=96.16), and EBNA2-VDR joint occupancy is preferentially enriched in MS regions, supporting that EBV participates in the gene-environment interactions predisposing to MS.

Rizzo et al 2016 Immunol Cell Biol.body: Longitudinal study of 35 RRMS patients showing that interferon-beta (IFN-beta) therapy specifically and markedly reduces circulating CD27+ memory B cells (with a concomitant increase in naive B cells), while leaving T cells and monocytes unchanged. The memory B-cell depletion is mediated by IFN-beta-induced FAS-receptor/FAS-L and TACI upregulation driving caspase-3-dependent apoptosis (increased Annexin-V and active caspase-3). Because CD27+ memory B cells are the reservoir of latent EBV, IFN-beta also reduced the elevated EBV LMP2A gene expression found in MS PBMCs (higher than healthy donors), with the LMP2A decrease correlating with memory B-cell reduction, suggesting a dual immunomodulatory and anti-viral action of IFN-beta in MS.

Rolls et al 2009 Eur Neurol.body: A UK case series (Rolls et al, Eur Neurol 2010;63:29-35) screening 1,987 MS patients across two NHS catchments for co-occurring lymphoma or nasopharyngeal carcinoma. It reports five patients with MS plus an EBV-associated malignancy (two with Hodgkin lymphoma, one with NHL, one with NPC and cervical cancer, plus one whose partner developed NHL), with most patients EBV EBNA1 IgG positive. Estimated incidence rates suggested heightened rates of HL and NPC (but not NHL) in MS patients, and the authors argue EBV is a common aetiological factor linking MS, lymphoma and NPC, while cautioning the associations may be due to chance.

Rostgaard et al 2023 Brain.body: A nationwide retrospective register-based cohort study of all 2,576,011 Danes born 1971-2018 (followed 1977-2018; 23,905 infectious mononucleosis and 4442 multiple sclerosis cases) testing whether sibship constellation affects multiple sclerosis (MS) risk in the same way it affects infectious mononucleosis (IM) risk, as an indirect test of the delayed-EBV-infection hypothesis. Using stratified Cox regression, hazard ratios for MS and IM per additional sibling could be assumed identical (test for homogeneity P=0.19), with maximum protection from a 0-2 years younger sibling (HR=0.80, 95% CI 0.76-0.85). The authors conclude that having siblings reduces MS risk by preventing delayed primary EBV infection, implying an EBV vaccine given before the teenage years could essentially eradicate MS.

Ruprecht et al 2014 J Neuroimmunol.body: Case-control peptide-microarray study (29 EBV-seropositive relapsing-remitting MS patients vs 22 EBV-seropositive healthy controls) profiling the epitope-resolved IgG antibody response to 8 full-length EBV proteins (1465 15-mer peptides). MS patients had higher antibody reactivities (p<0.001) to 39 EBV peptides: 17 from EBNA-1 (13 of them within the glycine-alanine repeat), plus peptides from EBNA-3, EBNA-4, EBNA-6, VP26, and LMP1, but none from BLRF2 or BZLF1. After Bonferroni correction, 3 peptides remained significant (EBNA-1_109-123, EBNA-1_214-228, EBNA-6_841-855); combined ROC AUC was 0.9 for discriminating MS from controls. The authors conclude the elevated anti-EBV antibody response in MS primarily targets, but is not confined to, the glycine-alanine repeat of EBNA-1.

Rød et al 2023 Mult Scler Relat Disord.body: A longitudinal substudy of the phase III Overlord-MS trial (NCT04578639) investigating how B cell depletion therapy (anti-CD20: rituximab or ocrelizumab) affects the humoral immune response to Epstein-Barr virus in 99 treatment-naive, newly diagnosed RRMS patients (290 serum samples) followed up to 18 months. Using mixed-effects models, EBNA1 IgG levels decreased by ~13% from 6 months onward while VCA IgG levels increased by ~14% from 3 months and persisted; CMV IgG and total IgG decreased modestly as controls. HLA-DRB1*15:01 carriers had higher baseline EBNA1 IgG, and circulating EBV-DNA was detectable in only 3 of 156 plasma samples. The authors conclude the mechanism of action of B cell depletion may involve modulating the EBV-specific response, mitigating immune cross-reactivity and disease perpetuation.
Rød et al 2023 Mult Scler Relat Disord.identifier: Rød et al 2023 Mult Scler Relat Disord

Røsjø et al 2016 Mult Scler.body: A 96-week randomised double-blinded placebo-controlled clinical trial (NCT00785473) testing high-dose oral vitamin D3 (20,000 IU/week) in 68 relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) patients, measuring serum IgG antibody levels against EBV antigens (EBNA1 whole protein and aa 385-420 fragment, VCA), CMV and VZV. Serum 25(OH)D more than doubled in the vitamin D group (123.2 vs 61.8 nmol/L placebo, p<0.001). Compared to placebo, anti-EBNA1 protein and fragment IgG decreased significantly from baseline to week 48 (p=0.038 and p=0.004) but the difference was no longer significant at week 96; antibodies against VCA, CMV and VZV were unaffected. The authors conclude vitamin D3 has a specific but possibly transient effect on humoral immunity against the latent EBV antigen EBNA1 in RRMS.

Sadam et al 2021 EBioMedicine.body: Using mimotope variation analysis (MVA), a next-generation phage display method, the authors profiled antibody epitope repertoires in serum/CSF of optic neuritis (ON) and multiple sclerosis (MS) patients across discovery (n=62), validation (n=20) and external (n=421) cohorts. They identified two highly immunogenic epitope clusters: A (mimicking CMV glycoprotein B AD2 epitope) and B (mimicking EBV viral capsid antigen p18 C-terminal epitope). Cluster B and EBNA1-aligning epitopes were enriched in ON patients who progressed to MS, and a two-epitope (A and B) biomarker model predicted MS with ON onset versus healthy controls at AUC 0.796 (75% sensitivity, 74.22% specificity) and versus non-demyelinating controls at AUC 0.82 (93.23% specificity).

Salzer et al 2013 Mult Scler.body: Prospective nested case-control study (192 MS cases, 384 matched controls) from northern Swedish biobanks assessing whether smoking (measured by serum cotinine, stratified at 10 ng/ml) and anti-EBNA-1 IgG reactivity interact statistically in conferring multiple sclerosis risk. Both high anti-EBNA-1 IgG and elevated cotinine were independently associated with increased MS risk, but no statistically significant interaction was found on additive or multiplicative scales. Stratifying by age at sampling, the data suggest a negative interaction in younger subjects (<26.4 years) and a positive interaction in older subjects, implying that divergent prior findings reflect differences in age at EBV assessment.

Salzer et al 2013 Mult Scler [6e02e9].body: Nested case-control study (n=192 prospectively-collected MS cases and n=384 matched controls from northern Swedish biobank cohorts) examining whether IgG antibody reactivity against EBNA-1 and five EBNA-1 domains predicts MS risk, and whether these antibodies confound or interact with 25-hydroxyvitamin D status. Risk of MS rose across tertiles of antibody reactivity against whole EBNA-1 and the EBNA-1(402-502) and EBNA-1(385-420) domains (p for trend <0.001), with the 385-420 domain conferring roughly a four-fold increased risk; the associations were stronger in young subjects (<26.4 years). 25(OH)D status did not confound the associations and no statistical interaction was found, but among young subjects 25(OH)D correlated inversely with EBNA-1 antibody reactivity (r about -0.13 to -0.35).

Santón et al 2011 Mult Scler.body: Molecular case-control study of 75 consecutive multiple sclerosis (MS) patients and 186 healthy Spanish controls in which EBV was simultaneously detected and typed by PCR amplifying a strain-specific sequence of the EBNA2 gene (160-bp for type 1, 176-bp for type 2). EBV was detected in 93.3% of MS patients vs 66.1% of controls, and MS was significantly associated with EBV presence (OR 7.171, 95% CI 2.755-18.667, p<0.001). Co-infection by both EBV type 1 and type 2 was found in 90% of MS patients vs 37.4% of controls and was significantly associated with MS (OR 15.065, 95% CI 6.362-35.675, p<0.001), providing molecular evidence linking type 1 and 2 EBV dual infection with MS.

Sargsyan et al 2010 Neurology.body: Sargsyan et al. used nested and real-time PCR, ELISA, and immunocytochemistry to search for latent and active EBV in MS brain and CSF. No EBV-encoded RNA (EBER-1) was detected in single MS CSF plasma cells or B-lymphocytes, and EBER-1/EBNA-2/LMP-1/BFRF-1 were absent in all 15 MS plaques; only rare EBER-1 was seen in the few EBV-DNA-positive plaques (type 0 latency). Intrathecal anti-EBV antibody synthesis did not differ between MS (3/20) and non-MS inflammatory controls (2/5; p=0.25), and 32 recombinant antibodies from clonally expanded MS CSF plasma cells did not bind EBV-infected cells. The authors conclude there is no evidence of active EBV infection or an MS-specific intrathecal anti-EBV response, arguing against a role for EBV in MS brain pathogenesis.

Sarkkinen et al 2025 JCI Insight.body: Using cyclic multiplex immunofluorescence (mfIHC) and single-cell spatial imaging of FFPE lymph nodes from 33 patients with multiple sclerosis (pwMS) and 35 non-MS controls (plus 5 prediagnostic preMS cases; ~2.4 million cells), this study shows that follicular T helper (Tfh) and Tfh-like cells are expanded in MS lymph nodes, accumulate in the mantle zone and follicles, and have increased spatial interactions with follicular, naive, and germinal-center B cells. The Tfh-to-Tfr (T follicular regulator) ratio is increased in the mantle zone, indicating reduced regulatory control, and these changes are already detectable before clinical MS diagnosis. EBER in situ hybridization and multiplex qPCR found no signs of EBV latency in lymph nodes of either pwMS or controls.

Sarkkinen et al 2025 Sci Immunol.body: Single-cell RNA-seq, CITE-seq, BCR/TCR sequencing, hybrid-capture viral sequencing, and saliva qPCR characterization of deep cervical lymph node (dcLN) fine-needle aspirations from nine newly diagnosed untreated patients with MS and seven healthy controls. The authors found an expanded memory B cell compartment with increased double-negative (DN) memory B cells and reduced, less-clonal germinal center (GC) B cells and GC T follicular helper cells in pwMS. DN and a GC.B subset transcriptionally resembled lytic EBV-infected lymphoblastoid cell lines, EBV-targeting clonally expanded memory CD8 T cells (against EBNA3B and BMLF1) were enriched in a subset of patients, and EBV DNA was elevated in patient dcLNs and saliva, implicating EBV-driven B cell dysregulation in MS pathogenesis.

Sattarnezhad et al 2025 Proc Natl Acad S.body: Case-control study of 650 MS patients and 661 matched population controls from the Swedish EIMS cohort using a bead-based multiplex serology assay. Elevated IgG against EBNA1 and the three CNS mimic antigens GlialCAM, CRYAB, and ANO2 associate with increased MS risk; competitive blocking confirms cross-reactive antibodies and molecular mimicry between EBNA1 and GlialCAM, with epitope spreading across adjacent peptides. Antibody reactivities are higher in HLA-DRB1*15:01 carriers, and combinations of HLA-DRB1*15:01 with anti-EBNA1 plus a CNS-mimic antibody raise MS risk additively (OR up to ~9.4-10), while absence of protective HLA-A*02:01 adds further risk.
Sattarnezhad et al 2025 Proc Natl Acad S.identifier: Sattarnezhad et al 2025 Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A

Schneider-Hohendorf et al 2022 J Exp Med.body: TCRb repertoire study querying peripheral blood of 1,395 MS patients, 887 controls, and 35 monozygotic MS-discordant twin pairs (plus COVID-19 positive controls) for multimer-confirmed, MHC-I-restricted, viral antigen-specific TCRb sequences. MS patients harbored more EBV-specific (but not CMV-, SARS-CoV-2-, or influenza A-specific) TCRb sequences across discovery, validation, and twin cohorts, indicating a broader EBV-specific CD8 T cell repertoire independent of genetics/environment. Anti-VLA-4 (natalizumab) treatment amplified peripheral EBV-specific T cells, whereas IFNb and anti-CD20 did not. scRNAseq showed EBV-specific CD8 T cells are effector-memory in healthy CSF but include central-memory cells directed predominantly at lytic epitopes in MS CSF, suggesting recent priming and an ongoing anti-EBV immune reaction in MS.
Schneider-Hohendorf et al 2022 J Exp Med.identifier: Schneider-Hohendorf et al 2022 J Exp Med

Schneider-Hohendorf et al 2025 Brain.body: Analysis of peripheral blood T-cell receptor beta chain (TRB) repertoires (n=1317 samples) showing that the broader MHC-I-restricted EBV-specific CD8+ TRB repertoire is specific to multiple sclerosis and is not seen in the MS differential diagnoses NMOSD, MOGAD or Susac's syndrome. EBV-specific TRB sequence matches spiked alongside EBV reactivation/reinfection during immune reconstitution after autologous haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation. Longitudinal cohorts showed that ocrelizumab, teriflunomide and dimethyl fumarate, but not glatiramer acetate or interferon beta, reduced EBV-specific (but not CMV-specific) TRB sequence matches, suggesting the aberrant anti-EBV T-cell response is MS-specific and modifiable by treatment.

Sebastian et al 2021 Neurology.body: Multicenter US case-control study (332 pediatric MS cases, 534 age- and sex-matched controls) testing sun exposure and ambient UVR as risk factors for pediatric-onset MS. Greater time spent outdoors during summer and higher ambient summer UVR dose were associated with markedly reduced odds of MS in a dose-dependent manner (1-2 h/day outdoors AOR 0.19; summer UVR AOR 0.76 per kJ/m2). Higher anti-EBV VCA IgG antibody levels were independently associated with greater odds of MS (AOR 1.45 per unit), consistent with EBV as an MS risk factor; tobacco smoke exposure and overweight were also more common in cases.

Serafini et al 2007 J Exp Med.body: Serafini et al. investigated EBV markers in postmortem brain tissue from 22 MS patients with different clinical courses. Contrary to prior studies, they found EBV infection (EBER, latent proteins EBNA2/LMP1, lytic protein BFRF1) in brain-infiltrating B cells and plasma cells in nearly 100% of MS cases (21 of 22) but not in other inflammatory neurological diseases. Ectopic B cell follicles in the meninges of secondary progressive MS cases were identified as major sites of EBV persistence and reactivation, and activated cytotoxic CD8+ T cells accumulated at sites of EBV-infected cells, with perforin polarized toward plasma cells, supporting a role for EBV persistence and reactivation in MS immunopathology.
Serafini et al 2007 J Exp Med.identifier: Serafini et al 2007 J Exp Med

Serafini et al 2010 J Neuropathol Exp Ne.body: Postmortem study of secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (MS) brain tissue investigating EBV latency programs and their link to intrathecal B-cell activation. By immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, laser-capture microdissection, and preamplification real-time RT-PCR, the authors show that a large proportion of CD27+ memory B cells infiltrating MS white matter lesions, meninges, and ectopic B-cell follicles express the EBV latency proteins LMP-2A and LMP-1 and that LMP-2A and EBNA-1 transcripts are detectable in B-cell-containing regions, indicating EBV uses the latency II program in the MS brain. They further show that BAFF is produced by EBV-infected B cells (and reactive astrocytes), suggesting EBV-driven, BAFF-amplified chronic B-cell activation contributes to viral persistence and possible disruption of B-cell tolerance.
Serafini et al 2010 J Neuropathol Exp Ne.identifier: Serafini et al 2010 J Neuropathol Exp Neurol

Serafini et al 2019 J Virol.body: Postmortem in situ MHC class I pentamer study of 18 brain tissue blocks from 12 progressive MS donors testing whether EBV-specific CD8 T cells infiltrate the MS brain. CD8 T cells recognizing latent (EBNA3A, EBNA3C, LMP1, LMP2) and lytic (BZLF1, BRLF1, BMLF1, BMRF1, BALF4) EBV antigens were visualized in white matter lesions and meninges of 11/12 donors (median 0.5-2.5% of CNS-infiltrating CD8 T cells), significantly more frequent than CMV-specific cells (detected in 4/12, <=0.3%), while influenza- and MBP-specific CD8 T cells were undetectable. EBV-specific CD8 T cells were CD107a-positive (cytotoxic phenotype) and made tight contacts with LMP2A+ and CD20+ EBV-infected B cells, supporting a virus-driven CD8 T-cell immunopathological mechanism in MS.

Serafini et al 2023 J Neuroimmunol.body: Immunohistochemical study of postmortem brain tissue from 16 progressive multiple sclerosis cases, 4 non-inflammatory neurological disease cases, and 5 non-neurological controls, characterizing tissue-resident memory (Trm) T-cell markers CD103 and CD69 in CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in the white matter and meninges. CD103 and/or CD69 were expressed mainly by a subset of CD8+ T cells that intermingled with and contacted EBV-infected (EBER+, CD20+, BZLF1+) B cells in infiltrated MS white matter perivascular cuffs and meningeal B-cell follicles. Some Trm-like cells expressed granzyme B and PD-1, mainly in white matter lesions. The authors conclude that CNS Trm cells could fail to constrain EBV infection while contributing to sustained inflammation in the MS brain.

Serafini et al 2024 J Neuroimmunol.body: Immunohistochemical study of the immune checkpoint molecule PD-L1 and its receptor PD-1 in postmortem brain tissue from six progressive multiple sclerosis (MS) cases and four non-neurological controls. PD-L1 was expressed by a fraction of CNS-infiltrating B cells and by most EBV latently infected (LMP2A+) B cells in white matter perivascular cuffs and meningeal B cell follicles, while PD-1 was expressed on many CD8+ T cells (including virtually all EBV-specific, EBNA3A/BZLF1 pentamer+ CD8+ T cells) and fewer CD4+ T cells. PD-1+ T cells were in direct contact with PD-L1+ and EBV-infected cells. The authors conclude that PD-L1 expression by EBV-infected B cells could favour local immune evasion, EBV persistence, and immunopathology in the MS brain.

Severa et al 2019 J Autoimmun.body: Using an Interferome-based, cell type-specific transcriptomic approach on freshly isolated B cells and monocytes from therapy-free RRMS patients vs matched healthy donors, the study found dysregulated IFN-regulated genes driving pathogenic features. MS B cells and monocytes show increased caspase-3-dependent apoptosis; MS monocytes over-express STAT3 and IL-16 (caspase-3 cleaves STAT3 N-terminus and pro-IL-16 into bioactive IL-16, a CD4+ T-cell chemoattractant); MS B cells have a multi-level defect in type I IFN signaling (low IRF7, OAS1, SP110, AIM2, MyD88, IFNAR1/2 and weak STAT1/2 activation). Consequently MS B cells less efficiently control in vitro EBV infection (higher EBV-GFP+ cells, EBER-1 and BZLF1), an effect partly rescued by IFN-beta.

Simon et al 2010 Neurology.body: Pooled individual-level analysis of 3 MS case-control studies (Nurses' Health Studies, Tasmanian MS Study, Swedish MS Study; 442 cases, 865 controls) examining the interplay between cigarette smoking, serum anti-EBNA antibody titers, and HLA-DR15 on multiple sclerosis risk. Higher anti-EBNA titers, HLA-DR15 positivity, and ever smoking were each associated with increased MS risk. The increased MS risk from high anti-EBNA titers was about twice as strong in ever smokers as never smokers (interaction p=0.001), and the smoking-MS association vanished after adjusting for anti-EBNA titers, suggesting a super-multiplicative smoking x EBV interaction. HLA-DR15 effects were independent of both smoking and anti-EBNA titer.

Simon et al 2011 Acta Neurol Scand.body: Nested case-control study within the Nurses' Health Study (NHS/NHS II) that sequenced the polymorphic N- and C-terminus regions of EBV EBNA1 and the hyper-variable C-terminal region of LMP1 from EBV DNA isolated from peripheral lymphocytes of 66 MS cases and 66 age- and cohort-matched controls. Comparing prototype (B95.8) versus mutant sequences and the presence of multiple strains, the authors found no significant differences between cases and controls for EBNA1 N-terminal (P=0.35), EBNA1 C-terminal (P=0.07) or any LMP1 variant (all P>0.05). EBNA1 and LMP1 variation was also not associated with anti-EBNA1 IgG antibody titers. The findings do not support a role for EBV strain variation in EBNA1 or LMP1 in MS risk.
Simon et al 2011 Acta Neurol Scand.identifier: Simon et al 2011 Acta Neurol Scand

Simon et al 2012 Mult Scler.body: Nested case-control study within the Nurses' Health Study (NHS) and NHS II cohorts examining whether EBV neutralizing antibody capacity (anti-gp350 neutralization, measured by competition ELISA against monoclonal antibody 72A1) in pre-diagnosis serum predicts subsequent multiple sclerosis risk. Among 31 women with pre-diagnosis blood (18 drawn before symptom onset), higher EBV neutralizing antibody titers tended to be associated with INCREASED rather than decreased MS risk (RR=2.2, 95% CI 0.97-5.1, p=0.06), contrary to the hypothesis. The association was attenuated after adjustment for anti-EBNA1 IgG titers (RR=1.4, 95% CI 0.5-3.5), suggesting EBV neutralizing antibody measurement is unlikely to contribute substantially to MS risk prediction; the underpowered study warrants confirmation in larger samples.

stats.qualifier: nested case-control study in NHS/NHS II testing pre-diagnosis EBV neutralizing antibodies and MS risk

Simon et al 2014 Mult Scler.body: Case-control study in the Accelerated Cure Project (ACP) Repository (1190 MS, 97 NMO, 124 TM, 454 controls) testing whether established MS risk factors (history of infectious mononucleosis, anti-EBNA1 IgG titers, HLA-DR15, smoking) are also associated with neuromyelitis optica (NMO) or transverse myelitis (TM). All four factors plus female sex were associated with MS as expected, with no significant interactions (supporting a multiplicative model). In contrast, anti-EBNA1 titers were not associated with NMO or TM, HLA-DR15 was not associated with NMO or TM, and smoking was inversely associated with NMO; a history of IM was associated with TM (OR=1.8). EBV seropositivity was marginally more common in NMO and TM than controls. The authors conclude established MS risk factors do not appear to drive susceptibility to NMO or TM, and act independently in MS.

stats.qualifier: case-control study of MS, NMO, TM risk factors in the ACP Repository

Simon et al 2014 Mult Scler Relat Disord.body: A case-control study of 1213 MS cases and 454 controls from the Accelerated Cure Project for MS Repository testing whether candidate SNPs in HLA-A, SH2D1A and IL15RA (genes linked to EBV infection or infectious mononucleosis susceptibility) are associated with odds of MS, history of infectious mononucleosis (IM), or anti-EBNA1 IgG antibody titer. No SNP was significantly associated with MS, IM, or anti-EBNA1 titer after multiple-comparison correction; the HLA-A rs6457110 'A' allele showed a non-significant decreased odds of MS (OR=0.86) consistent with prior literature. The authors conclude these polymorphisms are unlikely to explain the known association between IM/anti-EBNA1 titer and MS.
Simon et al 2014 Mult Scler Relat Disord.identifier: Simon et al 2014 Mult Scler Relat Disord

Simon et al 2014 Mult Scler Relat Disord.body: Case-control study (1213 MS cases, 454 controls from the Accelerated Cure Project for MS Repository) testing whether candidate SNPs in HLA-A, SH2D1A and IL15RA chosen for their role in EBV infection or infectious mononucleosis (IM) susceptibility are associated with MS risk, history of IM, or anti-EBNA1 IgG antibody titer. After correction for multiple comparisons no SNP was significantly associated with odds of MS, IM, or anti-EBNA1 titer. The HLA-A tag SNP rs6457110 'A' allele showed a non-significant decrease in MS odds (OR=0.86, 95% CI 0.72-1.02) consistent with prior reports, and the HLA-DRB1*15:01 surrogate SNP rs3135005 was not associated with IM. The authors conclude these polymorphisms are unlikely to explain the established association between EBV/IM and MS.

Simpson‐Yap et al 2025 Ann Neurol.body: Two MS case-control studies (Ausimmune, Australia: 206 cases/348 controls; EIMS, Sweden: 140 cases/139 controls) tested whether differential DNA methylation (DNAm) modules mediate the associations of canonical MS risk factors with MS onset. EBV indices (infectious mononucleosis history and anti-EBNA IgG titer), lower serum 25(OH)D, low sun exposure, and the HLA-DRB1*1501 risk variant were individually and jointly (synergistically) associated with MS risk. In each study, 2 DNAm modules (A1/A2 in Ausimmune via WGCNA; E1/E2 in EIMS via sPLS-DA) mediated 21-53% of these exposure-MS associations, were enriched for GWAS MS risk genes, and shared cross-study pathways (interferon alpha/beta, B-cell receptor signaling, NOTCH, RAC1 GTPase, MHC class II). The authors conclude EBV, low vitamin D, low sun, and HLA-DRB1*1501 act in concert through common epigenetic pathways to drive MS onset.

Sisay et al 2017 J Neuroimmunol.body: Case-control study measuring anti-EBNA-1 IgG antibodies and pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-8, IL-1beta, IL-6, IL-10, TNF-alpha, IL-12p70) in paired serum and CSF from 20 untreated relapsing-remitting MS patients and 17 healthy controls. Serum anti-EBNA-1 IgG and IL-8 were significantly higher in RRMS patients than controls. Anti-EBNA-1 antibody levels were higher in serum than CSF (periphery), whereas IL-8 (and IL-6) relative to total protein were preferentially elevated in CSF, implicating peripheral anti-EBV humoral responses and CNS-localized innate inflammation; serum and CSF levels of both markers correlated strongly.

SoRelle et al 2025 JCI Insight.body: Single-cell RNA-Seq + CITE-Seq and flow cytometry analysis of peripheral B cells from an early MS (eMS/CIS) cohort from the Immune Tolerance Network STAyCIS Trial, integrated with public scRNA-Seq from autoimmune diseases, chronic infections, healthy controls, and in vitro EBV infection. CD19+CD20+CD21loCD11c+T-bet+ atypical B cells (ABCs) were significantly enriched in early MS versus healthy controls and expressed an EBV-induced gene signature (including CXCR3, PD-L1, PD-L2, inflammatory cytokines CXCL8/IL18/VEGFA), enriched specifically in people who experienced subsequent MS activity. EBV transcripts were not directly detected in clinical samples, suggesting ABC expansion may be a bystander response to EBV.

Soldan et al 2024 Nat Microbiol.body: Soldan et al. characterized spontaneous lymphoblastoid cell lines (SLCLs) isolated ex vivo from multiple sclerosis (MS) patients (active, AMS; stable, SMS) and healthy controls to study endogenous EBV and host gene expression. SLCLs from patients with active MS had higher EBV lytic gene expression (Zta/EA-D), higher viral loads, increased genomic heterogeneity, compromised EBNA1 DNA binding, and an inflammatory host gene-expression profile (hypercytokinemia, interferon and IL-12/Th1 signalling, FOXP1 and CD44 up, HAVCR2 down). FOXP1 knockdown reduced EBV lytic gene expression and viral load, while LTA/TNF-beta supported EBV latency and B-cell survival. The antiviral tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) reduced EBV lytic gene expression, inflammatory cytokine production and autologous CD4+ T-cell responses without inducing cell death.

St-Sauver et al 2026 Neurology.body: A population-based retrospective cohort study using the Rochester Epidemiology Project (1998-2022) that assessed whether laboratory-confirmed EBV-positive infectious mononucleosis (IM) increases the risk of developing verified multiple sclerosis (MS). Among 4,721 EBV-positive IM cases and 14,163 age- and sex-matched referents, MS developed in 8 exposed (0.17%) vs 10 referents (0.07%). After adjustment for race, ethnicity, ADI, smoking, and Elixhauser comorbidity, EBV-positive IM was associated with a >3-fold increased risk of MS (adjusted HR 3.14, 95% CI 1.18-8.34), while risk of death did not differ (HR 1.00, 95% CI 0.65-1.50).

Strautins et al 2013 Mult Scler.body: Population-based case-control study of 426 MS patients (Perth Demyelinating Disease Database) and 186 healthy controls (Busselton, Western Australia) assessing how anti-EBV antibody levels combine with HLA-DR risk profiles, gender and age to stratify MS risk. MS cases had significantly higher anti-EBNA-1 (polyspecific 'long' and epitope-specific 'short') and anti-VCA IgG than controls (all p<10^-15). In logistic regression, anti-EBNA-1, anti-VCA, protective HLA-DR alleles and female gender independently classified cases/controls with an OR>20 (sensitivity 92%, specificity 64%, C-statistic 0.885); the strong effect of high-risk HLA-DR alleles was abrogated once EBV serology was included.

Sundqvist et al 2012 Neurology.body: Swedish EIMS case-control study (552 cases / 625 controls for serology+HLA+smoking) that attempted to replicate Simon et al. 2010's reported multiplicative-scale interaction between EBNA1 IgG and cigarette smoking in MS risk. The study confirmed independent MS associations for EBNA1 IgG, HLA-DRB1*15, absence of HLA-A*02, smoking, and infectious mononucleosis, but found NO interaction between EBNA1 IgG and smoking on either scale (failed replication). It did observe additive-scale interactions between EBNA1 IgG and DRB1*15 (AP=0.34) and between EBNA1 IgG and absence of A*02 (AP=0.36); individuals with all 4 risk factors had a 26-fold increased MS risk.

Sundqvist et al 2019 Genes Immun.body: Swedish population-based case-control study (EIMS) of newly diagnosed MS cases and matched controls testing interactions between anti-EBV antibodies, history of infectious mononucleosis, and HLA risk factors (presence of DRB1*15, absence of A*02). Infectious mononucleosis (OR=1.89) and raised EBNA1 IgG (OR=1.74) were associated with MS, and anti-EBNA1 385-420 fragment IgG was the strongest serological risk marker (OR=3.79). EBNA1 385-420 IgG showed significant additive-scale interaction with both DRB1*15 (AP=0.60) and absence of A*02 (AP=0.39); individuals carrying all three risk factors had a 16-fold increased MS risk (OR=16.03). The authors conclude HLA class I/II influence on MS risk may partly act through immune control of EBV infection.

Sundström et al 2004 Neurology.body: A nested case-control study using two Swedish population-based serum biobanks compared IgG antibody responses to EBV (EBNA-1, VCA), HHV-6, HSV, VZV, and measles in prospectively (n=73) and retrospectively (n=161) collected sera from MS cases versus matched referents. All MS cases showed signs of past EBV infection. High anti-EBNA-1 IgG activity significantly increased MS risk (multivariate OR=4.5 prospective; OR=11 within 5 years before relapsing-remitting onset), while high anti-VCA activity significantly decreased MS risk in samples collected <5 years before onset (OR=0.16). High HHV-6 antibody activity also increased MS risk (OR=2.3 overall; OR=12 within 5 years). The authors conclude that future MS patients exhibit an altered anti-EBV immune response (high EBNA-1 without high VCA), most pronounced in the 5 years preceding MS onset, with no support for major causal roles of HSV, VZV, or measles.

Sundström et al 2008 Mult Scler.body: A Swedish (Västerbotten/NSHDS biobank) case-control study of 109 MS cases and 212 matched referents examining the interaction between the two best-documented MS risk factors: elevated anti-EBNA-1 antibody reactivity and HLA DRB1*1501 positivity. Multivariate logistic regression showed both were statistically independent risk factors for MS in both sexes (EBNA-1 high vs low OR=9.4; DRB1*1501 OR=2.8). HLA DRB1*1501-positive referents had higher median EBNA-1 reactivity than HLA-negative referents (138 vs 127, P=0.002), and less EBNA-1 reactivity was required to raise MS risk in DRB1*1501-positives, suggesting these individuals have increased vulnerability to EBV-induced autoimmunity.

Sundström et al 2009 J Neuroimmunol.body: A case-referent study (108 MS cases, 207 matched referents; screening subset of 25 case-referent pairs) investigating epitope-specific plasma IgG reactivity against domains of the Epstein-Barr virus protein EBNA-1 and its interaction with HLA DRB1*1501 status as risk factors for multiple sclerosis. Using in-house ELISA against thioredoxin-EBNA-1 fusion fragments and linear-peptide blocking, MS cases had increased antibody reactivity to several EBNA-1 domains. Antibody reactivity to EBNA-1 amino acids 385-420 was most strongly associated with MS (OR=12, 95% CI 4.3-33), and the combination of high anti-EBNA-1 (385-420) reactivity with HLA DRB1*1501 positivity conferred a 24-fold increased risk, suggesting a role for molecular mimicry between EBNA-1 and CNS antigens.

Tao et al 2022 Mult Scler Relat Disord.body: Prospective multicentre Australian cohort (Ausimmune/AusLong) of 205 first-clinical-demyelination cases with baseline EBV and HHV-6 serology/viral-load data, followed for 5 years to assess associations with conversion to MS, relapse, and EDSS/MSSS disability progression. Higher anti-HHV-6 IgG (>40) showed borderline-significant increased risk of MS conversion (aHR 1.48) and relapse (aHR 1.61) and was significantly associated with greater disability progression (MSSS), while a history of infectious mononucleosis trended with higher relapse but not conversion. EBV serological markers were largely unassociated, except anti-EBV-EA-D IgG which was inversely (protectively) associated with annualised EDSS/MSSS progression.

Teymoori-Rad et al 2020 J Neurovirol.body: An in vitro case-control study of 15 MS patients and 15 age/sex-matched healthy controls (Tehran) evaluating the interplay of EBV infection and vitamin D on immune response. MS patients showed significantly higher plasma 1,25-(OH)2D (p=0.02) but not 25-OHD, higher EBV DNA load in PBMCs (p=0.04), and lower VDR expression (p=0.04) versus controls, with an inverse correlation between VDR expression and EBV load (higher EBV load in low-VDR patients). In vitro EBV-infected PBMCs from MS patients produced significantly more IFN-gamma (p=0.02) and IL-10 (p=0.002) than controls; in vitro vitamin D (1,25-(OH)2D) reduced IFN-gamma production in all treated cells but did not change IL-10. The authors conclude EBV and vitamin D exert opposite in vitro effects on immune dysregulation in MS.

Thomas et al 2023 Sci Adv.body: Case-control serology and immunology study in a Swedish cohort (713 pwMS, 722 controls) examining antibody and T-cell cross-reactivity between EBV nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA1) and the CNS heat-shock protein alpha-crystallin B (CRYAB). Anti-CRYAB IgG targeting CRYAB amino acids 7-16 was associated with MS (OR 2.0), and combining high anti-EBNA1393-412 with CRYAB positivity markedly raised MS risk (OR 9.0). Antibody-blocking experiments showed cross-reactivity at a shared RRPFF motif (CRYAB 11-15 / EBNA1 402-406), mouse immunization showed reciprocal T-cell cross-priming between EBNA1 and CRYAB, and natalizumab-treated pwMS had increased proinflammatory CRYAB- and EBNA1-specific CD4+ memory T cells, supporting molecular mimicry as a mechanistic link between EBV and MS.

Thomas et al 2024 PLoS Pathog.body: A case-control immunological study comparing EBV antibody and T cell responses in untreated relapsing-remitting MS patients (n=31), HLA-DRB1*15:01-matched healthy controls (n=33) and post-infectious-mononucleosis donors (n=11). EBV genome load in PBMC was unchanged between MS and HC, but plasma IgG responses to EBNA1, VCA, EBNA2 and EBNA3 family antigens were elevated/more frequent in MS, while tetanus toxoid responses were unchanged. EBV-specific T cell responses were only subtly altered, but in vitro WT-LCL-expanded polyclonal T cell lines from both MS and HC showed high reactivity (especially CD8+) to CNS autoantigens (MOG, MBP, PLP, MOBP, TAL-H), and dual EBNA1/MOG-reactive T cell clones were isolated from one MS donor, supporting EBV-CNS molecular mimicry.

Thomas et al 2025 Cell.body: Thomas et al. show that anoctamin-2 (ANO2)-specific CD4+ T cells are present in ~57% of persons with MS and are cross-reactive with Epstein-Barr virus nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA1). Immunization of mice with ANO2 or EBNA1 primed cross-reactive CD4+ T cell and antibody responses, and ANO2 pre-immunization or adoptive transfer of ANO2-specific CD4+ T cells (but not ANO2 antibodies) exacerbated experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE). Single-cell TCR sequencing of T cells from natalizumab-treated pwMS revealed significant overlap between EBNA1- and ANO2-reactive CD4+ TCR repertoires, restricted by HLA-DRB1*15:01/HLA-DRB5*01:01, providing the first mechanistic evidence linking EBV infection to the MS autoantigen ANO2 and neuroinflammation.

Torkildsen et al 2007 Eur J Neurol.body: A 1-year prospective study of 61 patients with definite relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) testing whether EBV reactivation drives MS exacerbations. All patients had serological evidence of prior EBV infection (100% anti-VCA IgG positive, 98% anti-EBNA IgG positive). Quantitative anti-EA-D IgG ratios in 23 baseline-paired exacerbation samples showed no change at exacerbation (Wilcoxon P=0.58) and no interferon-vs-placebo difference (P=0.33), indicating EBV reactivation does not play a significant role in RRMS exacerbations.

Torkildsen et al 2010 Brain Pathol.body: Postmortem microarray gene-expression study of cortical gray matter (lesions and normal-appearing gray matter) from MS patients versus controls. The authors found a massive upregulation of immunoglobulin-related genes in MS cortex (validated by qPCR for IGKC, IGHG1 and IGKV4-1) and, by immunohistochemistry, Ig deposition with CD138-positive plasma cells in the meninges of MS patients but not controls. No EBV latent (LMP1, LMP2, EBNA1, EBNA2) or lytic (BZLF1) transcripts or proteins were detected by qPCR or immunohistochemistry. They conclude the Ig upregulation is driven by a small number of meningeal plasma cells, not EBV-infected B-cells, and that CSF OCB-producing B-cells may be of meningeal origin.

Trend et al 2020 Front Immunol.body: Case-control flow cytometry study of CD32b (FcgammaRIIb) expression on peripheral B cell subsets in 22 people with clinically isolated syndrome (CIS) or multiple sclerosis (MS) versus 16 healthy controls. Females (but not males) with CIS or MS had significantly lower CD32b expression on total, naive and IgM(hi) marginal-zone-like B cells than control females. Lower CD32b on these subsets was associated with anti-EBV viral capsid antigen (VCA) IgM seropositivity (36% of patients) and higher serum BAFF and IgM. In controls, CD32b mediated IgG immune-complex inhibition of TLR7(R848)-induced TNF in naive and IgM(hi) MZ-like B cells, but no functional consequence of the lower CD32b was detected in patients.

Tschochner et al 2016 PLoS One.body: Tschochner et al sequenced autologous EBNA-1 (Epstein-Barr Nuclear Antigen-1) directly from buffy coat DNA of 73-79 Western Australian multiple sclerosis (MS) patients using Sanger and 454 FLX sequencing, finding limited EBNA-1 sequence variation (no multiple-strain evidence; 8.3% of nucleotide positions variant at a 1% FLX cut-off) that diverged from the B95-8 laboratory strain. In silico HLA-DRB1*1501 epitope mapping confirmed two known restricted epitopes (AEG aa 481-496 and MVF aa 562-577) plus two putative epitopes (502-543), and eight of nine viral polymorphic sites significantly associated with MS HLA risk alleles fell within these HLA-DRB1 binding regions. Cross-reactivity (molecular mimicry) analysis predicted shared HLA-DRB1*15-binding homology between EBNA-1 epitopes and major myelin/axoglial CNS antigens including CNP, alpha-B-crystallin, MBP, MOG, oligodendrocyte-specific protein, glial fibrillary acidic protein, neurofascin, contactin-associated protein and gelsolin, supporting an EBNA-1-driven cross-reactive autoimmune model of MS.

Tørring et al 2014 Acta Neurol Scand.body: Case-control study of 21 relapsing-remitting MS patients and 21 age/sex-matched healthy controls examining B-cell subsets (flow cytometry) and spontaneous EBV-driven lymphocyte transformation over 16 weeks of culture. MS patients had a normal distribution of B-cell subsets (naive, switched/non-switched memory, B1 cells, T cells, monocytes all non-significant) but a significantly higher incidence of spontaneous B-cell transformation events (14.8% vs 7.4% of wells; OR 2.56, 95% CI 1.65-3.95, P<0.000), confirmed as EBV by EBNA-1 qPCR. Transformation kinetics were similar between groups (peak weeks 2-4), suggesting MS patients harbour an increased frequency of latent EBV-infected B cells rather than a faster reactivation kinetics.

Umeton et al 2022 Sci Rep.body: A bioinformatics colocalization study testing whether MS-associated GWAS variants fall within genomic regions coding for the transient transcriptome (trRNAs) and DNA binding regions (DBRs) of MS-relevant molecular transducers. Using LOLA/Fisher's exact tests on GWAS Catalog MS regions (603 SNPs, trait EFO_0003885), the authors show that MS GWAS variants are significantly enriched in the T-cell transient transcriptome (especially short half-life transcripts) and that DBRs for VDR, EBNA2 and AID (but EBNA3C only weakly) significantly colocalize with MS GWAS regions and trRNA-coding DNA. They define 'hotspots' where multiple transducers converge and use Activity-By-Contact mapping to link these hotspots to candidate genes, providing a public resource at www.mscoloc.com.

Varvatsi et al 2021 Mult Scler Relat Dis.body: Case-control study from Cyprus (30 clinically definite MS patients vs 33 healthy controls) that partially Sanger-sequenced seven latently expressed, highly polymorphic EBV genes (EBNA-1, EBNA-2, EBNA-3A/3B/3C, LMP-1, LMP-2A) from B-cell-derived EBV genomic DNA. 26 EBV variants were detected; 17 were significantly enriched in MS and 9 in controls. At the allele level, the EBNA3B2.1 (p=0.0008) and LMP1.1 (p=0.01) alleles were associated with increased MS risk, while EBNA1.3 (p=0.005), EBNA2.1 (p=0.001) and EBNA3B2.2 (p=0.0003) alleles were enriched in controls and appeared protective. A 60 bp EBNA-3B deletion (68% MS vs 7% HC) and a 30 bp LMP-1 Cao deletion (42.8% MS vs 0% HC) were among the strongest MS-associated variants.
Varvatsi et al 2021 Mult Scler Relat Dis.identifier: Varvatsi et al 2021 Mult Scler Relat Disord

Vasilenko et al 2024 Front Immunol.body: Retrospective cross-sectional case-control multiplex serology study of 258 serum samples (EBV-negative and EBV-positive controls, untreated RRMS with/without relapse, SPMS, PPMS, and 8 treatment groups) measuring IgG and IgM antibodies against EBV lifecycle proteins (docking gp350/220, fusion gh/gp42 and gh/gL/gp42, immediate early BZLF1, early antigens, VCA capsid antigens, EBNA1) and putative cross-reactive EBNA1, GlialCAM, CRYAB and ANO2 peptides. IgG titers were significantly elevated in EBV-positive controls and all MS groups vs EBV-negative controls for nearly all lifecycle antigens; RRMS patients had significantly higher titers than EBV-positive controls for gh/gp42 and gh/gL/gp42 fusion proteins and certain EBNA1 peptides; an MS-specific anti-ANO2 response was found but not for GlialCAM or CRYAB. No significant treatment effects and no specific IgM (reactivation) response were detected, arguing against EBV reactivation as a driver of MS activity.

Vaughan et al 1996 J Neuroimmunol.body: In a Norwegian case-control series (35 definite MS patients vs 36 hospital controls from the Riise et al. 1991 cohort), MS sera had significantly elevated IgG antibodies to the EBNA-1 glycine/alanine repeat (anti-P62) and to a cross-reactive lymphocyte autoantigen p542. Anti-P62 was significantly higher during acute relapse in relapsing/remitting MS, whereas anti-p542 was not. High-titer anti-EBNA-1 antibodies from MS and SLE sera cross-reacted with 80-82 kDa and 60 kDa neuroglial proteins through EBNA-1's glycine/alanine repeat, supporting an EBV-related cross-reactive autoimmune response that, while not disease-specific, may contribute to MS pathogenesis.

Veroni et al 2015 J Neuroinflammation.body: Cross-sectional study of 31 therapy-free relapsing-remitting MS patients in which paired CSF cells and PBMC were profiled by pre-amplification real-time RT-PCR for 41 immune-related genes and 7 EBV (latent and lytic) genes. Despite the enhanced-sensitivity method, EBV transcripts were detected only in a minority of patients (3/31 CSF, 4/29 PBMC; 5 of 31 patients), with evidence of perturbed/deregulated viral latency activation or lytic reactivation; one clinically/radiologically active patient showed full EBV reactivation in PBMC with B-cell activation. Cluster and factor analyses of CSF immune-gene data separated patients into subgroups distinguished by type-1 interferon/antiviral and pro-inflammatory gene signatures (MHC class II, CD4, CD68, OAS1, COX-2, NAMPT, IL-1beta), independent of sex, clinical, or MRI status. CSF B-cell/plasmablast markers (CD138, BCMA) were enriched relative to blood and correlated with inflammatory CSF parameters.

Veroni et al 2018 J Neuroinflammation.body: Veroni et al. used immunohistochemistry, laser capture microdissection, and enhanced PCR/ddPCR to profile expression of 75 immune-related genes and 6 EBV genes in meningeal and white matter immune infiltrates laser-cut from postmortem brains of 11 progressive MS patients. Brain immune infiltrates were dominated by type 1 (cytotoxic CD8+ T cell, IFNγ) immunity and type I IFN pathway activation. EBV genes were detected in 9 of 11 MS cases, more frequently in meningeal than white matter infiltrates, with latent genes (EBER1, EBNA3A, LMP1, LMP2A) more frequent than lytic genes (BZLF1, gp350/220), supporting in situ EBV deregulation and an EBV-driven immunopathological model of MS.

Veroni et al 2026 J Autoimmun.body: Observational longitudinal study of 25 people with relapsing-remitting MS (pwMS) treated with peginterferon beta-1a (peg-IFN), comparing PBMC IFN-stimulated gene expression, EBV DNA load, EBNA2 allele distribution, T-lymphocyte phenotyping and glycolytic metabolism before (T0) and after 6 months (T6mos). Peg-IFN increased Mx1/ISG15 transcription and CD4+ T-cell glycolysis and reduced EBV DNA load without altering EBNA2 allele distribution. Carriers of the non-risk 1.3B EBNA2 allele showed the highest ISG increase and better 2-year clinical response, and lower CD4 T-cell glycolytic capacity at T0 predicted higher peg-IFN responsiveness, suggesting EBNA2 variants are predictive of peg-IFN response.

Vietzen et al 2023 Cell.body: Case-control study (270 EBV-seropositive MS patients matched to 270 healthy controls, stratified into EBNAhigh and EBNAlow) investigating why only some individuals with high cross-reactive EBNA386-405/GlialCAM370-389 autoantibody titers develop MS. The authors show that autoreactive GlialCAM370-389-specific cells are normally eliminated by cytotoxic NKG2C+ and NKG2D+ NK cells and HLA-E-restricted EBV-specific CD8+ T cells, but in MS patients these responses are weak (low NKG2C+/NKG2D+ NK levels, KLRC2 deletion, NKG2D-LNK, HLA-E*0101) while immune evasion is enhanced via EBV-variant-specific (LMP-1 GGDPHLPTL/GGDPPLPTL) and IL-27-mediated HLA-E upregulation that inhibits NKG2A+ effector cells. Defined virus and host genetic predispositions confer up to a 260-fold increased MS risk.

Vietzen et al 2024 J Clin Invest.body: Matched case-control study of 270 EBV-seropositive MS patients and 270 healthy controls (plus a flow-cytometry subset of 20 MS vs 80 controls) testing whether an antibody signature against the EBV EBNA1 region EBNA381-452 and its cross-reactive CNS epitopes is associated with MS. At MS diagnosis, MS patients had significantly higher IgG against EBNA-derived peptides and the cross-reactive CNS proteins GlialCAM, CRYAB, MBP, and ANO2 than controls, whereas no EBNA381-452 antibodies were detectable at primary EBV infection. Accumulation of high-level antibodies against >=3 cross-reactive regions conferred a 1,366-fold increased MS risk (EBNA-specific). MS patients also accumulated high-level EBNA- and CNS-specific CD19+ B cell, CD4+ T cell, and CD8+ T cell responses.
Vietzen et al 2024 J Clin Invest.identifier: Vietzen et al 2024 J Clin Invest

Vietzen et al 2025 Nat Commun.body: A multi-center retrospective case-control study (704 EBV-EBNA-1-seropositive relapsing-remitting MS patients and 5381 controls; a matched longitudinal subcohort of 324 vs 324) that developed an EBNA-1(381-452)-specific IgG ELISA as a prognostic biomarker for MS. Elevated and especially repeatedly high-level (OD >= 1.7) EBNA-1(381-452)-specific IgG titers were detected in MS patients as early as nine months after EBV seroconversion and a median 5.4 years before MS diagnosis. Continuously high titers predicted shorter time to MS diagnosis/onset and preceded the rise of plasma NfL and GFAP (markers of axonal damage and astrocytic activation) by ~3.6-3.8 years. The titers correlated with >10 T2 MRI lesions and higher NfL/GFAP, supporting use as an early, non-invasive MS-risk biomarker.

Vietzen et al 2026 JAMA Neurol.body: Retrospective, multicenter, longitudinal case-control study (Austria, Germany, US) testing whether serial plasma EBNA-1 peptide (EBNA-1 381-452) IgG antibody titers, measured by ELISA, can differentiate multiple sclerosis (MS) from MOGAD, NMOSD, and other neurological diseases. In a test cohort (310) and an independent validation cohort (183), persistently high-level EBNA-1 peptide antibody titers in 2 or more of 4 longitudinal samples were strongly and specifically associated with MS (test cohort vs MOGAD OR 303.4, vs NMOSD OR 114.9; persistent titers in ~96% of MS patients), including discrimination of MS from AQP4-IgG-seronegative NMOSD (OR 236.0). The authors conclude serial EBNA-1 peptide IgG is a reliable adjunct biomarker for MS differential diagnosis.

Virtanen et al 2013 Mult Scler.body: Case-control study of CSF and serum from 37 MS patients (28 RRMS, 7 PPMS, 2 SPMS) and 15 OIND controls testing for HHV-6 and EBV reactive oligoclonal bands (OCBs) and viral DNA. Using isoelectric focusing/immunoblot against virus-coated membranes and nested PCR, 38% of MS (none of OIND, p=0.0048) had intrathecal OCBs reactive to either HHV-6 (9 cases, p=0.046) or EBV (5 cases, p=0.305) but never both; banding patterns were stable over time. MS patients with herpesviral DNA in CSF had significantly more contrast-enhancing lesions (CELs) on MRI (p=0.0095), and viral-DNA-positive patients trended toward lower CSF viral antibody levels.

Wagner et al 2000 Viral Immunol.body: Cross-sectional case-control study of 107 multiple sclerosis (MS) patients versus 163 age- and gender-matched healthy blood donors from north Germany, measuring anti-EBV antibody prevalence and reactivity by ELISA (recombinant p72 for EBNA1; p54/p138 for early antigen). All MS patients were EBV-seropositive (100% vs 93.9% controls, p<0.01) with no primary EBV infections, indicating EBV infection precedes MS onset. MS patients showed significantly lower anti-EBNA1-IgG titers (more low-titer individuals: 31.8% vs 9.8%, p<0.0001; OD 1.16+/-0.37 vs 1.34+/-0.34, p<0.001), interpreted as a serological sign of defective control of the latent EBV carrier state and EBV reactivation, while anti-early-antigen (EA) IgG/IgM/IgA reactivities did not differ between groups.

Wagner et al 2004 Eur J Neurol.body: A prospective, nested case-control study in the Nurses' Health Study and Nurses' Health Study II cohorts testing whether plasma EBV DNA viral load in pre-diagnostic blood predicts MS risk. Among 31 MS cases and 62 matched healthy controls, EBV DNA was detected in plasma of 29% of cases versus 16% of controls (relative risk 2.5, 95% CI 0.78-7.8, P=0.12), a more than two-fold but non-significant increase in MS risk unchanged by adjustment for smoking, ancestry, and latitude at birth. No association was found between the quantitative EBV viral load and MS risk, and IgG geometric mean titers to VCA, EBNA, EBNA1, and EBNA2 were higher (non-significantly) in PCR-positive than PCR-negative cases. The authors conclude the results support a role for EBV in MS etiology but require confirmation in a larger study.
Wagner et al 2004 Eur J Neurol.identifier: Wagner et al 2004 Eur J Neurol

Wang et al 2020 Cell.body: Wang et al. characterized the immunopeptidomes of the two HLA-DR15 allomorphs DR2a (DRA*01:01P/DRB5*01:01) and DR2b (DRA*01:01P/DRB1*15:01) on primary B cells, monocytes, thymus, and MS brain tissue using allele-specific monoclonal antibodies. HLA-DR-derived self-peptides (HLA-DR-SPs), mostly from DR2a/DR2b themselves, were abundant on B cells and thymic APCs but nearly absent from MS brain. Autoreactive CD4+ T cell clones (e.g., the brain-derived, DR2b-restricted, RASGRP2(78-87)-specific TCC14) cross-reacted with HLA-DR-SPs and with peptides from the MS-associated foreign agents Epstein-Barr virus (lytic proteins BHRF1/BPLF1) and Akkermansia muciniphila, while control HCMV and Prevotella peptides were negative. Thus both DR15 allomorphs jointly shape an autoreactive CD4+ T cell repertoire via cross-reactivity and HLA cross-restriction, linking the HLA-DR15 genetic risk factor to EBV.

Wang et al 2020 J Neuroimmune Pharmacol.body: Wang et al. screened phage-displayed random 12-mer peptide libraries with total IgG purified from an acute MS brain plaque (MS 95-2 IgG) to identify disease-relevant antibody epitopes. They isolated two phage peptides, Pep 3-3 and Pep 3-2, sharing high sequence and predicted structural homology with EBV nuclear antigens EBNA1 (residues 386-416) and EBNA2 (residues 263-286), respectively. By phage-mediated immuno-PCR across 46 MS and 5 inflammatory-control CSF samples, MS CSF IgG bound the EBNA1 epitope (Pep 3-3) significantly more than IC CSF (p=0.0075), Pep 3-3 competitively inhibited EBNA1 protein binding to MS IgG (p=0.018), and the EBNA1 epitope was recognized by oligoclonal/intrathecal IgG bands in MS CSF and serum, reinforcing a potential role for EBV/EBNA1 in MS etiology.
Wang et al 2020 J Neuroimmune Pharmacol.identifier: Wang et al 2020 J Neuroimmune Pharmacol

Wang et al 2025 Cell.body: Wang et al. show that EBV infection reprograms the transcriptome and HLA-DR15 (DR2a/DR2b)-presented immunopeptidome of B cells, leading EBV-transformed B cells to present four myelin basic protein (MBP) peptides (MBP78-90, MBP83-90, MBP91-106, MBP91-114) that are absent from primary B cells and thymus. Three of these MBP peptides ending at residue F90 are also presented on HLA-DR15 in highly inflamed MS brain tissue. Memory CD4+ T cells from peripheral blood and CSF of HLA-DR15+ MS patients respond to MBP78-90/MBP83-90 with a Th1 (IFN-gamma) phenotype, and MBP-specific CD4+ T-cell clones (e.g., 1642KA_TCC1B3, core epitope VVHF) recognize all brain MBP peptides ending at MBP90 on DR2b. The study proposes that EBV infection and the HLA-DR15 haplotype jointly drive MS via altered processing and presentation of MBP peptides, independent of molecular mimicry.

Waubant et al 2011 Neurology.body: Retrospective case-control study of 189 pediatric-onset MS/CIS patients and 66 pediatric controls testing serostatus for EBV, CMV, and HSV-1 plus HLA-DRB1*1501/1503 as predictors of pediatric MS. EBV (anti-EBNA-1 and anti-VCA) seropositivity and DRB1*1501/1503 were associated with increased MS odds, while remote CMV infection was independently associated with lower MS risk. HSV-1 showed no main effect but a strong interaction with HLA-DRB1: HSV-1 raised MS risk in DRB1*15-negative individuals and lowered it in DRB1*15-positive individuals.

Waubant et al 2012 Mult Scler.body: Case-control study of 189 pediatric-onset MS/CIS patients and 38 pediatric neurologic controls measuring IgG antibody responses to EBV (EBNA-1, VCA, EA), CMV, and HSV-1 and HLA-DRB1*1501/1503 genotype. Viral antibody concentrations were similar between MS/CIS patients and seropositive controls for all viruses. Independent of MS status, HLA-DRB1*1501/1503 positivity was associated with higher anti-EBNA-1 antibody response (p=0.005) but not with responses to VCA, EA, CMV, or HSV-1, suggesting genotype influences the humoral response specifically to EBNA-1.

Wergeland et al 2016 Eur J Neurol.body: A prospective cohort substudy of the OFAMS randomized trial in 90 relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis patients examined the association between serum anti-EBNA-1 IgG and 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D) using repeated paired measurements every 6 months over 24 months. EBNA-1 IgG levels varied significantly by sampling month (peak in April, trough in September), were negatively associated with 25(OH)D (B=-0.230), and were higher in HLA-DRB1*15 positive patients (B=94.7). The 25(OH)D-EBNA-1 IgG association persisted after adjustment for age, gender, BMI, retinol, HLA-DRB1*15 and IFN-beta treatment, and was significant only in DRB1*15-positive patients.

Wieland et al 2022 Cells.body: Wieland et al. established EBV-immortalized lymphoblastoid B cell lines (LCL) from 32 individuals with relapsing-remitting MS and 10 controls and profiled them by RNAseq (mapped to GRCh38/hg38 and a synthetic virus metagenome) and qRT-PCR to find MS-relevant biomarkers and EBV/HERV expression patterns. EBV immortalization strongly induced lytic EBNA-1 and EBNA-2 transcripts and up-regulated HERV-K (HML-2) GAG and HERV-K18 (2.1-fold), with six HERV loci activated via CD40/BCR signaling. Lytic EBNA-1 was negatively correlated with PBMC-donor age and was higher in relapse-free and natalizumab-treated patients. MSLCL (vs control LCL) showed exclusive up-regulation of ERVMER61-1, ERV3-1 and several HERV-K loci, and a 15-gene panel distinguished MS from controls (AUC 0.972).

Willis et al 2009 Brain.body: Willis et al. examined whether EBV infection is a characteristic feature of multiple sclerosis brain using in situ hybridization (EBER ISH), immunohistochemistry (LMP1, EBNA2), and two highly sensitive real-time PCR assays (genomic BamHI-W repeat and EBER1) capable of detecting two or fewer EBV-infected cells. Across a cohort of 23 white-matter-lesion specimens from 12 MS cases (all with CD20+ B cell infiltrate) EBV was undetectable by every method, while EBV was readily detected in positive control CNS lymphomas. In a second cohort of 12 meningeal/parenchymal B-cell-aggregate specimens (same tissue bank as Serafini 2007), ISH was negative in all cases and PCR detected low-level EBV in only 2 of 12 cases. The authors conclude that CNS EBV infection is rare in MS brain and unlikely to contribute directly to MS brain pathology in the vast majority of cases, contradicting Serafini et al. (2007).

Wuest et al 2014 PLoS One.body: A blinded prospective NIH study of 100 subjects (21 PPMS, 20 SPMS, 21 untreated RRMS, 19 daclizumab/DAC HYP-treated RRMS, 19 OIND controls) using a novel co-culture assay of fresh CSF T cells with autologous antigen-loaded dendritic cells to profile CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell antigen specificity and cytokine (TNF-alpha, IFN-gamma) phenotype. T-cell reactivities to complex auto-antigens (myelin, brain homogenate, modified oligodendroglial/neuronal cell lysates) were comparably low across all cohorts and compartments. In contrast, the CSF was strongly enriched for EBV- and HHV6-specific (but not CMV-specific) Th1 reactivities, most pronounced in RRMS; long-term daclizumab treatment reversed this intrathecal enrichment, while progressive MS patients showed diminished intrathecal proliferation but enhanced cytokine production consistent with terminally differentiated T cells.

Xu et al 2021 JAMA Netw Open.body: Population-based Swedish cohort study (2 492 980 individuals born 1958-1994) using the Total Population Register and within-sibling stratified Cox regression to assess whether hospital-diagnosed infectious mononucleosis (IM) before age 25 is associated with a subsequent multiple sclerosis (MS) diagnosis independent of shared familial factors. IM in childhood (HR 2.87) and adolescence (HR 3.19) remained significantly associated with MS after controlling for measured and unmeasured shared familial factors, whereas IM in early adulthood (HR 1.51) did not. The findings suggest IM in childhood and particularly adolescence is a risk factor for MS, making greater susceptibility to infection less likely as the explanation.

Zdimerova et al 2020 Eur J Immunol.body: Using HLA-typed humanized NSG (huNSG) mice reconstituted with HLA-DR15 (HLA-DRB1*15:01) positive or negative human immune compartments, the authors show that HLA-DR15 reconstitutes hyperactive CD4+ and CD8+ T cells at steady state and after EBV infection, yet EBV viral loads are less well controlled (higher) under HLA-DR15 than under HLA-DR4. HLA-DR15-restricted CD4+ T-cell clones recognized EBV-transformed B-cell lines less efficiently, cross-reacted to the MS autoantigen MBP, and showed increased alloreactivity in cytokine production and cytotoxicity. The findings provide a mechanistic model in which EBV (environmental risk factor) and HLA-DR15 (genetic risk factor) synergize to prime hyperreactive, cross-reactive T cells in MS.
Zdimerova et al 2020 Eur J Immunol.identifier: Zdimerova et al 2020 Eur J Immunol

Ziaei et al 2024 Mult Scler.body: Multi-center case-control study (473 pediatric-onset MS cases, 702 frequency-matched controls) from the US Network of Pediatric MS Centers examining gene-environment interactions between childhood EBV infection (anti-VCA-IgG serostatus) and candidate HLA and non-HLA genetic risk variants for pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (POMS). Anti-VCA seropositivity was much higher in cases (94.6% vs 60.7%, p<0.001) and prior EBV infection was associated with POMS (OR=9.89). The study found significant additive and multiplicative interaction between childhood EBV infection and HLA-DRB1*15, and additive interaction between EBV infection and the CD86 rs2255214 GG genotype, suggesting a role for antigen-presenting cells/B cells in EBV-associated POMS risk.

Zivadinov et al 2008 J Neurol Neurosurg.body: Cross-sectional cohort study of 135 patients with clinically definite MS (with a retrospective longitudinal subset of 50 followed a mean 3.1 years) testing whether serum anti-EBV antibody levels (VCA, EBNA-1, early antigen IgG) correlate with quantitative MRI measures of brain injury and atrophy. Higher anti-EBV-VCA IgG levels were significantly associated with lower grey matter fraction (GMF, p=0.002) and brain parenchymal fraction (BPF, p<0.001), and anti-EBV-EBNA IgG with lower GMF (p=0.004); anti-EBV-EA IgG showed no association. Higher baseline anti-EBV-VCA IgG predicted accelerated BPF loss over 3 years (p<0.001), suggesting EBV-mediated immune dysfunction may contribute to grey matter atrophy in MS.
Zivadinov et al 2008 J Neurol Neurosurg.identifier: Zivadinov et al 2008 J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry

Zivadinov et al 2009 J Neuroimmunol.body: Cross-sectional cohort study (93 clinically definite MS patients, 122 healthy controls; 54 MS with 3-year follow-up) testing whether gene-environment interactions between HLA Class I (B7, A2) and Class II (DR15) alleles and humoral anti-EBV responses associate with quantitative MRI brain injury and disability in MS. HLA B7 was associated with increased T1-lesion volume and trends of increased T2-LV, decreased brain parenchymal fraction, higher EDSS and increased anti-EBV VCA IgG; HLA A2 was protective (lower EDSS and trend toward lower anti-VCA IgG); the B7-A2 haplotype was significantly associated with higher T2-LV and T1-LV. The authors conclude HLA Class I loci modify MS severity via interactions with EBV exposure.

Zivadinov et al 2019 Mult Scler Relat Di.body: Prospective, single-blinded, 12-month observational study of 30 relapsing MS patients starting teriflunomide and 20 age/sex-matched healthy controls, testing whether teriflunomide's effect on cortical gray matter volume loss is linked to humoral response to EBV. Anti-EBV VCA and EBNA-1 IgG titers were measured by ELISA at baseline, 6 and 12 months. Over 12 months MS patients showed a significant decrease in anti-EBNA-1 (-35.1, p=.003) and anti-VCA (-15.9, p=.05) IgG titers while HC titers were stable, and larger decreases in these titers correlated with less cortical and gray matter volume loss, suggesting teriflunomide may slow cortical GM atrophy by altering the humoral response to EBV.
Zivadinov et al 2019 Mult Scler Relat Di.identifier: Zivadinov et al 2019 Mult Scler Relat Disord

Zivadinov et al 2022 Mult Scler Relat Di.body: A Phase IV, prospective, open-label, single-center, observational longitudinal pilot study of 27-30 relapsing-remitting MS patients started on ocrelizumab, evaluated at baseline, 12 and 24 months. Over 24 months ocrelizumab significantly reduced the humoral response to EBV (EBNA-1 IgG decreased, p=0.013) but not anti-VCA IgG (p=0.993), most likely by depleting B cells. Treatment was safe and clinically effective (74.1% stable, 18.5% improved), but significant brain volume loss (cortex, gray matter, thalamus, deep gray matter) and T1 lesion-volume accumulation occurred, and ocrelizumab did NOT reduce leptomeningeal contrast enhancement (LM inflammation).
Zivadinov et al 2022 Mult Scler Relat Di.identifier: Zivadinov et al 2022 Mult Scler Relat Disord

Zivlaei et al 2025 J Neurol Sci.body: A case-control serology study measuring IgG antibody levels to a panel of 12 virus antigens (EBV EBNA1 and BARF1, SARS-CoV-2 S protein, CMV, HHV6, VZV, JCV, IAV, MeV, MuV, RuV, MCV) by ELISA in relapsing-remitting MS patients before (n=13) and during (n=29) Ocrevus (ocrelizumab) B cell-depleting therapy versus healthy controls (n=15). EBV EBNA1 IgG was the only virus antibody significantly elevated in RRMS patients vs HCs at baseline (p=0.0382), confirming EBNA1 IgG's diagnostic value, while OCR treatment did not change most virus antibody levels except SARS-CoV-2 S protein IgG, which was significantly reduced (p=0.0186).
Zivlaei et al 2025 J Neurol Sci.identifier: Zivlaei et al 2025 J Neurol Sci

de Mol et al 2024 J Neurol Neurosurg Psy.body: Using the population-based Generation R paediatric birth cohort in the Netherlands, this study examined how genetic (MS polygenic risk score, HLA-DRB1*15:01, and the severity variant rs10191329) and childhood environmental MS risk factors (EBV serology, vitamin D, BMI, outdoor activity, household parental smoking) relate to brain MRI outcomes in children aged 9-13 without MS. In EBV-positive children, a higher MS-PRS was positively associated with anti-EBV-VCA antibody titres (beta=0.15, p=2.98e-6), with HLA-DRB1*15:01 the strongest contributor. A higher MS-PRS was associated with lower subcortical grey matter volume, and the MS-PRS interacted negatively with household parental smoking to lower total brain, subcortical grey matter, and thalamic volumes; rs10191329 showed no brain associations.

van Nierop et al 2015 Eur J Immunol.body: Short communication developing a novel APC/T-cell platform that uses EBV-transformed B-lymphoblastoid cell lines (BLCL) to endogenously express eight candidate MS-associated autoantigens (MAG, MBP, MOG, PLP, KIR4.1, S100B, CNTN2, NFASC) and assay intrathecal CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell responses in CSF-derived T-cell lines from 7 CIS and 6 MS patients. Whereas measles virus fusion protein (MVF)-specific control T-cell clones efficiently recognized transduced BLCL, no substantial CSF T-cell reactivity to the candidate autoantigens was detected (the only positive call was NFASC-specific CD4 T cells in one RRMS patient), and no significant variation between antigens was found (CD4 p=0.74, CD8 p=0.30). The findings do not support these endogenously synthesized human autoantigens as prominent intrathecal T-cell targets in CIS and MS early after disease onset.
van Nierop et al 2015 Eur J Immunol.identifier: van Nierop et al 2015 Eur J Immunol

van Nierop et al 2015 Mult Scler.body: Comparison of the prevalence and fine specificity of EBV-specific intrathecal T-cells in CSF-derived T-cell lines (CSF-TCL) from clinically-isolated syndrome (CIS, n=17), multiple sclerosis (MS, n=12) and other neurological disease (OND, n=13) patients, using autologous EBV-transformed B-cells (autoBLCL) as antigen-presenting cells. CIS and MS patients had significantly higher frequencies of autoBLCL-reactive CD4 T-cells, and CIS patients had higher autoBLCL-reactive CD8 T-cells, than OND controls. In-depth analysis of four CSF-TCL showed oligoclonal CD8 T-cell responses directed to lytic EBV proteins (BRLF1, BaRF1, BXLF1, BCRF1, BBRF3) but not to the host autoantigen alpha-B-crystallin (CRYAB), and intrathecal EBV DNA and EBNA1-specific IgG were undetectable.
